Is that just for Vault dwellers or for people who come down here and murder Vault dwellers?|Norm to [[Betty Pearson]]|sound=Norm MacLean.ogg}} '''Norman "Norm" MacLean''' is a resident of [[Vault 33]] in [[Timeline#2296|2296]]. He is the inquisitive brother{{Ref|(Age)}} of [[Lucy MacLean]] and the son of [[Hank MacLean]]. He takes on a role as a deuteragonist in the story of the TV series once he begins exploring the mystery behind [[Vault 32|Vaults 32]] and [[Vault 31|31]]. ==Background== Norm was born to [[Rose MacLean|Rose]] and [[Hank MacLean]] of Vault 33 and has one sister, [[Lucy MacLean|Lucy]].[[Fallout season 1 Amazon overview|''Fallout'' season 1 character description on Amazon]]: ''"The younger brother of Lucy, and a bit of a black sheep in the Vault 33 community. Despite not fitting in and lacking enthusiasm in every job he’s ever been assigned, he is deeply loyal to his community. Vault 33 is his home."'' Rose suspected the surface world was hospitable and fled Vault 33, angering her husband because he viewed this as dangerous. Rose took Norm and his older sister to live in [[Shady Sands]], although the two children seemed too young to have memories of being on the surface. At some point, Hank finds Rose on the surface, but she refuses to return with him. Hank took his children back from Rose, moving them back to Vault 33, where they believed Rose had died of natural causes during their early childhood.{{FOTV|1|8}} [[File:Hank Lucy and Norm.png|thumb|250px|Norm with his father and sister]] Growing up in Vault 33, Norm became best friends with his cousin [[Chet (TV series)|Chet]]. However, he is a black sheep in the Vault's community due to his introversion and irreverent personality. As he came to working age, Norm went from job to job in the Vault, receiving a performance grade of "lacks enthusiasm" at each one. Despite his general apathy, he does care about the community to some degree, especially the people who are close to him.[https://web.archive.org/web/20240114045401/https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/2023/11/fallout-first-look Vanity Fair: "Fallout First Look: This Is How the World Ends—With a Smiling Thumbs-Up" (Archived)] ==''Fallout'' TV series== ===Season 1=== {{Quotation|The younger brother of Lucy, and a bit of a black sheep in the Vault 33 community. Despite not fitting in, and lacking enthusiasm in every job he’s ever been assigned, he is deeply loyal to his community. Vault 33 is his home.|[[Fallout season 1 Amazon overview|''Fallout'' season 1 character description]]}} ====[[The End (episode)|The End]]==== Norm discovers the residents of [[Vault 32]] are all dead just before an attack by [[Vault 32 raider|raiders]] posing as [[Vault 32 dweller|residents]]. During the attack, he hides in a storage space under the floor. [[File:FOTV Official Trailer Still 054.png|thumb|250px|left|Norm hugging Lucy goodbye]] After the attack, Norm's sister Lucy proposes they send a search party to the surface to find their kidnapped dad. However, the interim council rejects her proposal based on keeping the Vault safe, although Norm speculates they did so because they don't want to recover their father, and since then, they wouldn't be in charge anymore. He later helps his sister Lucy leave the vault and they share a brief hug.{{FOTV|1|1}} ====[[The Head]]==== [[File:FOTV The Head Norm.png|thumb|250px|Norm waiting for his punishment]] Due to helping his sister escape, the Vault council comprised of [[Woody Thomas]], [[Reg McPhee]], and [[Betty Pearson]] decide to punish Norm with a demotion. The council scolds Norm, saying he and Chet put their Vault in incredible danger since the radiation levels could have killed everyone and the last vestiges of human civilization. Norm attempts to defend himself saying it was Lucy's idea. When the council points out he could have tried to stop her, Norm replies it was not on his mind. He is reassigned from computer duty to delivering food to the surviving raiders, even after he suggests the raiders deserve punishment. He later suggested executing the imprisoned raiders in the Vault during an assembly, causing many of the dwellers to be disgusted at him and his idea. Betty rejects the idea, saying murdering them should be out of the question. Norm then, perhaps snarkily, apologizes to Betty for questioning her leadership. After the meeting, [[Steph Harper]] approaches Norm to tell him she agrees with his idea of executing the raiders.{{FOTV|1|3}} ====[[The Ghouls]]==== [[File:Betty brings pie.png|thumb|left|250px|Betty imploring Norm to tread lightly]] Betty brings some pie she made herself to Norm. She comes to talk to him about how his vocalizing his desire to kill the raiders upset the Vault dwellers and that what he says carries weight because he is the only MacLean left in the Vault. Norm expresses how he feels guilty about hiding during the raid, and Betty notices how he feels angry about it. Betty comments that because Norm is clever, how he channels his anger can lead to dark places, and asks him to tread lightly before she leaves. While delivering food to the raiders, Norm has a small talk with [[Veronica (TV series)|Veronica]] about how she feels the raiders do not deserve cake. Veronica wants some of the cake herself, so Norm secretly gives her the cake instead of the raiders. Once Veronica has left, Norm talks to one raider, [[Dervin]], who claims that the raiders did not kill the dwellers of Vault 32, and that the dwellers were not as innocent as Norm thinks. Afterward, Norm tries to look into files related to Vault 32, but his access is denied. He goes to Chet for help getting into Vault 32, whose door had been damaged in an explosion and was accessible if they moved some rubble. The pair explore Vault 32 and find that the dwellers had all died at least two years ago in what appeared to be internal conflict, meaning the raiders did not kill the residents. They eventually reach the overseer's office, finding the [[Ian Jackson|deceased overseer]]'s corpse; Norm accesses the overseer's terminal and finds that his mother [[Rose MacLean|Rose]]'s Pip-Boy was used to access Vault 32 from the surface.{{FOTV|1|4}} ====[[The Past]]==== [[File:The Past Vault 32 paint job.png|250px|thumb|Norm looking at the freshly painted Vault 32]] Exploring Vault 32, still confused as to how the Vault 32 raiders had his mother's Pip-Boy, Norm and Chet discover that many of the Vault 32 dwellers died trying to get into [[Vault 31]]. They hurriedly return to Vault 33 to try to avoid suspicion, but are seen not far away from the Vault 31 door by Betty, offering only a weak lie for what they were doing. Later, Norm investigates Vault 33's Inter-Vault trade records and discovers that all of the personnel traded have been from Vault 31 to Vault 33, and all of them have ended up being elected as overseer, with Hank and Betty being the latest ones in this trend. Norm congratulates Betty at the Vault's celebration for her electoral victory. He later visits Chet in [[Steph Harper]]'s apartment to discuss his findings, but Chet dismisses them, in part because Steph herself is from Vault 31. Norm directly asks Steph about how Vault 31 is different from Vault 33; she only says that its mashed potatoes were better, causing Norm to remark that Hank said the same thing. They are later confused when Betty takes everyone to a now-cleaned Vault 32, completely devoid of any traces of the violence and death that previously occurred and announces a project to resettle the vault. Norm returns to the now-refurbished overseer's office and is joined soon after by Betty. Knowingly praising her for the successful "cleanup" of the vault, he asks Betty what happened to his mother's Pip-Boy, and is left confused when Betty claims to have buried it with Rose when she died.{{FOTV|1|5}} ====[[The Radio]]==== Back in Vault 33, Norm continues to deliver food to the imprisoned Vault 32 raiders. He arrives one day to find all of the raiders dead by poisoning, and Veronica accused of the crime. Later, when the Vault reassignment decisions are released, Norm discovers he will be staying in Vault 33. Soon, the dwellers assigned to Vault 32 prepare to leave, and Norm takes advantage of Betty's preoccupation with the departing dwellers to sneak into her office. There, he hacks into Betty's terminal and communicates with Vault 31's overseer, fooling him into opening the door to Vault 31. ====[[The Beginning]]==== Norm secretly enters Vault 31 and discovers its overseer, [[Bud Askins]], who has had his brain removed and preserved in a rudimentary [[Brain bot#Rollerbrain|rollerbrain]] chasis. He soon walks deeper into the Vault and discovers the truth: that all of its residents are cryonically frozen Vault-Tec employees from before the Great War, including his father, intended to reshape the world in the image of Vault-Tec's and Bud's own plans. Bud refuses to let Norm leave and traps him inside the cryo chamber bay, as he knows too much. Bud implores Norm to enter one of the cryo chambers so that Norm will not starve. ===Season 2=== {{Quotation|Norm is brother to Lucy, son to Hank, and one of Vault 33’s few skeptics or rebels. While he began the show as a complete coward, his curious nature has thrust him down a path of uncovering dark, dangerous secrets about his family.|[[Fallout season 2 Amazon overview|''Fallout'' season 2 character description]]}} ====[[The Innovator]]==== In [[Vault 31]], Norm is still locked in the cryo facility with Bud Askins, having continually refused to enter a cryopod. Bud begins to panic upon discovering that Norm had disabled inter-Vault communications and goes to check on him. Bud is unable to reach Norm, as he has sequestered himself down the stairs into the cryopod area, now littered with emptied ration cases. Bud tries to persuade Norm with his "two rational choices:" either enter Hank's cryonic chamber or starve to death. Norm asks Bud if he would ever be released from cryonic suspension; Bud says he would, but only upon achieving [[Reclamation Day (event)|Reclamation Day]], which, according to Bud, will occur when everyone on the surface who could challenge Vault-Tec's monopoly on life has died. Norm stubbornly refuses to be Bud's prisoner and insists that someone would come for him, but Bud asserts that Vault-Tec had prepared for every contingency, including when a vault dweller goes missing, promising that Betty will cover up his disappearance. To further demoralize Norm, Bud shuts off the lights, certain that he'd be more "reasonable" when he grows hungrier. Bud later checks on Norm again while he is lying on the floor. As Bud tries once again to encourage him to take Hank's pod, Norm ignores him, asking what his father was like and why he was frozen in the first place. Bud boasts that Hank was an ambitious man and that becoming one of Bud's Buds was a highly coveted position in the pre-War era. Then, noticing Norm spotted a two-headed [[centipede]], he cautions that consuming the mutated insect will cause him a slow, painful death. He instead offers to inject Norm with an unnamed poison that will give him a quick and painless death, and that when he dies, his body will dissolve and be filtered from 31 through the ventilation system into the crops for the other Vaults. Norm refuses Bud's false dichotomy of "two rational choices" and asserts there are plenty of "irrational" ones. Norm approaches Bud and kicks off the syringe limb Bud had threatened him with. Norm tells Bud that he is releasing Bud's preserved junior managers. Bud tries to protest the disruption of his plan to create a race of super managers, but is kept back with Norm's foot as Norm releases all Vault-Tec executives from their cryo-chambers. ====[[The Golden Rule]]==== Before the junior managers are thawed, Norm kills Bud Askins and places him upside down in a mop bucket. This occurs off-screen. Norm observes as the pre-War [[Vault 31 dweller]]s emerge from their stasis, greeting them. When [[Clark (TV series)|Clark]] questions why they were unfrozen all at once and where Bud Askins is, Norm claims that a change of plans was needed. When everyone decides that this means it is Reclamation Day, Norm is forced to go along with it while explaining that Bud Askins has died. This sends the assembled group into a panic, some trying to return to their pods, with Norm himself left trying to regain control. Eventually, after some thinking, Norm comes up with a speech to get everyone's attention, hawking Bud's words that he is a "super manager" created from 200 years of genetic engineering, and that the assembled Vault 31ers were unthawed to serve as his staff. He rallies the executives by saying that, while some of Bud's claims seemed outlandish before, their presence in Vault 31 is a testament to Bud's work that they must now carry on. Norm tells them that they will have proven worthy to carry on Vault-Tec's corporate strategy if they can pass a "final test" of finding a way to escape Vault 31. Invigorated by Norm's words, the 31ers begin working to salvage parts of the Vault and find a way out. Later on, the group discovers a hatch connected to the surface on the ceiling of the cryo pod bay. Norm observes as several 31ers work to form a human ladder using the machinery on the wall as footholds until one is able to unlock the hatch. He himself is obliged to take the lead and ascend up the ladder behind the hatch, connected to an old ventilation shaft. This means he is the first of the expedition to set foot into the wasteland, looking out along the nearby shoreline where he spots the remnants of the [[Santa Monica Pier]]. While the 31ers are saddened or disappointed at the state of the surface, Norm is in awe of the outside world and remarks that it is "beautiful." ====[[The Demon in the Snow]]==== The Vault 31 expedition reaches a ruined urban area of [[Los Angeles]], where they stop to raid an old [[BlamCo]] food truck and consume the uncooked [[BlamCo Mac & Cheese]] it is carrying, though Norm advises them to conserve what they find in case they cannot find more food. He then notices [[Claudia (TV series)|Claudia]] looking toward an old bridge, which she says brings back the memory of when she drove across it heading to her interview with Vault-Tec just a week before she was frozen, which Norm sympathizes with. They are then interrupted by [[Ronnie McCurtry]], who asks about their goal to start "phase two." Norm asks his name, then tries to dismiss him, saying he makes the decisions for the group. However Ronnie shrugs it off and reveals that he was Bud's personal assistant before the bombs, taking lunch orders while the executive was talking with his Vaults' investors about phase 2, "Future Enterprise Ventures," and "the plan" forVaults 32 and 33. This deflates Norm and forces him to let Ronnie take the lead of the expedition while he is left nervous about his next steps. ====[[The Wrangler]]==== Under Ronnie's direction, the expedition arrives on the grounds of the abandoned [[Vault-Tec headquarters (TV series)|Vault-Tec headquarters]]. They break through the boarded-up front doors into the lobby, where Norm discovers a fresh blood splatter and advises them to leave, though this is ignored when the group finds the remains of a former coworker. Everyone is shocked when loud bangs and skittering emits from the elevator shafts. When [[Ma June]] and [[Barv]] appear to hold them at gunpoint, the former notes with distaste that they have found "more Vault dwellers," which gets Norm's attention immediately. Norm speaks privately with Ma June, wherein she reveals her encounter with his sister at [[Filly]]. She goes on to mention several factions and recent events around Los Angeles, like the [[Enclave]], [[New California Republic|NCR]], and [[Great Khans|Khans]], but Norm clarifies that he has no idea what she is talking about. Ma apologizes for trying to talk current events to a "vaultie" and changes subjects, telling him his sister is most likely dead, but Norm refuses to believe this. Ma firmly tells him the same advice she had for his sister: "Go home." He digests that information while Ma and Barv head off again, allowing the group access to their wealth of salvage to take what they need as long as they do not mess with their [[Radroach (TV series)|radroach]] farm. Later on, Norm follows Ronnie and other managers into a comms room, which Ronnie tells him they intend to use to reach out to "the investors," giving Norm a suspicious look. Norm then sees Claudia nearby, trying to keep herself from crying. He gives her a chance to talk as she reveals she has been struggling with the fact that she has woken up 200 years after everyone she knew and loved like her parents, friends, and her cat named Puppy have died. Norm gives her reassurances before asking if she knows anything about "Future Enterprise Ventures," but Claudia denies it since she had only been in Vault-Tec for a week before the bombs. She does, however, remember the name of an executive, [[Barb Howard|Barbara Howard]], who was Bud Askins' superior and was responsible for the Vault proposals, which tips Norm off. He follows Claudia as she leads him to Barb's old office, and he tries to get into Barb's terminal. Claudia reveals that she has figured out Norm is not really Bud's successor. Norm takes this in stride, asking how she figured it out, and chuckles when she says he is not "nuts" like the other 31ers. She offers to get them both a drink, which Norm reveals he has never had one. Once Claudia leaves, he looks into Vault-Tec's database to find "Future Enterprise Ventures," but discovers there is no mention of it apart from a related search on the acronym "F.E.V." which takes him to an entry on the [[Forced Evolutionary Virus]]. Before Norm can read further, however, Ronnie, having secretly followed and heard Norm's admission to lying about being Bud's successor, pulls out the terminal's power cord and threatens Norm. Norm attempts to defend himself with a lamp but is disarmed by Ronnie and strangled with the cord. He is forced to the ground and struggles for a while before falling unconscious. ====[[The Handoff]]==== A short time after Ronnie incapacitated him, Norm wakes up on the floor of the old office, hearing the [[Vault 31 dweller]]s discussing what to do with him. Ronnie suggests they abide by a section of the Vault-Tec employee handbook that allegedly made the impersonation of management punishable by death, which the rest sycophantically go along with. [[Pete (TV series)|Pete]] then notices him waking up, and the group gathers around him as Ronnie tells [[Clark (TV series)|Clark]] to knock him out again. Norm tries to ask what the plan is for the Three Vaults but he is ignored as Clark smashes a trophy against his forehead to render him unconscious. Sometime later, Norm is reawakened by Claudia who frees his hands that were bound earlier. She tells him they have to leave but Norm responds that he has to do something first. He goes to the headquarters' communications room and uses the ham radio there to broadcast a message. First, he tries to reach out to Lucy and tell her that he is out in the wasteland and ask why she did not tell him about the Vault experiments. He then calls for his father, asking why Hank had lied to him all his life and what is going to happen to their Vault. No answer comes before Claudia alerts him to their discovery by the Vault 31 group as Norm looks on grimly. ====[[The Strip]]==== Norm is dragged through the offices by the Vault 31 dwellers as Ronnie declares they will enact a "fair trial" to decide his punishment for lying to them. Claudia tries to pull Norm away from them, but is thrown against the wall by Ronnie. This inadvertently results in her activating the controls for the elevators, opening the doors into the shafts. While Norm is on the ground, the [[executive assistant]] who was holding him goes to inspect the elevator shaft and is then attacked and killed by a [[Radroach (TV series)|radroach]]. The entire group is sent into panic as all of Ma June's radroaches fly out of the shaft and begin attacking them. Norm is left behind while the 31ers flee, managing to shield himself from a radroach by using a chair for cover. Norm tries to run after the fleeing 31ers, briefly stopping to save the last 31er, who had fallen to the ground and was being attacked. However, Ronnie refuses to let him into the break room all of the 31ers are taking cover in; though both Norm and Claudia try to resist, Norm is ultimately shoved to the ground by Ronnie, making him unable to get in before the radroach swarm comes. However, Ronnie's delay in closing the door allows the radroaches to overpower him, sweeping into the break room and slaughtering the 31ers. Ironically, Norm manages to survive by ducking under a nearby table, where he is ignored by the radroaches, all of whom swarmed into the break room, with its door closing amidst the chaos. Norm is forced to listen to the 31ers' dying screams. Later, after the room had gone quiet, Norm crawls out and goes in to investigate, seeing the carnage with nearly every Vault 31 dweller and at least some of the radroaches dead. He manages to find Claudia still alive, but wounded. After recovering some supplies and improvising a sled, Norm harnesses himself to it to take Claudia with him as they leave the headquarters, promising to get her "home." ==Personality== [[File:Betty and Norm.png|thumb|250px|Norm speaking to Betty]] Norm is a clever young man who begins the series as a somewhat timid and apathetic individual but gradually becomes more confident as the series progresses. He seems to enjoy teasing others, such as when he tells Lucy her future husband might be a cannibal. Betty also figures out that Norm likes to upset people, although it also seems Norm simply prefers speaking his mind even if it makes him seem rude to others. Nevertheless, he maintains a sense of innocence that is common among Vault dwellers who have never been to the surface. Norm is also a perceptive individual, being one of the first to figure out that something is wrong with the "dwellers" from Vault 32 before they were revealed as raiders. Over time, Norm is shown to exhibit a great amount of bravery, having the courage to let his sister out of the Vault and exploring the decrepit Vaults 31 and 32. This stems from his regret over hiding in a duct while raiders attacked Vault 33, which spurs him to become more active. He is also shown to be somewhat vindictive, particularly towards the raiders, wishing them dead. That said, when it is discovered later that the raiders had been mysteriously killed from consuming rat poison in their food, Norm did not show joy. In the quiet life in the Vault, he does not seem to enjoy his family's book club; instead, he prefers to play Pip-Boy games. After being imprisoned in Vault 31 by [[Bud Askins]] to keep the secret of the Vault experiments, Norm shows a more ruthless side such as taking steps to sabotage Bud's controls and eventually upending his entire plan by thawing out the Vault 31 dwellers, ultimately killing Bud himself by destroying his robotic chassis. He demonstrates his cunning by crafting a story to the unfrozen Bud's Buds executives that he is Bud's successor and their leader in trying to escape Vault 31 and start reclaiming the surface. Despite the fact that he lies to them, Norm is still capable of empathy for the pre-War managers such as hearing Claudia reminisce about her pre-War life and later comforting her after she opens up about her sadness at losing everyone she knew and loved while she was frozen. He continues to show his empathy when he tries to save one of them who had fallen down during the radroach attack, later showing terror and sadness after being forced to listen to their dying screams as the swarm slaughters them. He waits until it stops to go in and recover a wounded Claudia, bringing her with him to find a safe place. ==Notable quotes== * {{Inline quote|And as for his looks? Big butt? No butt? But of course, it's just superficial concerns, it's what's on the inside that counts. And in that respect, he could be a cannibal, or just like crammed full of tumors.|sound=Norm for his looks.ogg|Norm talking to Lucy about her prospective husband}} * {{Inline quote|No, but that sounds accurate.|sound=Norm sounds accurate.ogg|Norm when asked if he knows his performance reviews have all been "lacks enthusiasm" in "[[The Head]]"}} * {{Inline quote|I don't know, I don't think it's our job to help these people. They're murderers.|sound=Norm theyre murderers.ogg|Norm regarding the Vault 32 raiders in "The Head"}} ==Appearances== Norm MacLean appears {{in|FOTV}}. He was also added to ''[[Fallout Shelter]]'' in update 1.17.0. {{FOTV appearances |1=101 |3=103 |4=104 |5=105 |7=107 |8=108 |9=201 |10=202 |12=204 |13=205 |15=207 |16=208 }} ==Behind the scenes== * Norm appears in six out of eight episodes in the first season and is the most frequently recurring character outside of Lucy, who appears in all eight episodes, and [[Maximus]] and [[the Ghoul]], who appear in seven each. ** Although Norm can be considered a major character of the show, he was not explicitly called a protagonist in any Amazon descriptions for season 1, nor was he featured in promotional marketing that focused on Lucy, Maximus, and the Ghoul. However, Moisés Arias is also credited as part of the main cast in episodes in which he appears, and Norm does play a leading role outside of the three main protagonists and thus could be considered a deuteragonist of the series. * Norm's actor, [[Moisés Arias]], is 4 feet and 11 inches (1.50m) tall. Compared to the rest of his family, Hank's actor, [[Kyle MacLachlan]], is 6 feet (1.83m) tall, and Lucy and Chet are of average height, although it is unclear how tall Rose's actress, [[Elle Vertes]], is. * {{Note|(Age)}} Moisés Arias is older than Lucy's actress, [[Ella Purnell]]. However, Norm is referred to as both older and younger than Lucy in various places: ** In the [[The End script|script]] for "[[The End (episode)|The End]]," Norm is referenced as being 22,{{inline quote|REVEAL: It’s not just the two of them at the dining table. Lucy’s older brother NORM (22, brilliant but unmotivated) is also there, playing a game on his Pip-Boy as his sister and father talk excitedly about the book.|[[The End script|"The End" script]], p. 10}} while Lucy is said to be 20.{{inline quote|VERY CLOSE ON: LUCY MACLEAN (20), reading a statement she has prepared.|[[The End script|"The End" script]], p. 7}} However, Norm's official [[Fallout season 1 Amazon overview|character description for ''Fallout'' season 1 on Amazon Prime]] calls him Lucy's younger brother, while the descriptions for ''Fallout'' season 2 only refers to him as her brother. And we will carry on until the day we bring that light to the surface.|"[[The Past]]"|sound=Betty Pearson.ogg}} '''Betty Pearson''' is a resident of [[Vault 33]] and a pre-[[Great War|War]] employee of the [[Vault-Tec Corporation]] {{In|FOTV}}. She becomes the [[overseer]] of Vault 33 in [[Timeline#2296|2296]] after the abduction of [[Hank MacLean]]. ==Background== [[File:FOTV s1 ep8 Young Betty.png|thumb|250px|left|Betty meets [[Cooper Howard]]]] Betty was a [[Vault-Tec Corporation]] employee before the [[Great War]], working as an executive assistant in the corporation's [[Vault-Tec headquarters (TV series)|Southern California headquarters]] and is from [[Solvang]], [[State#California|California]].{{FOTV|2|4}} She met [[The Ghoul|Cooper Howard]] when he visited the building and admitted to him that some of the corporation's knowledge was above her pay grade. She requested that Cooper meet his wife [[Barb Howard|Barb]]'s executive assistant [[Hank MacLean|Henry "Hank" MacLean]], as he was a big fan of the actor's work. [[File:Betty's cryonic chamber.png|thumb|right|250px|left|Betty's cryonic chamber]] She was [[Cryonics|cryonically]] frozen in [[Vault 31]] on the eve of the Great War as part of senior junior vice president [[Bud Askins]]' management training program "[[Bud's Buds]]." She was unfrozen on February 15, 2246, and later sent to [[Vault 33]].{{FOTV|1|8}}, 21:00 During her time in the Vault, she eventually became overseer before later retiring at some point. Hank MacLean, also sent from Vault 31, took her place as overseer in 2271. Around 2283, Hank orchestrated the [[Fall of Shady Sands|destruction of Shady Sands]], seemingly killing his wife [[Rose MacLean|Rose]], who had previously escaped to [[Shady Sands]], in the process. Though Betty's involvement in this event is unclear, she was evidently aware of his actions, as she helped cover up the circumstances of Rose's absence, including lying to Rose's children about having helped bury Rose (though this may be true in a metaphorical sense). By 2296, Betty had joined Vault 33's three-person governing council, working alongside [[Woody Thomas]] and [[Reg McPhee]]. Due to Woody's and Reg's personality traits, and her own training and experience, Betty became the effective leader of the council. Later that year, Hank was abducted in the attack on the Vault by [[Vault 32 raider]]s, and a crisis soon erupted when the Vault's [[Water chip (TV series)|water chip]] broke. The governing council was disbanded, and Betty was elected overseer in Hank's absence, beating Reg and Woody. Around this time, Hank's son [[Norm MacLean|Norm]] grew suspicious about the circumstances of the attack and the secrets behind his family, the Vaults, and Betty -- which Betty also seemed to be aware of. Working with Askins, who was the overseer of Vault 31, she initiated plans to reassign a group of Vault 33 dwellers to settle the now-abandoned Vault 32, and later covered up Norm's disappearance from Vault 33 (as a result of his having infiltrated, and subsequently being imprisoned inside, Vault 31). Since then, Betty has been focused on solving the issue of Vault 33's broken water chip. ==''Fallout'' TV series== ===Season 1=== {{Quotation|A former [[Overseer]], Betty is part of Vault 33's governing council along with [[Woody Thomas]] and [[Reg McPhee]]. She cares deeply for the community and holds paramount its security and safety. Her no nonsense personality and natural leadership skills make her the real face of the council despite what Woody and Reg would like to believe.|[[Fallout season 1 Amazon overview|''Fallout'' season 1 character description]]}} ====[[The End (episode)|The End]]==== [[File:FOTV S1 Amazon promo 16.jpg|thumb|250px|Betty approving Lucy's marriage application]] Betty approves Lucy's marriage application with [[Woody Thomas]] and [[Reg McPhee]]. During the wedding dance, Betty notices [[Chet (TV series)|Chet]] disappointed Lucy is married to [[Monty (TV series)|someone else]] and so she invites Chet to dance with her. [[File:Betty opposes opening Vault 33.png|thumb|250px|left|Betty opposes opening Vault 33]] Betty is mysteriously absent during [[Lee Moldaver]]'s raid on Vault 33, and it is unknown if she was hiding somewhere. When Lucy requests to open the Vault door to rescue her father, Betty feels everyone's first priority should be to maintain the security of the Vault and is against opening it. {{clear}} ====[[The Head]]==== [[File:The Head meeting Betty Reg Woody.png|thumb|250px|Betty, Reg and Woody leading the vault-wide meeting]] Betty appears during [[Norm MacLean]]'s job reassignment, saying that Norm put not just Vault 33 at risk, but Vault 31 and 32 as well. She claimed to have telegrammed with [[Bud Askins|the Overseer]] of Vault 31 and confirmed that they are unscathed. Eventually, she comes up with a new job for Norm: feeding the [[Vault 32 raider|raider prisoners]]. During the vault-wide meeting, Betty sits while Reg and Woody stand at the podium. When everyone discusses what should be done with the raiders, Betty feels Norm's idea of killing them should not be considered, although she empathizes with his anger. ====[[The Ghouls]]==== [[File:Betty brings pie.png|thumb|250px|left|Betty tells Norm to tread lightly]] Betty brings some pie she made herself to Norm. She comes to talk to him about how his vocalizing his desire to kill the raiders upset the Vault dwellers and that what he says carries weight because he is the only MacLean left in the Vault. Norm expresses how he feels guilty about hiding during the raid, and Betty notices how he feels angry about it. Betty comments that because Norm is clever, how he channels his anger can lead to dark places, and asks him to tread lightly before she leaves. ====[[The Past]]==== When Norm and Chet return from their morbid investigation of Vault 32, Betty asks the two men where they have been. They lie, but Betty seems suspicious of them. She is elected overseer of Vault 33 in 2296 to succeed Hank with 98% of the vote after his abduction, making her overseer again. During Betty's celebration ceremony, she is prepared to serve jello. Norm seems to disturb Betty when he prefers having a slice of cake instead of jello, which goes against the Vault Dwellers overwhelmingly preferring jello. Betty stares down Norm as he leaves, and his action suggests rebellion against her leadership. [[File:Betty and Norm.png|thumb|250px|Betty speaks to Norm in Vault 32 Overseer's office]] Later, Betty announces to the residents that she spoke with the overseer of Vault 31. The two of them agreed that the Vaults were too sacred to leave empty. She says the residents will partake in a resettling campaign. Norm asks Betty about his mother's Pip-Boy, and Betty replies that she buried it with Rose. ====[[The Radio]]==== [[File:Betty at Vault 32 door.png|thumb|250px|left|Betty tells the [[Vault 33 gatekeeper|gatekeeper]] to open the door]] Betty sends out new vault assignments to each dweller, with some staying in Vault 33, while others are to relocate to Vault 32. Later, Betty announces that [[Steph Harper]] is to be the new Overseer of Vault 32. Then she orders the inter-vault door to be opened and says good luck to the new dwellers of Vault 32 as they depart to enter. Meanwhile, Norm uses Betty's terminal to impersonate her and communicate with [[Bud Askins|the overseer]] of Vault 31, requesting a meeting. {{clear}} ===Season 2=== {{Quotation|After the raider attack on Vault 33 and Hank MacLean's abduction, Betty was elected to Overseer in Hank's place. With the Vault's water chip damaged, many in Vault 33 felt she was the obvious choice due to her previous tenure as Overseer.|[[Fallout season 2 Amazon overview|''Fallout'' season 2 character description]]}} ====[[The Innovator]]==== In [[Vault 33]], Betty Pearson discusses plans to repair the [[Water chip (TV series)|water chip]] with an [[Vault 33 engineer|engineer]]. [[Reg McPhee]] tries to help, but Betty hints that he should not interfere with important matters, suggesting, for example, that he create a support group. Reg takes her suggestion too seriously and organizes a support group for victims of inbreeding, which he himself is. ====[[The Demon in the Snow]]==== Betty is supervising a dwindling crop field when Reg crosses her while going on another water collection run for his support group. She chastises him for wasting water on his "snack club" that could be used to help the rest of the Vault. Reg is unfazed, reminding Betty she is dropping in popularity and had agreed to his terms for creating his support group, though he still meekly apologizes for his rude tone before hurrying away to get the water. ====[[The Other Player]]==== During another meeting of the [[Products of In-breeding Support Group]], Betty marches in with a team of [[Vault 33 guard|Vault security guards]] who deliver her orders to cut their snack budget and dissolve the group. Reg demands to see Betty, who walks in behind the lead guard. She calls Reg out for hiding away in his clubroom while she has been wanting to speak to him. Reg, realizing he might lose his place of importance, tries to make a popular stand by allowing the group to be dissolved but demanding the snack budget be left alone. Betty calls him out for celebrating during a water shortage in the Vault and exacerbating their problems by feeding people salty snacks. She remarks that they should not get special privileges just because of who their parents were, but Reg uses this statement to gain the crowd's support by claiming that they are still in "America" and they are all in the Vault because of who they are related to/descended from. Betty tries to calm the situation, but Reg takes it further, remarking on Betty's status as someone who came from [[Vault 31]] and acknowledging the Vault 31 dwellers' own claims that they are "plum different somehow." When Betty then tries to reference the Weevil Famine crisis, Reg rebukes her, saying nobody wants to hear about it anymore. This gains him the crowd's admiration, including a compliment from Marianne. As a final show of defiance, Reg grabs a handful of a jelly mold and devours it right in front of Betty, which fully turns the Vault 33 dwellers in the room to his side while Betty looks on in concern. ====[[The Handoff]]==== While loudspeakers in Vault 33 announce continued water restrictions, now prohibiting showers and even flushing the toilet, Betty sits in her office, lamenting that the situation is at a tipping point which leaves her with only one option. From a wall safe hidden behind a painting, she takes out Hank MacLean's Keepsake Box, which Steph demanded in exchange for giving water to Vault 33, while lamenting Hank's habit of keeping secrets. Later on, Betty stands in a shadowy corner of the inter-vault space as Steph comes to retrieve the box, where she then surprises Steph congratulates her on her engagement. Steph questions if this means Betty has spies in Vault 32, which Betty indirectly confirms. Betty pointedly notes that Steph still behaves like she did before the Great War, including her demeanor that often frightened her coworkers, then says that Betty herself has learned plenty in the time she has been awake. Steph draws a forced smile while responding that she had learned plenty of life lessons herself, even in the time before being frozen in Vault 31. As Steph goes to wheel the box out, Betty stops her and firmly reminds her fellow overseer that she gave her word to divert half of her Vault's water to 33. Steph matches her seriousness and says she will get what she wants, then walks back into her Vault. Betty calls out to say that she wants nothing to do with whatever Steph is planning, only wishing that it will not stop the Vaults from living in peace. Steph coldly responds that their deal was for the water exchange only, but she cannot speak for "[a] future [that's] bigger than [them]," leaving with a smile that unnerves Betty. ==Personality== [[File:Betty smiling.png|thumb|250px|Betty smiling]] Betty seems to be a kind and responsible member of her Vault; she also portrays herself as the coolheaded, experienced, moderator of Vault 33's governing council. She is seen comforting Chet, such as by asking him to dance during Lucy's wedding, as well as [[Norm MacLean]]. However, she is treated very suspiciously by Norm throughout the show, as if she is hiding a darker side. Norm finds it strange how Vault 32 was cleaned up, and Betty did not mention anything about what she found in it. While she claims killing the Vault 32 raiders is out of the question, it is unclear if she was the one who poisoned them. [[File:Betty sending assignments.png|thumb|left|250px|Betty sending out new vault assignments]] It is later revealed that Betty was one of Vault-Tec's employees who had been frozen through time. Betty claims she "buried" Rose MacLean when she died, although it is unclear if her choice of wording hints she was also responsible for nuking [[Shady Sands]] with Hank. It is also unknown if her motive for having people resettle into Vault 32 has a dark ulterior motive, especially given the water chip failure. However, she relocated Steph into the Vault as an overseer, another Vault-Tec employee; while this was done in continuation of the Three Vaults' experiment, Betty also notes that she hoped Steph would repay her by being cooperative in the future. She also made careful decisions about who was reassigned to Vault 32, including sending Chet while having Norm stay in Vault 33, suggesting she was trying to split up their partnership that was looking into the Vault's secrets. Later on, however, as the Vault's water crisis worsens, Betty demonstrates a greater deal of concern and dread about the fates of the Vault dwellers she oversees, including getting angry with and scolding [[Reg McPhee]] when his [[Products of In-breeding Support Group]] becomes a serious drain on their resources. She is initially angry with him when he refuses to obey her orders as overseer, but upon seeing that the Vault dwellers' support of her has fallen away, can only fall back on old platitudes that further harm her reputation in the Vault. After investigating Vault 31 and discovering Norm's escape and the death of Bud Askins, Betty fully reveals to Steph that for a long time before then, she had come to understand that Vault-Tec was never going to be their saving grace, and she wants to rededicate herself to ensuring the continued peace and prosperity of her Vault. This ultimately leads her to make what she sees as a [[wikipedia:Faustian pact|Faustian pact]] in having to fulfill Steph's demands to get access to 32's water and directly saying to Steph that she will not allow any of Steph's plans to endanger the safety of Vault 33. {{clear}} ==Notable quotes== * {{Inline quote|Regular boys... can get angry and they'll just pee on the wall. When clever boys like you are angry... You're lucky not to have seen where that can lead.|sound=Betty clever boys.ogg|Betty to Norm in "[[The Ghouls]]"}} ==Appearances== Betty Pearson appears {{in|FOTV}}. It's big.|Chet to [[Lucy MacLean|Lucy]]}} '''Chester "Chet"'''[[Fallout (TV series)]] Episode 5: "[[The Past]]" is a resident of [[Vault 33]] who later moves into [[Vault 32]] {{In|FOTV}}. ==Background== Chet was born a resident of [[Vault 33]] to a father named [[Chet Jr. (mentioned)|Chet Jr.]]. He is [[Lucy MacLean]]'s cousin, and prior to Lucy's marriage in 2296, he and Lucy were engaged in incestuous relations for about 10 years. Both of them consider these acts to be little more than "messing around" in their youth and fine for children, but not sustainable for the long term; however, Chet still finds himself in love with Lucy to some extent.[[Lucy MacLean]]: ''"Oh, gosh. After ten years of cousin stuff, I'm definitely excited for the real thing."''
({{FOTV|1|1}})Chet: ''"Lucy, I love you."''
[[Lucy MacLean]]: ''"We all know that, Chet. Messing around with your cousin, it's all well and good for kids, but it's not a sustainable, long-term sexual practice, you know?"''
Chet: ''"Yeah, I know."''
({{FOTV|1|1}})[[Lucy MacLean]]: ''"And you should know that I am not even a virgin. And that's not including all of the cousin stuff I did, which is at least a page or two on my resume."''
({{FOTV|2|3}}) He is also best friends with his cousin and Lucy's brother, [[Norm MacLean]]. At some point in Chet's life, Vault 33 was struck by a Weevil Famine, during which his father starved to death. This became somewhat of a source of trauma for Chet.Chet: ''"Well, see, Chet Jr. was my father's name. It's, uh, sort of a personal area for me, having watched him die of starvation in the Weevil Famine."''
({{FOTV|2|1}}) By 2296, Chet had been given the position of gatekeeper in Vault 33, meaning that he was responsible for opening the Vault's exterior door and intra-Vault doors when occasions required it. ==''Fallout'' TV series== ===Season 1=== {{Quotation|Lucy’s cousin, who also finds himself unshakably smitten with her — even though everyone knows messing around with your cousin is not a sustainable long-term sexual practice. He’s Norm’s best friend, and is loyal to a fault.|[[Fallout season 1 Amazon overview|''Fallout'' season 1 character description]]}} ====[[The End (episode)|The End]]==== Chet is first seen in Vault 33 as the dwellers begin to initiate the 2296 Triennial Trade with [[Vault 32]]. He initially tries to delay the trade due to his feelings for Lucy, claiming that the door system is malfunctioning, but she talks him into opening the door to allow the trade. During the wedding dance, he is clearly gloomy and heartbroken about not being able to love Lucy. [[Betty Pearson]] notices Chet's sorrow, and she invites him to dance to cheer him up. [[File:FOTV Official Trailer Still 032.png|thumb|250px|left|Chet trying to leave the Vault with [[Lucy MacLean|Lucy]]]] During the [[Vault 32 raider]]s' attack on Vault 33, Chet is manning the control panel for a door leading back to Vault 32. He is confronted by a [[burly raider]] carrying an incapacitated [[Vault 33 guard]], and Chet warns him to back away, but realizes he is in over his head when the raider takes a hit of a chem. He avoids the raider's lunge, accidentally causing the door to close and bisect the raider. When Lucy resolves to leave the vault in search of her father, Norm and Chet decide to help her. While Norm keeps lookout, Chet gains access to the elevator leading up to the surface entrance of the vault, and later prepares to open the Vault door for Lucy. Lucy asks him to take care of Norm for her, but Chet demands to join Lucy, leading her to tranquilize him to prevent anyone else from being hurt on her behalf, easing him down to the floor as he loses consciousness.[[Fallout (TV series)]] Episode 1: "[[The End (episode)|The End]]" ====[[The Head]]==== Chet is seen exiting the council room in Vault 33, having been reassigned from his gatekeeping duties for helping Lucy escape. Though he tries to downplay his feelings to Norm, smiling stiffly, he states that he is having a slight identity crisis due to losing his job.{{FOTV|1|3}} ====[[The Ghouls]]==== [[File:FOTV_The_Ghouls_Chet_and_Steph.png|thumb|250px|Chet and Steph kissing]] In his apartment, Chet is about to have a meal when [[Steph Harper]] swings by to check in on him, and he tells her he is despondent about losing both Lucy and his job. He then asks Steph if she is coping with the death of her husband [[Bert (TV series)|Bert]], and she comes in to offer Bert's belongings to Chet. Chet tries to offer condolences, saying that Bert was a "good man," but struggles to think of anything else to say about him apart from the good condition of his shoes. This leads to Chet being roped into accepting and being dressed in some of Bert's old clothes, which then causes Steph to start crying, apparently seeing Chet as Bert, and rushing into his arms. Chet confusedly tries to comfort Steph, and is even more confused when Steph starts kissing him, but quickly gets into it. He starts undressing Bert's clothes, but Steph tells him to keep them on. While they are kissing, Steph, who is pregnant, has her water break. Norm visits Chet's apartment while Steph is in labor, being attended to by [[Vault 33 medic|medics]], and asks Chet to help him enter [[Vault 32]]; Chet is all too happy to leave. The pair explore Vault 32 and find the residents had all been dead for at least two years, meaning the raiders did not kill them; Chet is left confused. They eventually enter the overseer's office and find the [[Ian Jackson|Vault 32 overseer]]'s corpse, with Chet concluding that the dwellers "went bananas;" Chet's opinion is reinforced by the graffiti on the walls, and he assumes that anyone left alive presumably allowed the Vault 32 raiders to enter. However, Norm finds out that his mother [[Rose MacLean|Rose]]'s Pip-Boy was used to open the Vault door, confusing both of them.[[Fallout (TV series)]] Episode 4: "[[The Ghouls]]" ====[[The Past]]==== [[File:FOTV S1 Amazon promo 4.jpg|thumb|250px|Chet and [[Norm MacLean|Norm]] after exploring Vault 32]] Still exploring Vault 32, Chet and Norm try to make sense of their findings; they soon also discover that many of the dwellers died trying to get into [[Vault 31]], which unsettles them into returning to Vault 33. They are discovered by [[Betty Pearson]] not long after they return, telling her -- unconvincingly -- that they were just planting [[tato]]s in the farm. Later, Norm sits with Chet in his apartment as Chet cares for Steph's newborn child. Norm, who has been further investigating the events in the Vaults, asks whether Chet is concerned about the fact that Vaults 32 and 33 only elect overseers from Vault 31; Chet does not suspect anything, assuming that Vault 31 is simply better equipped. He returns to playing with Steph's child, but Norm's look makes him sheepishly stop. Chet still claims not to find the situation strange, but Norm points out that he is whispering, though Chet claims this is because they broke the rules earlier and because Steph herself is from Vault 31. The following day, Betty Pearson takes everyone to a now-cleaned Vault 32 and announces a project to resettle the vault. Chet, pushing Steph in a wheelchair, and Norm are both left confused by this state of affairs. ====[[The Radio]]==== Betty releases the decisions for which dwellers have been reassigned to Vault 32; Chet receives notice of his and Steph's transfers while he is caring for Steph's child. Norm comes to visit Chet before he leaves, with Chet now handling all of the dishes and being told that he will have to do all of the packing for both him and Steph as well. He tells Norm that he will be living with Steph and her child in a starter home unit; Norm asks if he is simply going to ignore what happened during their investigation, and Chet feels he would rather try to have a fresh start. Norm calls Chet a coward, and he agrees, saying that they all are, given that they live in a Vault. He then closes the door on Norm. Later, Chet and the other transferees step through into Vault 32, being seen off by Betty, Norm, and other Vault 33 dwellers. As the door closes, Chet seems to experience a moment of regret as he watches Norm leave to continue the investigation. ===Season 2=== {{Quotation|Lucy and Norm's cousin, and Norm's best friend. In the aftermath of the raider attack on Vault 33, Chet finds himself a resident of Vault 32 without any designated purpose, aside from being the unwitting father figure for Overseer Steph's baby.|[[Fallout season 2 Amazon overview|''Fallout'' season 2 character description]]}} ====[[The Innovator]]==== In Vault 32, [[Steph Harper]] -- now the Vault's overseer -- has fully delegated [[Chet Jr.|her child]]'s care responsibilities to Chet, even though he's not her husband and the child isn't his. Chet, sitting outside Steph's office with the child, runs into [[Davey (TV series)|Davey]], who is leaving from a meeting with Steph. Davey gripes about Steph to Chet, who emphasizes his situation, though Davey doesn't seem to acknowledge it. In a measured manner, Chet points out his situation to Steph, asking if she will give him a new job, but she is content to have him keep caring for her child. Disgruntled, Chet specifically mentions that the child still doesn't have a name, mentioning that everyone calls him Chet Jr. Stephanie suggests giving the child that name, but Chet tries to protest, saying that the name Chet Jr. evokes unpleasant associations with his father's death during the Weevil Famine in Vault 33. Stephanie slams her knife into her desk, aggressively making it clear that she's not in the mood for an argument, and Chet reluctantly agrees to name the child Chet Jr. Left unnerved, Chet turns to leave when Steph asks if he knows how to use computers. Chet tells her that that was [[Norm MacLean|Norm]]'s specialty before leaving with the child. ====[[The Demon in the Snow]]==== While folding laundry and caring for Chet Jr, Chet listens in as [[Woody Thomas]] reports Steph's infraction of the Vault-Tec guidelines to Steph herself, revealing that he found out about her secret meeting with Betty. As Chet puts away clothes, he discovers a false bottom to a drawer in their dresser, finding a purse hidden underneath; inside the purse, he finds an ID card revealing that Steph was born before the Great War and that she was from [[Canada]]. This revelation shocks Chet, but he puts the ID back and chats with Woody as he leaves, pretending that nothing is wrong. On his way out, Woody asks about an "experiment" that he overheard Betty and Steph talking about, and this leaves Chet further shocked. After Woody leaves, he puts on a stiff smile for Steph and then closes the curtains on their apartment's bedroom. ====[[The Other Player]]==== While Chet is sitting nearby taking care of Chet Jr, Davey asks [[Irv]] if he has seen Woody, as they were meant to play checkers together that morning. Chet overhears Davey and calls him over, and Davey asks if he wants to know the truth; Chet is eager to hear it, but is let down when it turns out to be simply that Davey dislikes checkers and is merely playing for Woody. Irv says that they should tell Steph if Woody is missing. Davey scoffs, before apologizing to Chet for speaking bad about his wife. Chet reiterates that Steph is not his wife, but Davey simply corrects himself, calling her his fianceé with a knowing wink. This surprises Chet, who, after hearing about a poster, discovers said poster and finds out that he will be married to Steph in a wedding ceremony the next day. ====[[The Handoff]]==== {{section|FOTV}} ====[[The Strip]]==== {{section|FOTV}} ==Personality== [[File:FOTV Official Trailer Still 096.png|thumb|250px|Chet talking to Norm]] Chet is cowardly, but always good-hearted and loyal to his friends and his Vault. He is in love with Lucy, who does not return his feelings but likes him as a good friend and relative very much. After one final attempt to prevent Lucy's marriage with Monty, he respects her boundaries after. Due to being passive, Chet may be interpreted as easy to manipulate. For example, [[Steph Harper]] may have tried to seduce Chet and roped him into being the stepfather of her unborn child, replacing her deceased husband, [[Bert (TV series)|Bert]]. However, it is unclear how genuine Steph is. He also chooses to ignore the suspicious issues associated with the network of vaults in order to cling to the normalcy of his vault-life. ==Notes== * Given [[Hank MacLean]]'s origins, it can be presumed that Chet is related to Lucy on her [[Rose MacLean|mother]]'s side. * Chet is never explicitly referred to as "Chet III," but given his father's name was [[Chet Jr. (mentioned)|Chet Jr.]], this would indicate that he is the third in a line of Chets in his family. ==Appearances== Chet appears {{in|FOTV}}. He was also added to ''[[Fallout Shelter]]'' in update 1.17.0. {{FOTV appearances |1=101 |3=103 |4=104 |5=105 |7=107 |9=201 |12=204 |14=206 |15=207 |16=208 }} ==Gallery== FOTV Official Trailer Still 114.png|Chet prior to being splattered in blood in "[[The End (episode)|The End]]" FOTV Chet blood S1E1.png|Chet covered in blood in "The End" Chet The Past.png|Chet in "[[The Past]]" FOTV Chet wedding S2E7.png|Chet at the wedding in "[[The Handoff]]" FOTV Steph Chet "She's Canadian!" I'm sorry.|Dane to [[Maximus]] about their choice to injure themself}} '''Dane''' is a member of the [[Knights of San Fernando]], a chapter of the [[Brotherhood of Steel]] operating in the greater [[Los Angeles]] area in [[Timeline#2296|2296]]. They appear {{In|FOTV}}. Dane is the first known [[LGBT representation in the Fallout series|non-binary]] member of the Brotherhood in the ''Fallout'' series. ==Background== Nothing is known about Dane's history save for that they were not born into the Brotherhood of Steel, though how and when they were recruited is also unknown. In their military career, Dane has experienced living in the wasteland and knows the worst of how humanity can be. In joining the Brotherhood of Steel, Dane was attracted to the idea of having "brothers" and "sisters" that supported each other, and values in learning about technology. With Maximus, Dane is attracted to their fellow aspirant's fortitude and has sympathy towards him over his misgivings at failing to become a knight as they both dreamed, seemingly serving as his only close relationship in the organization.[https://youtu.be/3zPyFNwwBlQ?t=2013 Collider interview] ==''Fallout'' TV series== ===Season 1=== {{Quotation|Dane is a confident and eager Initiate of the Brotherhood of Steel, and [[Maximus]]'s closest peer. They believe in the mission of the Brotherhood and dream of one day suiting up as a Knight.|[[Fallout season 1 Amazon overview|''Fallout'' season 1 character description]]}} ====[[The End (episode)|The End]]==== [[File:FOTV BoS Base Clinic.png|thumb|left|200px|Maximus visits Dane in the camp clinic]] By [[Timeline#2296|2296]], Dane resides with the rest of their chapter at the Knights of San Fernando's [[Brotherhood base|main base]] somewhere on the West Coast. They are also the only friend Maximus apparently has among his fellow aspirants, whereas most others readily join in with [[Thaddeus]] in physically harassing and belittling Maximus. After the arrival of knights from the [[Brotherhood of Steel (Fallout 4)|Commonwealth chapter]] on the [[East Coast]], Dane ends up being among those selected for promotion to [[Brotherhood squire|squire]] under [[Titus|Knight Titus]], which Maxmius privately envies. However, shortly after, Dane is injured by a razor blade hidden in their boot that ends up maiming their ankle and incapacitating them. While some accused Maximus of orchestrating the incident out of jealousy for Dane's promotion, Dane themselves expresses that they don't believe those rumors about him. As a result of Dane's incapacitation, Maximus is chosen to take their place as Titus' squire during the manhunt for [[Siggi Wilzig]].{{FOTV|1|1}} ====[[The Beginning]]==== [[File:Dane The Beginning.png|thumb|200px|Dane seeing Maximus return]] When Maximus returns to the Brotherhood, Dane is shown to have recovered from their wound and now wears a [[scribe (TV series)|scribe]] uniform rather than that of a squire. Dane observes as Maximus reveals the death of Knight Titus and presents Elder Cleric [[Quintus]] with a [[critic|fake head]] posing as that of the target. After discovering the deception due to the head lacking the [[cold fusion]] device, Quintus accuses Maximus of lying about the artifact just as he lied about his culpability in Dane's maiming. When Quintus prepares to order Maximus' execution for treason, Dane interjects, confessing that their injury was self-inflicted and pleads that Elder Quintus listen to Maximus for the sake of the Brotherhood, which the Elder grants while commending such a rare display of loyalty from a member of the Brotherhood. Dane later confesses to Maximus the truth about how they deliberately maimed themselves with the razor blade, stating they feared dying horribly in the wasteland, and apologizes for the trouble it caused him as a result. Maximus forgives Dane, alluding to the fact that he never would have met [[Lucy MacLean]] if he had not become a squire. Maximus then confesses his intention to return to [[Vault 33]] with Lucy, with Dane warning their friend that nowhere is safe from violence in the wasteland and that leaving the Brotherhood is not an option.{{FOTV|1|8}} [[File:Maximus Dane battle.png|thumb|left|200px|Dane and Maximus during the [[Battle of Griffith Observatory]]]] Dane gears up and accompanies Maximus during the Brotherhood's [[Battle of Griffith Observatory|assault]] on the [[Griffith Observatory]] occupied by [[Lee Moldaver]] and the remnants of the [[New California Republic]] from [[Los Angeles]] with the aim of taking control of the cold fusion device brought to Moldaver by Lucy that can restore power to the ruined city. Maximus and Dane avoid the worst of the firefight outside the observatory, with the former later entering the structure ahead of the main contingent of Brotherhood forces. Maximus is knocked out by [[Hank MacLean]] in a stolen suit of [[T-60 power armor (TV series)|T-60 power armor]] and left there by Lucy and [[the Ghoul]] to be found by Dane shortly after. When Dane discovers the dead body of Moldaver who succumbed to her wounds before they arrived, though Maxmius tries to say he was not responsible, when the other members of the Brotherhood of Steel arrive, Dane uses the opportunity to assert that Maximus dealt the killing blow and credits him with taking down the rebel leader, pushing for him to be granted knighthood for the feat. They raise a chant of "Knight Maximus" as the Brotherhood hails him as a hero, unaware of Maximus' discomfort with the manner of his promotion. ===Season 2=== {{Quotation|Dane is a scribe of the Brotherhood of Steel, and was once Maximus’s closest peer. After surviving the battle against the NCR at Griffith Observatory, Dane was the first to hail Maximus as a Knight for his supposed defeat of Lee Moldaver.|[[Fallout season 2 Amazon overview|''Fallout'' season 2 character description]]}} ====[[The Golden Rule]]==== Dane continues in their duties as a scribe during the San Fernando chapter's mobilization to claim [[Area 51]] as their base of operations. They meet with Maximus as he is polishing his claw-marked suit of T-60 power armor, remarking on Maximus' renewed adherence to the [[Codex]]. Dane tries to remind him of his former goal to reunite with Lucy and the better life he wanted with her, but Maximus asserts that the Brotherhood is the best hope for improving the wasteland. This further concerns Dane, as they change the subject to Quintus' impending meeting with the elders of other Brotherhood chapters, particularly their deliberate exclusion of the [[Brotherhood of Steel (Fallout 4)|Commonwealth chapter]]. The conversation is interrupted by the arrival of the other chapters' airships as Maximus goes to attend. Dane stands among the ranks during the elders' meeting, where they instigate their rebellion against the Commonwealth to return power over the wider Brotherhood back to the West Coast. During this, Dane alerts Maximus to [[Gnatius|Knight Gnatius]] and [[Riley (TV series)|Knight Riley]] playing hot potato with a live [[plasma grenade]], which he then confiscates. In the subsequent celebration, Dane observes as Maximus is challenged to a bare-back duel with a [[Coronado knight|knight]] from the [[Coronado Brotherhood of Steel|Coronado chapter]]. After he kills the knight, Maximus notices Dane's somber expression as they walk away from the violent spectacle. Dane remains nearby to witness the arrival of [[Xander Harkness|Paladin Xander Harkness]], the liaison of the Commonwealth Brotherhood.{{FOTV|2|2}} ====[[The Demon in the Snow]]==== Dane meets Maximus on the flight deck of the ''Caswennan'' after he is brought back from his impromptu "hunting trip" with Xander Harkness, telling him that Quintus is enraged by his action. When Dane sees the paladin (actually [[Thaddeus]] impersonating Xander) awkwardly moving around in his power armor, they deduce right away that something went wrong. Maximus confirms that he killed Xander and Dane wryly responds that the Commonwealth will most certainly be gunning for the West Coast chapters as a result. Maximus claims to have a plan to resolve this, and tells Dane to gather all of the aspirants in a safe place. Confused, Dane is left shocked when Maximus reveals that he plans to kill Quintus to prevent conflict. While Maximus is meeting with Quintus and Thaddeus is off in the cafeteria masquerading as Harkness, Dane leads a group of aspirants (including a [[young aspirant]] whom Maximus mentored earlier) into an empty garage room, warning them not to leave "until the shooting stops." Dane then leaves to sneak into the hangar containing the cold fusion relic and finds it unguarded, allowing them to remove the diode. However, their theft is discovered shortly thereafter by the Grand Canyon elder, causing him to accuse the other elders of being the thieves and inciting all-out conflict between the chapters. Dane navigates the chaos to find Maximus having just locked the still-living Quintus in his chamber. Though Maximus apologizes for having left Quintus alive, Dane consoles him, saying he should not be sad over refusing to take a life, even that of Quintus. Dane gives Maximus the relic, telling him to take it far away from the Brotherhood, saying that they trust Maximus for being the only person at Area 51 who is not a "total asshole." Dane and Maximus hug; Maximus questions what Dane will do, and Dane responds that they'll survive like they always have. While Maximus and Thaddeus subsequently flee, Dane remains behind at the base as the airship fleet launches attacks on each other and sends one crashing into the desert nearby. ====[[The Strip]]==== Amidst the chaos of the civil war started by Maximus' and their own actions, Dane brings Quintus the blueprints for [[Liberty Prime|Liberty Prime Alpha]] and is present when he announces that he now seeks to destroy the Brotherhood, rather than reunify it. ==Personality== [[File:Dane and Maximus.png|thumb|200px|Dane and Maximus looking at power armor]] Dane is shown to be kind towards Maximus, the two of them having a shared dream of being able to don the signature [[T-60 power armor (TV series)|T-60 power armor]] of a knight. However, Dane also lacks foresight in their actions, seemingly unaware that Maximus would be given the blame for their self-inflicted maiming. Dane is also shown to lack the bravery expected in a knight, being frightened by the idea of having to venture into the wasteland to the point of willingly injuring themselves with a razor blade to avoid being sent on missions to the [[Wilds]]. Despite this, Dane seemed to be excited about the idea beforehand, suggesting Dane was merely putting on a brave face in order to gain the respect of their peers, or conforming to the Brotherhood's expectations of its members. Dane later expresses immense guilt when Maximus is falsely announced to be dead. Whereas Maximus is ambitious in wanting to climb the Brotherhood ranks or even leave the Brotherhood to pursue his own agenda, Dane meekly resigns themself to Brotherhood life, and accepts their punishment for their cowardice, even though that means they would be used as cannon fodder in the upcoming battle. After the Battle of Griffith Observatory and Maxmius' ascension to knighthood, Dane expresses concern that their friend is falling deep into the Brotherhood's militaristic dogmatism, hoping to remind him of his former ideal to live a happier life with Lucy, and is concerned to see Maximus participating in the violent spectacle when he is challenged to a fight by a Coronado knight. Their worries for Maximus' fate increase even more after finding out that he was responsible for the death of Xander Harkness and irrevocably set the Brotherhood on the path to civil war, yet Dane remains steadfast as an ally, stealing the cold fusion relic and giving it to Maximus to keep it out of Quintus' hands even as Dane themselves resolves to stay behind while their friend flees. ==Notes== Aspirant Dane is referred to with they/them pronouns by the clergy and could be described as apparently gender non-conforming. ==Notable quotes== * {{Inline quote|There's nowhere safe, Max. And there's no leaving. I wish there was!}} ==Appearances== Dane appears only {{in|FOTV}}. Researcher |affiliation =[[Enclave]] (formerly)
[[Vault-Tec Corporation]] (formerly)
[[Lee Moldaver]] |TV actor =[[Michael Emerson]] |stunt double=[[Frank Alfano Jr.]] |special ={{SPECIAL|3,7,6,5,10,5,4}} {{Icon|FOS}} }} {{Quotation|If you insist on staying, then you will have to adapt.|Wilzig to [[Lucy MacLean|Lucy]]}} '''Doctor Siggi Wilzig''' is an associate of [[Lee Moldaver]] and former member of the [[Enclave]] until his defection around [[Timeline#2296|2296]]. He appears {{In|FOTV}}. ==Background== Siggi Wilzig is known to have lived before the [[Great War]], and it is suggested that he had already started working for the Enclave by that time. In the late 2070s, he was sent to the [[Vault-Tec headquarters (TV series)|Vault-Tec headquarters]] in [[Los Angeles]] to deliver a message to [[Vault-Tec Corporation]] executive [[Barb Howard]], threatening her into claiming that Vault-Tec would be willing to cause nuclear war during an upcoming meeting of American corporate leaders. Wilzig already seemed disillusioned at this time, noting that he was also forced to do what he did under threat of his own life, and believing that no one would be able to stop the plans for the end of the world.Wilzig: ''"You're just a very replaceable part in this machine."''
[[Barb Howard]]: ''"I'm sorry, who are you?"''
Wilzig: ''"But if you forget your place in the company... you'll die. And so will your family. The same will happen to me if I don't communicate this message. We're all in the same boat. And not one of us can stop it. You know that. You wake up knowing it. The leaders of the most powerful corporations will be gathering here. And when they do... you tell them... the only way to guarantee results is-- [by dropping the bomb yourselves.]"''
({{FOTV|2|6}}) Wilzig survived the end of the world and the two hundred years that followed by unknown means. For many years prior to 2296, he lived in an isolated Enclave cell, an unnamed [[Enclave research colony|research colony]] located in a mountainous, snowy region of North America.[https://web.archive.org/web/20240114045401/https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/2023/11/fallout-first-look Fallout First Look: This Is How the World Ends—With a Smiling Thumbs-Up (Archived)] ==''Fallout'' TV series== During his time conducting scientific research for the Enclave, Wilzig came into possession of [[Lee Moldaver]]'s [[cold fusion]] technology that had been appropriated by the [[Vault-Tec Corporation]] before the [[Great War]].{{FOTV|1|1}} Aside from that, he also participated in the Enclave's behavioral conditioning research involving [[Dog|canines]]. Wilzig personally saved [[CX404]] from being incinerated at birth by lying about her weight and sheltering her in his private laboratory while training her up. At some point, he secretly came into contact with Moldaver and also learned about the [[Three Vaults]] in [[Los Angeles]], Moldaver's close ally [[Rose MacLean]] and her daughter Lucy. A few years before 2296, Wilzig rescued CX404 by falsifying her weight, as all puppies under 10 oz had to be incinerated. He kept her hidden in an alcove behind a chalkboard in his laboratory while training her and continuing his work on cold fusion. He eventually injected the cold fusion technology into himself, below the right ear. One day, an [[Enclave administrator|administrator]] walked in on him with CX404 and confronted him for secretly keeping and raising a canine. Seeing Wilzig as under threat in this exchange, CX404 attacked and killed the administrator. Since the alarm had been sounded, Wilzig knew that he and CX404 needed to leave immediately. They were fired upon by a [[Machinegun turret (TV series)|turret]] while trying to get away but were able to escape unharmed due to its incredibly poor accuracy. As a result of his defection, however, a [[bounty]] was put on them both, attracting the attention of both [[bounty hunter]]s like [[Honcho]] and [[the Ghoul]][[Honcho]]: ''"A bounty came down. A huge one. Enough to be a last score for me and whoever's with me. Yeah. Now, somebody made a run from the Enclave."''
[[The Ghoul]]: ''"Well, what makes you think I'd give a good goddamn about that?"''
Honcho: ''"It ain't where they's running from I figured you'd be interested in. It's where they's running to. That witch Moldaver. In California. That's where you from, ain't it? Originally, I mean."''
({{FOTV|1|1}}) and groups like the [[Brotherhood of Steel (Lost Hills)|Brotherhood of Steel]] in [[New California]] (who received word of Wilzig's Enclave connections from the [[Brotherhood of Steel (Fallout 4)|Commonwealth chapter]] on the [[East Coast]]).{{FOTV|1|2}}[[Quintus]]: ''"Our mission comes from the highest clerics in the Commonwealth. It is believed that a denizen of the Enclave has escaped."''
Squire: ''"The Enclave's real?"''
Quintus: ''"And that he has with him an object of profound potential to harm our nation or to save it. Each knight in this legion will search a section of the Wilds for this target. Brothers, we exist for moments such as these. Go forth with honor! And may the shape of the future be cut by your sword!"''
({{FOTV|1|1}}) At one point, the duo stopped in a clearing in [[the Wilds]] where Wilzig tried to consume a trail ration of [[Cram]] before being forced to flee after CX404 came back with a severed hand she had picked up from a nearby cave, hinting at the danger nearby; as [[Maximus]] and [[Titus|Knight Titus]] discovered later when they tracked Wilzig's movements to the cave, it was home to a [[Yao guai (TV series)|yao guai]]. Wilzig's trek towards reaching Moldaver later brought him to a chance encounter with [[Lucy MacLean]] shortly after she had left [[Vault 33]] to track down Moldaver too and rescue [[Hank MacLean|her father]]. Wilzig attempted to warn her about the dangers of going unprepared in the wasteland, evidenced by CX404 snacking on a [[Radroach (TV series)|radroach]] that had been stalking Lucy, remarking on how it had adapted to its surroundings to survive while telling her to return home before she ended up dead. After she insisted on continuing her journey, Wilzig gave one last word of warning that the wasteland might change her for the worst before she reaches her goal, before he and CX404 left to continue on their own way. A short time after Lucy got there, Wilzig reached the trading town of [[Filly]] where he had planned to rendezvous with [[Ma June]] to complete passage to Moldaver's territory, where he also expressed his intimate knowledge of Lucy's home Vault. Before they could talk more, Wilzig was ambushed by the Ghoul and received a severe wound to his left leg from [[Mare's Leg (TV series)|his revolver]],[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TS5KcXj-Obc YouTube: Walton Goggins Talks Fallout, His White Lotus Panic Attack and His Dad Forging His Signature] forcing Ma June to fit him with a [[Jim's Limbs]]-brand prosthetic. After getting the coordinates to Moldaver's stronghold from Ma June, Lucy helped Wilzig escape from Filly after the Ghoul got into a fight with Maximus in his [[T-60 power armor (TV series)|T-60 power armor]]. However, due to the severity of the wound and the prosthetic's sub-par design, Wilzig realized he would die from blood loss and shock before ever reaching his destination. After getting as far as the desert plains near [[Los Angeles International Airport]], Wilzig discreetly consumed a [[Plan D]] cyanide pill to hasten his end. Once Lucy found out about this, Wilzig requested that she carry out the delivery of the cold fusion (though she did not know the exact nature) by using his [[Ripper#Surgical Ripper|Ripper]] to sever his head and take it with her to Moldaver. Just before expiring, Wilzig calls her by her last name, confusing Lucy further. ==Personality== According to his actor Michael Emerson, Wilzig is a "disenchanted loner with a big heart" who ends up getting involved with some "deep stuff."[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7H9_nIdp_Yw GVN Exclusive Interview: Jonathan Nolan & Michael Emerson Talk Amazon Prime 'Fallout' Series] In the TV series, Wilzig repeatedly expresses concern for Lucy's safety traveling in the wasteland and tries to convince her to return to her Vault. When he sees no other option for the success of his mission except for Lucy to carry his head, he takes his own life by privately ingesting a cyanide pill to spare her the trauma of personally killing him. In his final words to her, he expresses great trust and hope in her abilities. He harbored great affection for CX404 and was mortified to witness her apparent death at the hands of the Ghoul while she was protecting him in Filly. CX404 also cared for Wilzig as she relentlessly tracked down his head after their separation. ==Appearances== Siggi Wilzig appears {{in|FOTV}}. While he only appears fully in one episode of the first season, his severed head also appears in all subsequent episodes of the first season. {{FOTV appearances|2=102|14=206}} As of July 18, 2024 (version 1.18.0) he also appears in ''[[Fallout Shelter]]''. ==Behind the scenes== * Doctor Siggi Wilzig shares a name with [[wikipedia:Siggi B. Wilzig|Siggi B. Wilzig]], a [[wikipedia:The Holocaust|Holocaust]] survivor, self-made billionaire, and philanthropist who helped fund the [[wikipedia:United States Holocaust Memorial Museum|U.S. Holocaust Memorial Museum]]. * Much of Wilzig's character appears to be a nod to Harold Finch, Michael Emerson's character on the TV series ''[[wikipedia:Person of Interest (TV series)|Person of Interest]]''. Like Finch, Wilzig's pet dog is a Belgian Malinois (Bear for Finch, CX404/Dogmeat for Wilzig). Wilzig also ends up having a nasty limp after losing his foot and having to use a prosthetic, not unlike Finch's distinctive gait brought on as a result of spinal injuries. ** Wilzig's line to Barb Howard in season 2's "[[The Other Player]]" about her being "a very replaceable part in this machine" (referring to the Enclave) similarly references Harold Finch. Finch created an artificial intelligence called The Machine to predict threats to the United States government, wheras Wilzig works for a shadow organization within the U.S. government. ==Gallery== Fallout Season 1 Amazon Wilzig.png|Amazon preview FOTV Wilzig in Enclave lab.png|Working on cold fusion FOTV Official Trailer Still 097.png|Wilzig readying an injection FOTV S1 Ep2 Siggy with dog.png|Siggi with [[CX404]] FOTV Enclave research colony 21.png|Siggi and CX404 flee the Enclave colony FOTV Trailer 1 14.png|Lucy meets Wilzig FOTV Wilzig Enclave Civvies.png|In civilian clothes FOTV S1 Amazon promo 9.jpg|In Filly with Lucy and [[Ma June]] Pip boy tv series tracking device.png|Lucy with his head ;Fallout Shelter FOS Siggi Wilzig Promo.jpg|Promo image introducing them in ''Fallout Shelter'' FOS Wilzig.png|Sprite ==References== {{References}} '''External''' {{References|group=Ext}} {{Navbox characters FOTV}} {{Navbox cyborgs}} {{Navbox Enclave}} {{Navbox characters FOS}} [[Category:Fallout TV series human characters]] [[Category:Enclave characters]] [[Category:Fallout Shelter characters]] [[ja:Siggi_Wilzig]] [[ru:Доктор Зигги Вильциг]] [[uk:Сіггі Вілзіґ]] [[zh:西吉·威尔齐格]]
