({{FOTV|2|6}}) The two of them had a daughter, Janey, who was born on April 14, 2065.[[Cooper Howard]]: ''"You said you knew everything."''
Robert House: ''"I routinely design and run mathematical paradigms based on global, political, and socioeconomic conditions in an effort to... predict future events. And one spring morning, the data coalesced, and it told me, in no uncertain terms, that the world would... well, end."''
Cooper Howard: ''"Calculator told you that?"''
Robert House: ''"The date of the end of the world may not interest you, Mr. Howard. But the date the data coalesced might. April 14th, 2065, at 5:17 a.m. Is that date of any interest to you?"''
Cooper Howard: ''"That's my daughter's birthday."''
Robert House: ''"Oh, that is vexingly curious, isn't it? More curious is that you were not meant to come to Vegas this weekend. Your wife Barbara was meant to come alone. The moment that you bought your ticket to Las Vegas, the date the world was going to end... jumped forward by one month."''
Cooper Howard: ''"What are you, a f-fortune teller now?"''
Robert House: ''"I am a mathematician, a roboticist, and a casino owner. And I don't know yet how you figure into all of this, but you most certainly do. And I don't like unknown variables. Irksome. Not knowing exactly how you play a part in ending the world."''
({{FOTV|2|5}}) After the breakout of the [[Sino-American War]] and the [[China|Chinese]] invasion of [[Alaska]], Barb stayed home with their daughter while her husband was deployed to Alaska with the [[United States Marine Corps]]. She claims to Cooper that she was worried every day whether or not he would return alive; dreading every time she opened a letter in the mail, and she would always try to be near the phone in case she got a call saying he had been killed in action.[[The Ghoul|Cooper Howard]]: ''"No, I want to know about my freedom. I didn't go to war defending that freedom so that I could live in a cellar under the boot heel of Chairman Bud Askins."''
Barb Howard: ''"And while you were away at war, I stayed home."''
Cooper: ''"I know--"''
Barb: ''"I was checking the mail every day."''
Cooper: ''"I know."''
Barb: ''"I was waiting by the phone every night. And every night I was driving myself crazy imagining the worst. So, no, you do not need to tell me how bad war is, Coop."''
({{FOTV|1|6}}) ===Working for Vault-Tec=== At some point, Barb acquired a job for the [[Vault-Tec Corporation]] and, by the 2070s, had managed to climb the corporate ladder to a high-ranking executive position. She claimed to Cooper (and to herself) that all of her work at Vault-Tec was for the purpose of ensuring that her family would be guaranteed a future, whether that be in future employment or in survival after the bombs dropped.Barb Howard: ''"Every day I go into work and I think about how humanity can survive a nuclear event that will wipe out 90% of life on earth and I come home and you're talking to me about hiding out at a ranch up in Bakersfield. You know, I don't even know what planet you're on sometimes, Coop. But when the bombs drop, a two-hour drive ain't gonna cut it. So yes, there will be no dogs in the vaults. And no, none of it is ideal. But if billions of people are going to lose their lives, I will do whatever it takes to make sure the people I love... that is you and that is Janey... aren't among them. I have worked hard to make sure we go into a special vault for management, where we will oversee all of the other vaults. You don't get it. That is the best we can possibly hope for. For Janey."''
({{FOTV|1|6}})Barb Howard: ''"Don't walk away from me, Coop. I know more than you know, okay? There are over 12,000 nuclear warheads set-"''
[[Cooper Howard]]: ''"I'm not a board member. I am your husband."''
Barb: ''"Don't--"''
Cooper: ''"I don't care about your fuckin' statistics."''
Barb: ''"Statistics? This is about Janey."''
Cooper: ''"So... four our daughter, you would kill millions of people."''
Barb: ''"Don't do that."''
Cooper: ''"Billions of people. Other-other mothers just like you."''
Barb: ''"Don't do that, Coop, do not do that."''
Cooper: ''"Other daughters just like our daughter!"''
Barb: ''"Wouldn't you? For Janey. Wouldn't you? There are worse people out there than me, Coop."''
Cooper: ''"Who? Who could possibly be worse than you?"''
({{FOTV|2|6}}) On the former side, Barb managed to secure a role for Cooper in advertising Vault-Tec and its products, and also (only half-jokingly) considered having Janey join Vault-Tec's payroll as well in the future.[[Cooper Howard]]: ''"You ever... think about working somewhere else?"''
Barb Howard: ''"I used to. But with you doing these ads, it's... it's practically the family business. Maybe we get Janey a job in payroll when she's 15."''
({{FOTV|1|6}}) In the latter, Barb worked to land spots for herself and her family in a special Vault reserved for [[Vault-Tec Corporation|Vault-Tec]] management to oversee all the other Vaults—one of the "good Vaults," in her words.[[Cooper Howard]]: ''"Bud Askins."''
Barb Howard: ''"Bud Askins. Trust me, I know. The company's filled with guys like him. But Vault-Tec exists with or without me. Doesn't do anyone any good to complain from the sidelines."''
Cooper: ''"All I'm saying is we have this one life. Do you really want to spend your nine-to-fives working with these assholes?"''
Barb: ''"I need this job, Coop. It guarantees us a spot in the vaults."''
Cooper: ''"We got money. We can buy a spot in the vaults."''
Barb: ''"One of the good vaults."''
Cooper: ''"What's that supposed to mean?"''
Barb: ''"I'm doing what I can, okay? Just... trust me. Please."''
({{FOTV|1|6}}) This was especially important to Barb, as she was all too familiar with the corporate callousness of Vault-Tec managers such as her subordinate [[Bud Askins]],[[Bud Askins]] to Barb: ''"Our internal early alert system gives us at minimum 30 minutes from notice to ignition in downtown Los Angeles. You know, we'd be crazy not to offer specialized freeway lanes for our premium customers. I mean, that's just money on the table right there."''
({{FOTV|2|6}})[[Norm MacLean]]: ''"You don't strike me as the kind of person who would sign up for a program like this. Did you know going in about the Future Enterprise Ventures?"''
[[Claudia (TV series)|Claudia]]: ''"Like I said, I just started this job a week ago. But everything these people talked about sounded pretty nutty to me."''
Norm MacLean: ''"But you don't remember what they said? Nothing about doing something to the people in Vault 32 or 33?"''
Claudia: ''"No. There was this exec. Bud's boss? Her name was Barbara Howard. She was in charge of all the Vault proposals."''
({{FOTV|2|5}}) and she was also aware of the true purpose of the Vaults: Barb had the position of approving any and all proposals made for Vault experiments, and so had access to information about subjects such as the [[Forced Evolutionary Virus]]. She was also given notice of deadly flaws such as the high failure rate of the [[Water chip (TV series)|water chips]]. In effect, she had some ability to control who lived and who died.[[Vault-Tec engineer]] to Barb: ''"The bad news is our water chips have a 30% fail rate. The good news is we'll know which ones fail before installation. So, we get to choose who runs out of water. Any, uh, preferences?"''
({{FOTV|2|6}}) To her family, she heavily downplayed her role in Vault-Tec, presenting herself as a voice of reason among corporate zealots such as Bud Askins. These secrets weighed on Barb, but she ultimately chose not to resist, convincing herself it was all for her family's survival. She was further convinced not to defy the company when she received a threat from an [[Siggi Wilzig|unknown man]] representing [[Enclave|some unknown party]], warning that her family would be killed if she did not claim during an upcoming meeting of corporate leaders that Vault-Tec would be willing to guarantee the effectiveness of its Vaults by starting the nuclear war themselves. This convinced Barb that Vault-Tec was being controlled by a hidden power from the shadows, with plans of their own for the company and beyond,[[Siggi Wilzig|Wilzig]]: ''"You're just a very replaceable part in this machine."''
Barb Howard: ''"I'm sorry, who are you?"''
Wilzig: ''"But if you forget your place in the company... you'll die. And so will your family. The same will happen to me if I don't communicate this message. We're all in the same boat. And not one of us can stop it. You know that. You wake up knowing it. The leaders of the most powerful corporations will be gathering here. And when they do... you tell them... the only way to guarantee results is--"''
Barb Howard: ''"By dropping the bomb ourselves."''
({{FOTV|2|6}}) but it also convinced her to keep in her lane, seeing any further actions as futile;[[Cooper Howard]]: ''"Who threatened you?"''
Barb Howard: ''"Please, Coop. You don't need to get involved in any of this."''
Cooper Howard: ''"Who controls Vault-Tec?"''
Barb Howard: ''"I don't know."''
Cooper Howard: ''"Well, let's find out."''
Barb Howard: ''"No, no, no, no, no. This is not one of your movies with a happy ending. There is nothing we can do. If there was, I would have done it. I tried to do it. This deal is going forward whether we like it or not. Please, look at me. I am your wife. You know me. You know me."''
Cooper Howard: ''"I don't. I don't know you, Barbara."''
({{FOTV|2|6}}) even dropping the bombs could be justified if it kept her family safe. ===Falling out with Cooper=== Cooper's participation in Vault-Tec gradually began to wear on him, and his and Barb's affiliations with the company eventually became a point of contention in their relationship. However, they seemed to be stable overall, even as Barb was left conflicted by the apocalyptic plans she had been roped in being a part of. What Barb did not know was that Cooper had also become aware of her secrets: Cooper had met [[Lee Moldaver|Kate Williams]], a scientist whose work on [[cold fusion]] was bought up by Barb's division in Vault-Tec to prevent the technology from threatening their business model,[[Cooper Howard]]: ''"How do you know my wife?"''
Miss Williams: ''"My research company was acquired by her division. We were developing this kind of technology that's... difficult to monetize. Cold fusion. Infinite energy. That's what I was on the verge of achieving when Vault-Tec swept in and bought up every company I'd ever worked for."''
({{FOTV|1|7}}) and Williams gave him the means to spy on his wife and learn the truth. Cooper took this opportunity at just the right time to hear Barb delivering the proposal to start nuclear war.As shown in {{FOTV|1|8}} Not long afterwards, Barb was scheduled to visit Las Vegas during a defense contractors' summit in order to present the cold fusion technology to magnate [[Robert House]], who had struck a deal with Vault-Tec to receive it in exchange for having given them his "[[Brain-computer interface chip|automated man]]" mind control chip technology; he did not tell her what he would use it for, only that she would find out "after the bombs drop."[[Robert House's double]]: ''"RobCo presents the automated man. Spent a lot of time trying to make my machines more lifelike, but, hey, works the other way around, too."''
Barb Howard: ''"Mr. House, Vault-Tec and RobCo have always had a special arrangement. You have multiple Vaults to do with as you wish. If this is the research you'd like to pursue in the Vaults, you--"''
Robert House's double: ''"You must have missed the telegram. You're paying me for this. In exchange, I get Cold Fusion to power my little project in Vegas."''
Barb: ''"And what project is that?"''
House's double: ''"Might be above your paygrade. You'll find out about it after the bombs drop, I guess."''
({{FOTV|2|6}}) Cooper went with her, having been convinced by Williams that House would instead be selling nuclear weapons to Vault-Tec in exchange for cold fusion, which would then enable them to start the nuclear war. However, House subsequently met with Cooper, revealing his true intentions for the technology and that he did not believe Barb, Vault-Tec, or any other corporation would start the war—but that some other, hidden player might instead.{{FOTV|2|5}} Left reeling from the news but not actually believing House, Cooper subsequently confronted Barb, revealing that he knew of her and Vault-Tec's secrets. They briefly experienced a major falling out, though Barb still helped Cooper retrieve the cold fusion diode from [[Hank MacLean]], Barb's personal assistant, who had come with them to act as the carrier, and the two of them repaired their bond by agreeing to try and subvert what they believed were Vault-Tec's plans to start the apocalypse.{{FOTV|2|6}} To do so, Cooper gave the diode to the [[Last President of the United States|U.S. president]], with Barb's full awareness;{{FOTV|2|7}} though the two believed they had managed to end the conspiracy for good, they were proven wrong when Cooper was arrested on the orders of the [[House Un-American Activities Committee]] soon afterwards (the president was a member of the [[Enclave]], the hidden power behind Vault-Tec). Having been warned by House of his impending arrest, Cooper ordered his wife to let him take the fall for Janey's sake rather than fighting it, telling Barb to deny any involvement in his activities.{{FOTV|2|8}} The events that directly followed are currently unknown. Regardless, by October 2077, Barb and Cooper were publicly believed to have gotten divorced.[[Frank (TV series)|Frank]]: ''"Why the hell is Cooper Howard working kids' birthday parties?"''
[[Bob Spencer]]: ''"What else? Alimony."''
({{FOTV|1|1}}) On October 23, the day of the Great War, Cooper was with their daughter Janey, performing at a birthday party in [[Hollywood Hills]]. The ensuing events are unclear; Cooper was evidently separated from Janey at some point and either knew or believed that she and Barb had managed to get to safety inside one of Vault-Tec's management Vaults, though he did not know if he was correct, or which facility they would have entered. ===Post-War events=== Barb and Janey indeed had [[cryonics|cryo-stasis]] chambers allotted for them inside the executive preservation wing of the [[Las Vegas management Vault]], but it is unknown if either of them ever used them. Barb is suggested to have entered the facility at one point, though the only evidence of this is a [[Colorado]] postcard placed in her cryo chamber seemingly as a message for her husband.As seen in {{FOTV|2|5}}, the Vault-Tec facility has cryonic chambers with Barb's and Janey's names on them, which are shown to be occupied. The episode also seems to show a human silhouette inside Barb's cryonic chamber, though it is later revealed to be empty in "[[The Strip]]." Not knowing this, Cooper spent the next two centuries traveling all across the post-War United States in search of his family. Though he found numerous other Vaults over the years, including some management Vaults, he never found his family there, or even any clues to where they could have gone.[[Lucy MacLean]]: ''"I'd ask why my dad ran into a den of giant monsters, but you'd probably just tell me to shut the fudge up."''
[[The Ghoul]]: ''"[sighs] Before the war, there was a plan... for a special Vault. A Vault for management. That's where my wife is. Where my daughter is, too."''
Lucy MacLean: ''"You never found it?"''
The Ghoul: ''"Oh no, I found one, in California. It was empty. Found another one in Oregon. It was empty, too. Turns out, there's more than a few special Vaults for management sprinkled across the Wasteland. All of 'em empty. But I've never found one in Vegas."''
Lucy MacLean: ''"So, you think if my dad's in there, maybe your wife and daughter are, too?"''
The Ghoul: ''"Uh-huh. And now, they're surrounded by these fuckin' things."''
({{FOTV|2|5}}) This seemed to change in 2296, when Cooper (now [[ghoul]]ified, and going by [[the Ghoul]]) tracked a still-surviving Hank MacLean to New Vegas, convinced that Hank would lead him to a Vault-Tec facility where Barb and Janey may have been preserved. This seemed to be confirmed by Hank when he threatened Cooper into abandoning his pursuit by claiming to hold his family hostage via the control of their cryonic chambers in the Las Vegas management Vault, though this was merely a bluff. With the help of a reactivated House, Cooper located Barb and Janey's cryo pods inside the Vault, but they were empty aside from the postcard, with the message "Colorado was a good idea," referencing something that Cooper had told his wife before he was arrested. Cooper took this as a sign that Barb and Janey were still alive and set out in the direction of Colorado to search for them. ==''Fallout'' TV series== ===Season 1=== ====[[The Head]]==== [[File:FOTV Barb Thomas episode 3.png|thumb|200px|Barb and Cooper]] Barb appears to Cooper after he is finished filming a movie scene. She tells him how much she enjoys lavender. She gives Cooper a Vault jumpsuit to advertise the Vaults and watches Cooper give a thumbs up. ====[[The Trap]]==== After Cooper is done filming a [[Vault 4]] ad, he kisses Barb, and she informs him about a wrap party at their house. [[File:FOTV Barb Thomas episode 6.png|thumb|left|In the hot tub]] While relaxing in their hot tub, she denies the idea of Cooper getting their family away from Vault-Tec and city life. She shows Cooper her [[Pip-Boy 3000 Mark V]] and claims she needs this job because it will ensure them a spot in a good Vault, and asks Cooper to trust her. While eating breakfast, Cooper and Barb debate a new rule stating that dogs will not be allowed in the Vaults. Cooper is ultimately worried about infringement of freedom. ====[[The Radio]]==== Barb comes inside to take her Pip-Boy. Although Cooper is initially reluctant, he decides to put Moldaver's listening device into Barb's Pip-Boy. ====[[The Beginning]]==== {{Quotation|text=A nuclear event would be a tragedy... but also an opportunity. Perhaps the greatest opportunity in history. Because when we are the only ones left, there will be no one left to fight. A true monopoly. [...] This is our chance to make war obsolete. Because in our current societal configuration, which took shape without intentional guidance, we have friction. We have conflict, and we have war. And war, well... War never changes.|source=Barb}} [[File:Vaultcountrymap.jpg|thumb|200px|At the Vault-Tec meeting]] Barb is dropped off by Cooper at the [[Vault-Tec headquarters (TV series)|Vault-Tec headquarters]] for work, entering alongside Bud Askins. Using the listening device, Cooper hears Barb having a meeting with [[Robert House]], [[Frederick Sinclair]], Bud Askins, [[Julia Masters]], and [[Leon Von Felden]]. Barb presents Vault-Tec's proposal to run [[Vault#True purpose|experiments]] on vault inhabitants, offering to give each of the companies represented by the meeting attendees several vaults to run their own experiments unchecked. In response to skepticism from House, Barb also suggests that Vault-Tec could drop the first nuke to guarantee results for their shareholders, horrifying Cooper. ===Season 2=== ====[[The Innovator]]==== On the day of the Vault-Tec meeting, after discovering Barb's involvement in Vault-Tec's plans, Cooper initially decides to flee Los Angeles with Janey and Roosevelt. However, he is convinced by Kate Williams to stay and join Barb on her upcoming trip to Las Vegas, where she will apparently meet Robert House to deliver the [[cold fusion]] technology to him in exchange for receiving the nuclear weapons that Vault-Tec will use to kickstart nuclear war. Barb soon returns home, and is seen collecting herself at the front door before heading further inside to face her family. She then walks into the kitchen and is greeted by Cooper, who also had to compose himself before welcoming his wife home. ====[[The Profligate]]==== Cooper hears Barb quietly sniffling and sobbing in their kitchen, where he finds her attempting to put items into a "Keepsake" capsule for when they have to go into a Vault. Despite his unease over Barb's involvement with Vault-Tec's secret plans, Cooper still tries to comfort his wife, remarking that there may not be a need to go into a Vault. He changes the subject and says he has to go to an event with his friend Charles Whiteknife; as soon as he is out of sight, Cooper turns back in thought, conflicted between his love for Barb and knowing who she really is. ====[[The Wrangler]]==== Cooper and Barb prepare for their flight at [[Los Angeles International Airport]], where they are met in the terminal by her assistant [[Hank MacLean]]. After Cooper points out the locked briefcase handcuffed to Hank's wrist, Barb sends Hank ahead. She waits nearby after Cooper excuses himself to use a payphone, in truth to have a final meeting with Kate Williams where he says he will recover the cold fusion diode without killing House. Upon landing in Las Vegas, Barb and Cooper are driven in a limousine to the [[Lucky 38]], where they observe anti-war and anti-corporate protesters outside. [[Diane Welch|Congresswoman Welch]] is dragged out of the Lucky 38 by MPs after protesting inside. She is thrown onto the steps of the casino, and Cooper helps her up, telling her to keep at it, after which Barb gets him to follow her into the casino. Inside, Barb excuses herself to go speak with RobCo reps while Cooper offers to get them some drinks. In truth, he begins following Hank to try and get at his briefcase, but is pulled away when Robert House himself summons him to the [[Lucky 38 penthouse]] for a private meeting via his [[Robert House's double|body double]]. During his meeting with House, Cooper is told the CEO's belief that it will not be Barb or anyone at the corporate meeting who will drop the bombs. However, he does believe that Barb and Cooper are more involved than originally thought. He reveals that he has been running mathematical equations according to various factors, all in an effort to predict the end of the world, and achieved the first conclusive results on the same day that Barb gave birth to their daughter Janey; this indicated to House that the Howard family would have an important role to play in future events. House adds that Cooper's decision to travel to Vegas with his wife in the present also had an influence, shortening the calculated timeframe of the war's start by a month, which further cemented this belief. Cooper leaves his meeting with House in emotional turmoil and tries to drown out his thoughts with alcohol, causing him to go on an alcoholic bender and make a spectacle of himself on the casino floor until Barb finds him and brings him to recover in their hotel room. As she nurses her hungover husband in their hotel room, Cooper wakes up and tells her they need to talk. ====[[The Other Player]]==== In a flashback set before the Vault-Tec meeting in "The Beginning," Barb is shown at work fielding several staff meetings, including a promotional campaign explicitly depicting nuclear explosions in Los Angeles; an R&D meeting with an [[Vault-Tec engineer|engineer]] who reveals that the Vaults' [[water chip]]s have a 30% fail rate that upper management wants to purposefully exploit; and a proposal by [[Bud Askins]] to create specialized freeway lanes for premium Vault-Tec customers. Another meeting is with Robert House (actually the double), wherein Barb learns that RobCo is licensing their [[brain-computer interface chip]] technology to Vault-Tec; in exchange, House is being given ownership of the [[Cold fusion|cold fusion diode]] for his own uses, a fact Barb was not privy to. She tries to ask what his plans are, but House slyly points out she will have to wait for the bombs to fall to find out. The meetings leave Barb increasingly uncomfortable and eventually bring her to tears at the thought of Vault-Tec's plans. Back to the relative present in the Lucky 38, Cooper starts their talk by reminiscing about the day he proposed to Barb at Catalina before revealing he knows about the plans she made with the corporate leaders at the Vault-Tec conference, stunning her silent. Barb tries to convince him of her side, but he denounces her complicity in a plan that would kill millions if not billions, including families just like theirs. However, Barb shoots back that Cooper would do the same if it meant protecting their daughter, to which Cooper does not respond. Barb tries to emphasize that there are people involved who are worse than her, but Cooper insults her belief that anyone could be worse than her in their situation, leaving Barb distraught. The scene returns to the Vault-Tec headquarters, right after Barb's meeting with Robert House's double. After House leaves, Barb tries to get her assistant [[Betty Pearson]] to find out everything she can about the cold fusion technology, and responds to Betty's concerns with a remark that none of what Vault-Tec is doing with House is a good idea. As she enters an elevator, she finds herself in an impromptu meeting with [[Siggi Wilzig]], whom she does not recognize. He informs her that any actions she takes against "the company" to stop the coming events will result in deadly consequences for her family, then gives her the exact words she would later use at the boardroom meeting where she advocated for Vault-Tec to directly instigate the apocalypse. Back in the Lucky 38 again, Barb has evidently told Cooper about her encounter with the mysterious man and what Cooper heard while spying on the meeting. Cooper still is convinced that they can do something to avert the plans to end the world, but Barb pleads with him not to, believing that there is nothing left they can do, and claiming that she had tried all of the options she had, which all failed. Cooper remains undeterred and leaves to do "something." That turns out to be getting Hank MacLean drunk. After bringing him back to their hotel room, Cooper pours a drink for them both, drugging Hank's drink with Barb's sleeping pills to break into the briefcase. Cooper discovers it is an extractor gun but is confused about what it is. When Barb returns to the room, she finds Cooper holding the extractor gun. She wordlessly takes it and removes the cold fusion diode implanted inside Hank's neck via the gun. She shows it to Cooper as he starts to understand more about what his wife has had to go through. ====[[The Handoff]]==== In their hotel room in the Lucky 38, after having acquired the cold fusion diode, Barb hides as Cooper arranges for a maid ([[Steph Harper]]) to take the passed-out Hank away to his own room. Barb reemerges after Steph leaves, and she shares a look with her husband. Later, Cooper meets with Representative Welch to try and negotiate a way to deliver the cold fusion diode to the government, though he purposefully omits his wife's agreement with his plans. He agrees to Welch's offer to arrange a meeting with the [[Last President of the United States|U.S. president]], to whom Cooper can personally hand the diode. Barb evidently also agrees with this, as she later accompanies Cooper on the streets of Las Vegas to the assigned meeting place, though she stays away as Cooper delivers the diode to the president. ====[[The Strip]]==== In a flashback at [[Camp McCarran|McCarran International Airport]], Cooper and Barb share drinks, satisfied at having seemingly averted Vault-Tec's conspiracy. They briefly discuss their next plans, with Barb now agreeing with Cooper's suggestion to go to Bakersfield and Cooper now suggesting Colorado instead. The two learn that Hank and Steph have gotten engaged before House calls Cooper with a warning that something is about to happen and a reminder that House had told Cooper that there are worse people than him in the world. Seeing [[U.S. federal agent|several men]] approaching and deducing that he is about to be arrested, Cooper orders Barb to let him take the fall for what happened while she denies any knowledge of it so as to protect Janey. After they kiss one final time, Barb tearfully watches as the men, federal agents, arrest her husband on the authority of the [[House Un-American Activities Committee]]. In the present, House's [[Artificial personality|AI backup]] helps the Ghoul find Barb and Janey's cryo pods in the [[Las Vegas management Vault]]. However, when House opens them, they are both empty. On the seat of Barb's pod is a Colorado postcard with a message reading "Colorado was a good idea," seemingly from Barb herself, referencing her husband's idea that they go there before he was arrested. With relief, the Ghoul tells House that for the first time in 200 years, he has a clue that his family may still be alive. The Ghoul heads for Colorado with [[CX404|Dogmeat]] in search of his wife and daughter. ==Personality== The initial interactions between Cooper and his wife show them both to be deeply in love with each other, to the extent that Cooper willingly starts a collaborative media campaign as Vault-Tec's spokesman solely for the sake of making Barb happy. However, Barb's dedication to working her way up the corporate ladder of Vault-Tec to get her family into a "good" Vault, and the compromises in personal freedoms he observes coming with that, strains Cooper's marriage to Barb. Once he is helped by Kate Williams to see that there are deeper, darker secrets to Barb and Vault-Tec, Cooper's trust in her fractures, ultimately breaking apart once he discovers via spying on her meeting with the corporate leaders that Barb planned to set the nuclear apocalypse in motion to keep Vault-Tec and its allies in power regardless of the immense death toll. However, it is only after finally having an honest talk with Barb and confronting her with what he overheard that Cooper discovers that what he originally thought was Barb's willingness to condemn humanity to its destruction was masking a great inner turmoil; Barb was not willingly making plans to start a nuclear war, but she felt she could not save her family from the threat posed by those holding her in their power, and was forced to cooperate, hoping that all of them could live through the end of the world together. Even once husband and wife finally understand all of this, Barb is desperate to stop Cooper from continuing in his plan to oppose the conspiracy and its creators, as she knows there is little, if anything, either of them can do against entities with far too much power and influence to be stopped. ==Notable quotes== * {{Inline quote|I'm doing what I can, okay? Okay, back to work.|Thaddeus, addressing the child laborers|"[[The Profligate]]"}} '''Thaddeus''' is a former aspirant of the [[Knights of San Fernando]] chapter of the [[Brotherhood of Steel]] and supporting character {{In|FOTV}}. Initially, he is a bully to his fellow Brotherhood member, [[Maximus]], but then becomes his companion after Maximus assumes [[Titus|Knight Titus']] identity. Eventually, Thaddeus starts transforming into some sort of mutant (he believes himself to be turning into a [[ghoul]], but the mutations he receives imply this is not the case) and is forced to flee the Brotherhood as a result. Fleeing to the Mojave Wasteland, Thaddeus ends up reencountering Maximus and the Brotherhood, and subsequently joins him on his journey to New Vegas. ==Background== Thaddeus was born in the Shithole, a rough side of the [[Los Angeles|Boneyard]]. He grew up on a fly farm; he worked as a "shitter," meaning he would be fed so that he would excrete often, with his feces used to feed the flies, which were then mulched up and sold as protein. Because of this, Thaddeus is self-admittedly somewhat fat.Thaddeus: ''"I've seen some things. I grew up working on a fly farm. I was a shitter, so they'd feed us, and then they'd feed our shit to the flies. Mulch 'em up and sell it as protein. Anyway, that's why I'm so fat."''
({{fotv|1|3}}) Beyond this, Thaddeus implies that his life in the Shithole was also rough, and that he was forced to engage in thievery, violence, and deception to survive. As a result, Thaddeus also does not believe that there are any truly "good" people, having never met any in his life.Thaddeus: ''"We definitely gotta sell it."''

And then we'll have the means to be one of those good people you're talking about. 'Cause I've seen a lot o' things. You know, like, crazy things. But 'good people'? No."''

({{FOTV|2|6}}) Thaddeus eventually joined the Knights of San Fernando, a Brotherhood chapter active in the region, and became an [[Initiates#Aspirant|aspirant]]. Among the aspirants, Thaddeus became known as a "consummate bully" who would get together with his friends to pick on others they saw as weak. Thaddeus' main target was Maximus, but this was not personal. Before Maximus came to the base, Thaddeus was the person being bullied by the other aspirants. When Maximus came, Thaddeus saw an opportunity to save himself by proposing that they all gang up on Maximus instead; it worked, and Thaddeus became popular within the Brotherhood ever since, seeing it as a sign of his own growth that he was now the bully and not the bullied. Privately, he still hoped that Maximus would also find someone to beat up eventually, which "only seem[ed] fair" to him.[[Maximus]] (as [[Titus|Knight Titus]]): ''"Say something about him."''
Thaddeus: ''"Well, he, uh, he was a good guy."''
Maximus: ''"Say something negative about him."''
Thaddeus: ''"Well, uh, he-he's dead. I don't know, it feels weird."''
Maximus: ''"An order, my squire."''
Thaddeus: ''"Okay. Uh, to be honest, me and the other guys used to be pretty hard on him. Like, regularly beat the shit out of him. It wasn’t personal, you know. It's just… well, you know, people at the base, they used to beat the shit out of me all the time. This shipment of new recruits came in, and, uh, one of them was Maximus. So I had this funny idea, what if we beat the shit out of that guy instead? And it worked. Yeah, I was really popular. It was great. I just wish he'd lived long enough to find someone else to beat up, you know? Only seems fair. I realize that, uh, people die all the time. It's the law of the Wasteland, so who cares, right? But still, uh, I feel bad."''
Maximus: ''"Don't feel bad. It's like you said, it's the law of the Wasteland. Let's go. We're losing daylight."''
({{fotv|1|3}}) Maximus was later made the squire to [[Titus|Knight Titus]] and sent into the [[Wilds]] on the manhunt for [[Enclave]] deserter [[Siggi Wilzig]]. Maximus was later reported dead to the Brotherhood, and Thaddeus was dispatched to replace him as Titus' squire, though neither he nor the Brotherhood knew that it was actually Titus who died, and that Maximus was impersonating him. The two of them managed to achieve the Brotherhood's mission by retrieving Wilzig's head and the [[Cold fusion|relic]] within; however, Maximus revealed himself to Thaddeus, and the deception caused Thaddeus to turn on him. Thaddeus' foot was mangled, though he managed to trap Maximus by removing his armor's [[Fusion core (TV series)|fusion core]] and flee with Wilzig's head. Unable to walk far with his injury, Thaddeus was able to heal himself by ingesting an [[elixir]] given to him by the [[snake oil salesman]] in exchange for the fusion core. He then went to the [[KPSS radio station]], where he arranged for pickup by the Brotherhood after reporting he had completed his mission. However, he was then confronted by Maximus and [[Lucy MacLean]] for Wilzig's head, and was then shot through the neck by a trap outside the radio station. The trap did not kill Thaddeus; though he did not know it at the time, the snake oil salesman's elixir had given him some additional side effects, making him nearly immune to pain and completely immune to radiation. He displayed abnormal endurance and regenerative properties, and his wound instantly healed. In addition to this, it is shown that he was beginning to [[Mutant|mutate]] into what Maximus believed was a ghoul. This forced Thaddeus to flee from the Brotherhood, though he gave Wilzig's head to Maximus before doing so. Later in 2296, having fled his old life, Thaddeus had taken up a job managing a [[bottle cap]] harvesting operation from a [[Sunset Sarsaparilla factory]], overseeing a group of [[factory children|child laborers]]. However, the factory was attacked by Maximus as well as [[Xander Harkness|Paladin Xander Harkness]], who attempted to kill Thaddeus and his child employees for being ghouls; Maximus killed the paladin to save them. Maximus convinced Thaddeus to disguise himself as Harkness and return to [[Area 51]] with him in order to prevent a war between the Knights of San Fernando and the [[Brotherhood of Steel (Fallout 4)|Commonwealth Brotherhood]]. However, the West Coast chapters at Area 51 ended up fighting each other, and Thaddeus fled with Maximus, who had been given the cold fusion diode by [[Dane (TV series)|Dane]]. The two of them soon encountered [[the Ghoul]], and Thaddeus decided to join them on their journey to [[New Vegas]] to rescue Lucy from the [[Las Vegas management Vault|management Vault]], which required fighting past [[Deathclaw (TV series)|deathclaws]] infesting the [[New Vegas Strip|Strip]]. Though Thaddeus intended to help them, he became unable to when his right arm fell off just outside the Strip, and the other two decided to go on without him. When Maximus was forced into the defensive to protect Freeside, Thaddeus chose to believe in Maximus even when the other [[Freesider]]s did not, stepping up to fulfill his intended role as a sniper despite his lost limb when no one else came to Maximus' aid. Thaddeus is under the impression that he is becoming a ghoul. However, his growing second mouth and sudden loss of an arm imply he is turning into a different type of mutant, though the exact type is not yet known. ==In the TV series== ===Season 1=== {{Quotation|An Initiate{{Ref|(Note)}} of the Brotherhood of Steel and a consummate bully, Thaddeus takes advantage of Maximus' perceived weakness and uses him as a means to build up his own confidence and perceived toughness.|[[Fallout season 1 Amazon overview|''Fallout'' Season 1 character description]]}} ====[[The End (episode)|The End]]==== Thaddeus is an aspirant of the Brotherhood of Steel alongside Maximus, whom he regularly beats up and bullies with his friends; he is first seen during one such occurrence, fleeing with [[Thaddeus' minion|his minions]] when a cleric spots them. He later celebrates when [[Dane (TV series)|Aspirant Dane]] is assigned to leave for [[the Wilds]] as [[Titus|Knight Titus]]' squire. Still, after Dane is mysteriously injured, he is annoyed at seeing that Maximus is reassigned as Titus' new squire. He later gives Maximus sketches of [[Siggi Wilzig]] and [[CX404]] before Maximus leaves on his mission with Knight Titus.{{FOTV|1|1}} ====[[The Head]]==== Maximus, who has assumed the deceased Knight Titus' identity, is contacted by the Brotherhood of Steel for a status report. To maintain his cover, he tells them his squire died, and Thaddeus is sent as a replacement squire. Maximus pretends to be Knight Titus and, after initially considering killing him, decides to keep Thaddeus as his squire. Under the guise of Knight Titus, Maximus initially bullies Thaddeus the same way Knight Titus bullies him and finds it amusing to bully his former bully. Thaddeus is eager to please "Knight Titus" and tries to be as helpful to him as much as possible. The pair find Wilzig's headless corpse, which they believe to be [[the Ghoul]]'s doing. Believing Wilzig's head to be a thing of value and in The Ghoul's possession, Thaddeus comes up with the idea to use a device to track The Ghoul's radiation. During their journey, Maximus presses Thaddeus to disclose his opinion of him, and Thaddeus reveals the reason why he bullied Maximus and that it wasn't personal. Although he realizes that "it's the law of the [[wasteland]]" and people die all the time, he feels bad that Maximus died before things could get better for him. Maximus tells Thaddeus not to feel bad, as he reiterates that "it's the law of the wasteland." They eventually arrive on [[Hollywood Boulevard]], where they are attacked by a [[Gulper (TV series)|gulper]]. Maximus rebukes Thaddeus for leading them to danger but orders him to run to safety while he personally deals with the gulper. While attempting to take the creature down, Maximus runs out of ammo from his pistol and is about to fight in close-quarter combat; Thaddeus aids him and shoots the gulper with a rifle. However, this alerts the gulper to Thaddeus' location, and he is chased down and dragged by the beast. The gulper nearly swallows Thaddeus, but Maximus comes to aid Thaddeus by grabbing him and pulling him out of the beast's mouth from the opposite side. The tug of war causes the gulper to vomit and die. While recovering from the situation, they find the target (Wilzig's head) to be among the things the gulper vomited and being licked by [[CX404]], who had been searching for Wilzig as well. They celebrate at the sight of this and prepare to return the head to the Brotherhood.{{fotv|1|3}} ====[[The Past]]==== [[File:The Past Maximus and Thaddeus.png|thumb|250px|Maximus and Thaddeus]] While sitting around a campfire celebrating their success, Thaddeus requests that Maximus, who he still thinks is Titus, brand him. After the branding, Maximus reveals his identity to Thaddeus. Since Thaddeus and Maximus grew close during their journey, Maximus hoped that Thaddeus would corroborate a made-up story that would help him avoid punishment from the Brotherhood. When Thaddeus asks Maximus what happened to Knight Titus, and he reveals that Titus is dead, Thaddeus tells Maximus that the Brotherhood will uncover his deceit and will kill him for it. Seeing that Thaddeus refuses to participate in his scheme, Maximus attacks Thaddeus and crushes his foot, but Thaddeus manages to remove the [[Fusion core (TV series)|fusion core]] from Maximus' [[T-60 power armor (TV series)|power armor]]. Thaddeus then steals Wilzig's head and escapes, leaving Maximus trapped in his armor to die alone.{{fotv|1|5}} Lucy later rescues Maximus, and they begin tracking Thaddeus to get the head from him. ====[[The Radio]]==== While traveling with Siggi Wilzig's head and an injured foot, Thaddeus stops at a [[Red Rocket (TV series)|Red Rocket]] to check on his foot. Seeing it mangled, he realizes that he will die without medical assistance. He decides to leave behind most of his squire equipment apart from a pistol and Wilzig's head. He also leaves CX404 inside a Nuka-Cola fridge to stop her from following him, but only after making sure she can still breathe in the fridge. He then begins looking for a radio tower to contact the Brotherhood for pickup, tracking [[Carl (TV series)|DJ Carl]]'s signal from the [[KPSS radio station]]. Thaddeus later encounters the [[snake oil salesman]] and trades him the fusion core from Maximus' power armor for a "[[elixir|serum]]" to heal his foot. He initially contemplates shooting the salesman and taking the serums for himself, but the salesman talks him out of it, saying he would not know which serums would harm him and which would not. The serum heals Thaddeus's foot, and once the process is complete, he asks the salesman if there is a radio tower nearby so that he may contact the [[Brotherhood base]]. He responds by telling Thaddeus that one is near the ruins of Shady Sands, which the soldier notes as being radioactive. Before slapping his shoulder and parting ways, the salesman says that Thaddeus will not have to worry about the radiation anymore.Thaddeus: ''"Do you know where I can find a radio tower? I have to make contact with my base."''
[[Snake oil salesman]]: ''"Yes, I believe there's one yonward. Past the big crater in the middle of the Shithole. It's near a town that used to be called Shady Sands."''
Thaddeus: ''"Shady Sands? That place is radioactive as hell."''
Snake oil salesman: ''"Well, you don't have to worry about that anymore, do you, buddy boy? Toodles and anon."''
({{fotv|1|7}}) Thaddeus eventually reaches the KPSS station and talks Carl into letting him borrow his radio tower to contact the Brotherhood, after which they talk about Carl's music for a while. Eventually, Lucy and Maximus arrive at the radio station, startling Thaddeus, who fires an entire magazine's worth of rounds at them but misses every shot. He then accidentally sets off a trap, lodging a [[crossbow (TV series)|crossbow]] bolt in his neck. Surprised that he hasn't died, Thaddeus takes out the crossbow bolt, only for his wound to be instantaneously healed. Maximus suspects that Thaddeus may be turning into a [[ghoul]], causing Thaddeus to be distressed, as the Brotherhood of Steel will surely kill him now. With the Brotherhood already en route to him, Maximus instructs Thaddeus to give him the head, and he will return to the Brotherhood to slow them down so Thaddeus can escape to safety. Thaddeus thanks Maximus and gives the two abrupt apologies and farewells.{{fotv|1|7}} ===Season 2=== {{Quotation|Once an Initiate{{Ref|(Note)}} of the Brotherhood of Steel and a bully with his sights set on Maximus, Thaddeus has since undergone some serious transformation (both figuratively and LITERALLY).|[[Fallout season 2 Amazon overview|''Fallout'' season 2 character description]]}} ====[[The Profligate]]==== Sometime after his escape from KPSS, the visibly mutated Thaddeus took control of an abandoned [[Sunset Sarsaparilla]] bottling factory close to [[New Vegas]], which he used as a shelter. The plant was also apparently housing an [[extremely broken Securitron]] that Thaddeus kept around for "security." He eventually decided to create a cap collecting operation; to maximize profit, he installed himself as floor manager and gathered a "crew" of orphaned human and ghoul children to man the conveyor belts bringing out crates of soda so they could pry off the caps while drinking the leftover soda for refreshment. The quiet living Thaddeus was enjoying was eventually upended when the bottling factory was stormed by Maximus and [[Xander Harkness]] from the Commonwealth Brotherhood after they detected the plant's power signature. They destroyed the Securitron and discovered the crew of children, which Xander wanted to eliminate the ghouls in accordance with the Codex. Thaddeus tried to intervene to protect them, but Xander's refusal to back down forced Maximus to kill him by driving a [[Super sledge (TV series)|super sledge]] into his head. As Xander's body collapses, Maximus reveals himself to Thaddeus and they quickly catch up, with Thaddeus still in shock from nearly dying. ====[[The Demon in the Snow]]==== Maximus tells Thaddeus he has to help him cover up Xander's death from the Brotherhood, just as a vertibird arrives, having tracked Xander and Maximus. Despite initial reluctance, claiming he prefers to run away, Thaddeus agrees to help after Max points out the Brotherhood would discover the kids in the process of looking for him, killing the ghouls and recruiting the humans, if they did not create a distraction. Thaddeus takes Maximus' suit of T-60 power armor and disguises himself as Xander Harkness as they are flown back to [[Area 51]]. His complete inexperience in using the armor and nervous comments are enough to fool [[Gnatius|Knight Gnatius]] and others, but it immediately tips off [[Dane (TV series)|Dane]] to Xander's death once they arrive back at Area 51. Max embarks on a plan to kill Quintus to prevent war with the Commonwealth, asking Dane to provide support; Thaddeus simply continues acting "as normal" as the paladin. Thaddeus fails to remain discreet, loudly vocalizing his nervous thoughts through his helmet while at the mess hall, which earns him glances from the confused Brotherhood members present. He decides that the risk of coming back to the Brotherhood is not worth it and tries to leave, but is met by [[McRae|Elder McRae]] of the [[Yosemite Brotherhood of Steel]], who asks for an audience with "Xander," which he is forced to agree to. McRae tries to convince "Xander" to put in a good word with [[Arthur Maxson|Elder Maxson]] after her chapter's involvement with [[Quintus]], but they are then interrupted by the [[Coronado elder]], who also tries to make a deal. In the tense situation, Thaddeus suffers a panic attack and is almost exposed when McRae offers to lift his visor to help him breathe until the [[Grand Canyon elder]] storms in, revealing the cold fusion relic was stolen and kick-starting an all-out war between the chapters. Thaddeus quickly removes himself from the situation. He finds Maximus and Dane after the former reneges on his plan to kill Quintus. The two separate from Dane and flee from the base with the cold fusion relic in Maximus' hands as the airship fleet opens fire on one another, with one crashing into the desert behind them. ====[[The Other Player]]==== The combat continues at Area 51. In the sand dunes some distance from the base, Thaddeus has exited the T-60 power armor he was wearing due to Maximus' warning that the Brotherhood has trackers in its power armor and would be able to find them if they kept it. Seeing Maximus observe the vial with the cold fusion diode, Thaddeus sits behind him, marveling at the "sacred remnant." However, Maximus is surprised when Thaddeus' first instinct is that they should sell the diode. Maximus shuts him down, but Thaddeus continues to try and persuade him as the two start walking further into the distance. Later at night, the two have walked out of the sand dunes and reached an area with dry brush and ramshackle buildings, where they have set up a campfire. When Maximus still refuses to sell the diode, saying they will give it to a "good person" instead, Thaddeus challenges Maximus by asking him to name a "good person." Maximus mentions Lucy, but Thaddeus scoffs at this, believing that Lucy's "goodness" was only possible because she lived in a Vault and thus had guaranteed safety and abundant resources, in his view. He believes that he would not have been forced to resort to violence to survive, or have become a ghoul, if he grew up in a Vault like Lucy had. His ultimate claim is that, if they sold the diode, they could achieve the means to become "good" like Lucy; otherwise, in Thaddeus' view, he has never seen a good person before in his life. Hearing this, Maximus asks Thaddeus where he came from, learning that Thaddeus was from the Shithole; Maximus responds that he was comparably "lucky" to have grown up in Shady Sands and remembers good people. However, Thaddeus sarcastically points out that Maximus was not much luckier than him. After some time, Thaddeus and Maximus have fallen asleep next to their campfire. Dogmeat approaches them, carrying [[the Ghoul]]'s hat in her mouth, she barks, jolting them awake. Dogmeat starts walking away, and Maximus and Thaddeus begin following her, having recognized her from before. They follow her to the [[Mojave Mission School]], where they discover the Ghoul lying wounded in one of the buildings. Maximus and the Ghoul curse in annoyance at finding each other there, while Thaddeus just awkwardly greets and waves hello. They stand there, looking over the Ghoul, as the episode ends. ====[[The Handoff]]==== Thaddeus, along with the Ghoul and Maximus, enter an [[run-down town|abandoned NCR town]]. Thaddeus attempts to talk with the Ghoul, trying to bond, as he is under the impression that he is becoming a ghoul just like the bounty hunter, but the Ghoul ignores him. When Maximus asks the Ghoul where they are going, the Ghoul tells them that they are going to [[New Vegas]] to save Lucy; however, Thaddeus points out that New Vegas is in an opposite direction from them. The Ghoul explains that they need equipment to get past the deathclaws on the New Vegas Strip. The Ghoul then turns and points his gun at Maximus, demanding he explain why he has the cold fusion diode. Thaddeus mostly stays out of their conversation, apart from urging caution at pointing out the obvious, that the Ghoul has a gun. [[File:FTV S2E7 Still 065.png|thumb|250px|Thaddeus growing a mouth on his body.]] The three enter a former NCR armory in the town. Thaddeus grabs a hunting rifle and again tries to talk to the Ghoul, even showing him that he is growing a second mouth. He asks the Ghoul if it is normal, but the Ghoul only looks at him, wide-eyed, and returns to equipping himself. Thaddeus, dejected from not getting any answers, asks if a scope is around. Thaddeus watches as Maximus subsequently gives up the cold fusion diode to the Ghoul in exchange for getting access to a suit of [[Ranger power armor|NCR Ranger power armor]]. Sometime later, the three arrive in [[Freeside]], approaching the [[New Vegas Strip]] gate to deal with the deathclaws. They are cheered on by the crowd of [[Freesider|Freeside residents]] around them at the sight of a figure wearing NCR-marked armor. Thaddeus expresses confusion at this, but is told by the Ghoul that it is due to their "brand recognition" of the NCR. Once they reach the gate to the Strip, Thaddeus is told to get into position as a sniper. However, his right arm falls off, leaving him unable to fulfill his role. Despite insisting he can still help, Maximus tells him to stay back, and the others go forward without him. ====[[The Strip]]==== Thaddeus and the other gathered Freesiders watch as Maximus is thrown back by the deathclaws. Seeing the deathclaws start to enter Freeside, Maximus tells Thaddeus and the other townspeople to get to safety, and Thaddeus tries to help hurry them along, before running into the Atomic Wrangler alongside [[Shotgun Jeff]], Dogmeat, and many other Freesiders. The Freesiders soon start betting on Maximus' survival, despite knowing that his loss would mean they all die. Aggravated that most of the Freesiders do not think Maximus will win, Thaddeus silences the crowd and instead bets 500 caps on Maximus' survival, spilling a large number of caps from inside his clothes which he reveals he had been carrying from when he "used to make money for a living" at the Sunset Sarsaparilla factory. As Maximus is worn down over time, Thaddeus grows concerned, and takes it upon himself to join the fight like he was supposed to despite the loss of his arm. By bracing his rifle with his foot, Thaddeus provides sniper support to Maximus, though he struggles to reload his rifle due to his condition. Thaddeus manages to kill one, but Maximus is soon forced to abandon his armor and face down a deathclaw while Thaddeus is stuck reloading. To both of their surprise, [[New California Republic|NCR]] forces arrive to join the battle, turning the tide against the deathclaws. ==Personality== Thaddeus is eager to please his superiors and can be friendly and loyal to people if it does not get him in trouble. However, like Maximus, he also has a strong sense of self-preservation, as expressed by the actions he admits having taken for survival in the Shithole; in his having targeted Maximus as a victim for bullying among the aspirants; and in how he left Maximus for dead after discovering he had been disguised as Titus, and intending to finish the mission for the Brotherhood himself. Thaddeus did not enjoy bullying Maximus; he did it only because he wanted to fit in with his peers and because he sought to escape being a bullying victim himself, believing this to be the "law of the wasteland." Thaddeus' experiences have made him cynical, believing that there are no truly good people in the wasteland, and that goodness is only possible for those who have lived in abundance and who thus had the means to "become" good. While initially loyal to the Brotherhood, he was not a fanatical believer in their ideals, as seen by his quick abandonment of his Brotherhood ties, alongside his rivalry with Maximus, upon discovering he may have become a ghoul. Understanding the Brotherhood's "shoot on sight" approach to mutants, he willingly hands over Siggi Wilzig's head and flees, having lost any hostility to Maximus, as there was no longer anything gained by continuing to oppose him. Despite his cynicism, Thaddeus still willingly endangered himself to try and protect the ghoul children working under him from being killed by Paladin Harkness. He did so despite having no means of escaping the situation if not for Maximus' intervention. Later on, after meeting the Ghoul, he seemed eager to get along with him as a "fellow ghoul" and showed some concern and confusion over how he was mutating. Upon losing an arm when preparing to fight against the deathclaws on the Strip, he seemed only slightly surprised, and insisted he could still fight, but was left behind. ==Appearances== Thaddeus appears only {{in|FOTV}}. {{FOTV appearances |1=101 |3=103 |5=105 |7=107 |11=203 |12=204 |14=206 |15=207 |16=208 }} ==Behind the scenes== {{Note|(Note)}} Though Thaddeus' descriptions on Amazon Prime Video for both [[Fallout season 1 Amazon overview|season 1]] and [[Fallout season 2 Amazon overview|season 2]] call him an "initiate" in the Brotherhood, this is not used anywhere else in the TV series (apart from a description for [[Dane (TV series)|Dane]] on the same website). Within the series, Thaddeus and all of the other trainees are only referred to as aspirants. ==Gallery== ===Season 1=== Fallout Season 1 Amazon Thaddeus.png|Profile image from Prime Video character description Thaddeus trailer.png|Thaddeus attacked by a gulper FOTV s1 ep7 Thaddeus concerned.jpg|Thaddeus checking on his foot injury at the [[Red Rocket (TV series)|Red Rocket]] Thaddeus Inhaling.png ===Season 2=== Fallout-S2-maximus-2048x1365.jpg|Promotional image for season 2 of Thaddeus with Maximus Fallout Season 2 Amazon Thaddeus.png|Profile image from Prime Video character description FOTV S2E3 The Profligate thumbnail Thaddeus.jpg|In "[[The Profligate]]" ==References== {{References}} '''Script''' {{References|group=Script}} {{Navbox characters FOTV}} [[Category:Fallout TV series human characters]] [[Category:Brotherhood of Steel characters]] [[ru:Таддеус]]

Event planner |education =Doctor of Event Planning |family = |TV actor =[[Rodrigo Luzzi]] }} Doctor '''Reg McPhee''' is a resident of [[Vault 33]] {{In|FOTV}}. ==Background== Reg is a native resident of Vault 33. Along with three others in the Vault, he is to some extent a product of inbreeding, though he claims to have personally "come out on the other side" in terms of self-doubts related to it.{{FOTV|2|1}} He holds a PhD in event planning from the Vault's education system and, by 2296, had become a member of the Vault's three-person governing council alongside [[Betty Pearson]] and [[Woody Thomas]], under overseer [[Hank MacLean]]. However, following the attack on the Vault by [[Vault 32 raider]]s that year, Hank was abducted, and a crisis erupted when the Vault's [[Water chip (TV series)|water chip]] broke. The governing council was disbanded, and Betty was elected overseer in Hank's absence, beating Reg and Woody. Though he remained in Vault 33 while others including Woody were sent to resettle Vault 32, he has since been left adrift, seeing himself as the only one left behind while everyone is "moving up in the world." He was subsequently convinced by Betty to start a club, which became a support group for products of inbreeding. ==''Fallout'' TV series== ===Season 1=== {{Quotation|A native resident of Vault 33, Reg sits on the Vault’s governing council. He cares for the Vault and its future, but his personal ambitions may supersede the needs of the community and betray his authenticity.|[[Fallout season 1 Amazon overview|''Fallout'' season 1 character description]]}} ====[[The End (episode)|The End]]==== [[File:FOTV S1 Amazon promo 16.jpg|thumb|250px|left|Reg on the Vault council with Betty and Woody.]] Reg, alongside his Vault 33 council associates Betty and Woody, listens to [[Lucy MacLean|Lucy]] give her speech request to be allowed to participate in the Triennial Trade with [[Vault 32]]. The council unanimously agrees to approve Lucy's marriage application. Sometime later, Reg is seen greeting the [[Vault 32 raider|Vault 32 dweller]]s and their new Overseer, [[Lee Moldaver]], who introduces Lucy's new husband, [[Monty (TV series)|Monty]], to her. After the wedding ceremony is held, he and Woody are seen setting up the podium for Overseer Hank, who gives a poignant speech about his daughter's marriage. The two then stand and watch as the [[Vault 33 dweller]]s dance with their Vault 32 counterparts. Soon after the wedding, the Vault 32 dwellers are revealed to be [[Vault 32 raider|raiders from the surface]]. Reg is not seen during the attack, but he is injured during the attack and is forced to wear a neckbrace in the aftermath. With Hank having been kidnapped by the raiders, Reg, Woody, and Betty hold an emergency assembly with the surviving Vault 33 dwellers in their authority as the governing council. During the assembly, Lucy proposes sending a search team to the surface to save her father. However, none of the council members agree; Reg asks Lucy if she intends to open the outer Vault door in seeming dismay, and Betty refuses on the grounds of preserving the Vault's security, to which both Reg and Woody agree. Lucy leaves, disconcerted, while Reg and the others continue the assembly. Lucy's brother [[Norm MacLean|Norm]] tells her that Reg and the other council members may have refused out of a desire to preserve their newfound authority. [[File:FoTV vault 33 anxious dwellers.jpg|thumb|250px|Reg and [[Davey (TV series)|Davey]] concerned about Lucy leaving the Vault]] Lucy soon forms a plan to look for her father on her own, with help from [[Chet (TV series)|Chet]] and Norm. When they open the exterior Vault door, and Lucy is about to exit, Reg and [[Davey (TV series)|Davey]] catch up with them. Reg tries to reason with Lucy to stop and not pass through the Vault door, but she does so regardless. Reg desperately moved to the console to close the Vault door but was too late to keep Lucy from leaving. ====[[The Head]]==== In the wake of Lucy's departure from Vault 33, Reg and the other two councilmembers hold disciplinary sessions to punish Chet and Norm, firing Chet from his role as gatekeeper. During Norm's session, Reg and Woody alternate, discussing Norm's involvement and the dangers of opening the Vault door. Reg also mentioned how the raiders could have only managed to enter Vault 32 because a "bonehead" allowed it. However, Betty seems to get the final say in Norm's punishment, and in response to a comment he makes, she reassigns him to deliver food to the surviving sixteen raiders, who have been imprisoned in the Vault. [[File:The Head meeting Betty Reg Woody.png|thumb|250px|Woody, Reg and Betty at the assembly]] Afterward, an assembly is held in the Vault to brainstorm what to do with the surviving raiders. After Woody announces their ethical dilemma, Reg chimes in, claiming that they have been given a prime opportunity to prove to the surface world the Vault's goal of repopulating and building a better world on the surface. Woody then notes that a collective decision has to be made about the Vault 32 raiders, with Reg commenting that the decision should fit the Vault's shared values. Betty suggests that they promote possible ideas; thanks to a "conversation" that Woody had with one of the raiders, Reg suggests that the Vault 33 dwellers rehabilitate the Vault 32 raiders to integrate them into their society. On the other hand, Woody notes that it's understood that the process may take years, but claims it is something they can accomplish if they put their minds to it. A few ideas are then proposed by some Vault 33 dwellers, including Davey and [[Marianne (TV series)|Marianne]]. Hearing the suggestions, Norm scoffs at the ideas, and when Reg asks him if he has something to say, he opines that it's not their obligation to help the raiders. This opinion is met with backlash, and Reg tries to reason with Norm, stating that they can't simply "let them go" because they have intimate knowledge of their Vault security. He then asks Norm what he suggests they do, and Norm answers that they should kill the raiders as retribution, although he takes back his comment following further disagreement. At that moment, the [[Vault 33 engineer]] appears and tries to privately talk with Reg and Woody. However, the two insist that they talk in public. The engineer insists that Overseer Hank would have done so privately, but Reg argues that it will be fine. As such, the engineer announces that Vault 33's [[Water chip (TV series)|water chip]] has been destroyed, leaving only two months of water reserves left for the Vault 33 residents to survive on. Before the engineer can finish, Reg cuts him off, and the meeting is adjourned. ====[[The Ghouls]]==== With Hank now gone, an election is set to be held for the Vault's new overseer. Woody, Reg, and Betty are all running in the election, and Woody and Reg are seen hanging up posters for their electoral campaign. Later, they meet outside a cell where a semi-sedated Vault 32 raider is being held for interrogation about his background and the kidnapping of Hank. As they continue talking, the semi-sedated Vault 32 raider regains consciousness and acts wildly and uncooperatively, thrashing about and not providing any answers. Woody decides to give up and try again the next day, moving to grab a [[Tranq gun (TV series)|tranq gun]]. Meanwhile, Reg watches the Vault 32 raider struggle to undo his restraints. ====[[The Past]]==== [[File:Vault 33 election.png|thumb|250px|Reg in the line to vote]] On the day of the election, Reg gets in line to vote and encounters Davey, who apologizes, first alluding to but then directly admitting that he will vote for Betty instead of Reg given the current water crisis and Betty's stated past experience as overseer. Reg expresses understands and doesn't hold it against Davey. Admitting to himself that he is unlikely to win, he also votes for Betty. Betty indeed wins the election in a landslide, with 98% of the vote. During the ceremony for Betty's victory, Woody and Reg are in the back, also clapping for Betty. Woody comments "better luck next time" to Reg, and he softly agrees. Soon after, Betty announces that she and the [[Bud Askins|Vault 31 overseer]] have formulated a plan to resettle Vault 32, which will involve transferring many of Vault 33's dwellers into the new Vault. Reg tours Vault 32 along with many other Vault 33 dwellers, unaware that its newly-cleaned facade hides the violence and death that had occurred in the Vault. ====[[The Radio]]==== While Norm is delivering food to the captive Vault 32 raiders, Reg's voice is heard over the PA system, announcing that Betty will be releasing the reassignment decisions for which dwellers will be sent to repopulate Vault 32. Not long after, the reassignment decisions for the Vault 33 dwellers are released by Betty. Reg is sitting on a toilet when he receives the decision, and is relieved to learn he will continue staying in Vault 33. However, Woody is set to be transferred. Before Woody leaves for Vault 32, Reg hugs him goodbye. ===Season 2=== {{Quotation|Before the raider attack, Reg was part of Vault 33's governing council. Now, with the council dissolved and everyone focusing on solving the water chip crisis, he finds himself without a purpose.|[[Fallout season 2 Amazon overview|''Fallout'' season 2 character description]]}} ====[[The Innovator]]==== [[File:FTV S2E1 Still 099.png|thumb|250px|left|Reg with his lollipop]] In [[Vault 33]], [[Betty Pearson]] discusses plans to repair the [[Water chip (TV series)|water chip]] with an [[Vault 33 engineer|engineer]]. Reg, licking a lollipop, comes in and asks if he can help, but he instead breaks a piece of technology. Betty hints that he should not interfere with important matters, suggesting, for example, that he create a support group. Reg takes her suggestion too seriously and organizes a support group for victims of inbreeding, which he himself is. [[File:FTV S2E1 Still 185.png|thumb|250px|Reg's support group sign]] Reg soon hosts the group's first meeting, attended by only three others: Marianne and a [[red-haired man]] and [[Red-haired woman|woman]]. As Reg leads the group in a chant about not needing to feel ashamed about their lineage, the red-haired duo smile at each other suggestively, which arouses Marianne's suspicion; Reg himself seems totally unaware. The red-haired duo then ask Reg if they plan to change the Vault's rules to allow inbreeding; Reg says no, clarifying that the "rules are good" and that he is only trying to help people accept themselves for being inbred. This causes the red-haired duo to leave. Marianne then asks Reg if her dust allergy could be due to her father's inbreeding; Reg professes not to know, as he never studied genetics. This causes Marianne to grab her plate of snacks and prepare to leave, but Reg hurriedly claims that it ''could'' be her father's fault to stop her from leaving. This causes Marianne to, after thanking Reg for the snacks that he prepared for the group, start talking in depth about her convoluted inbred family lineage. Reg sits and listens, seeming satisfied but still conflicted. ====[[The Demon in the Snow]]==== As Reg's inbreeding support group grows in number, he leaves to refill two water jugs. He runs into Betty, who chastises him for wasting rations during the water crisis. Unfazed, Reg defends himself by pointing out that Betty signed off on his food and beverage budget. He adds that his group is growing in numbers weekly, to the point that he claims they are a distinct subculture, while Betty's own popularity has dwindled. After Betty derides Reg's group as merely a "snack club," Reg snaps that he will not let her take his position away from him. Meekly apologizing for his outburst, he then continues on his way. ====[[The Other Player]]==== Reg's group has grown even more popular, to the point of having a long waiting line and enforcing stricter standards for who is considered inbred. However, Reg himself remains unpopular, with most of the dwellers seemingly only sticking around because of his free food. Reg is seen making small talk with a visibly disinterested dweller who walks away mid-conversation. Though this leaves Reg deflated, he seems to get some satisfaction seeing all of the group's attendees eating and talking among themselves. Reg decides to play the piano, preparing as though he is about to launch into a masterpiece. In the following sequence, Reg seems to perform a full rendition of "[[Uranium Fever (song)|Uranium Fever]]," which leads to the entire group dancing around the snack table and reacting positively to Reg's performance. However, it quickly becomes apparent that this is just a daydream that Reg had, and he actually only played a simple melody of "Mary Had a Little Lamb." Once he finishes, he looks up expectantly, but finds that no one was interested. Just then, [[Vault 33 guard]]s barge into the room, announcing that Betty has ordered for the support group to be dissolved and its snack budget rescinded. Reg takes charge, telling the guard that he wants to talk to Betty, and taking an indignant stance once she arrives. Betty reveals that Reg has been avoiding her attempts to meet and discuss the situation; Reg claims to accept the dissolution of the support group, but refuses to let her take away the snack budget, refusing her subsequent demand to talk privately in her office. Betty points out that Reg is offering salty snacks, which will exacerbate Vault 33's water crisis; however, Reg claims to be "giving the people what they want," and the attendees back this up. He refutes Betty's point that the group should not get extra rations just because of their heritage, stating that they, in fact, do deserve this given that they are only in the Vault to begin with because of their ancestry. He sees the selfishness of his ancestors as a net positive and claims not to be ashamed of it anymore. Betty claims to sympathize, but Reg says that she never could due to her being "different" (having come from Vault 31). Betty tries to regain control by hearkening back to a past crisis, the Weevil Famine, but Reg loudly interrupts her, stating that the 33ers are sick of hearing about the famine; the attendees express agreement. In one final act of defiance, Reg grabs a handful of a jello mold and messily shoves it into his mouth, to the cheers and applause of his group's attendees. ==Personality== [[File:Reg's assignment.png|thumb|250px|Reg relieved about staying in Vault 33]] Reg portrays himself as idealistic and moralistic, perhaps to a fault. This is illustrated when Reg proposes that Vault 33 can reform the Vault 32 raiders into well-mannered people and assimilate them into Vault 33's society, even though the raiders have recently attacked Vault 33's people and have been disrespectful ever since. However, Reg firmly believes that the raiders would want to adopt Vault 33's civilized values and that the vault dwellers are responsible for reforming them. Reg is also very arrogant in his leadership capabilities, even though it backfires on him. When an engineer advises him to keep an important issue private, Reg insists on discussing the matter publicly in front of an assembly, which leads to the engineer revealing the Vault's impending water crisis; Reg, in a panic, tries to cover up his mistake by interrupting the engineer. Reg vies with his peer, Woody, for relevance in the governing council, and even competes with his other peer, Betty, for the position of overseer. However, he knows that Betty's reputation as an experienced and more competent leader will overshadow him; ultimately, even he votes for her. Reg desperately clings to the status and prestige he has cultivated in Vault 33 and is relieved that he wasn't one of the residents reassigned to Vault 32. Despite this, he perceived himself as having stagnated after Betty became overseer, Woody was sent to Vault 32, and Norm was also sent to Vault 31 for a "leadership exchange program" (a lie by Betty), and professed to feel shame at this -- though not uselessness. His own ego was soon exacerbated after he formed the Products of In-Breeding Support Group, leading him to completely neglect the water crisis as he carelessly supplied its members with extra rations, eventually growing to the point where he became openly defiant towards Betty's authority. ==Appearances== Reg McPhee appears {{in|FOTV}}. {{FOTV appearances |1=101 |3=103 |4=104 |5=105 |7=107 |9=201 |12=204 |14=206 }} ==Gallery== Fallout Season 1 Amazon Reg.png|Profile image from Prime Video character overview (S1) Fallout Season 2 Amazon Reg.png|Profile image from Prime Video character overview (S2) ==References== {{References}} '''Script''' {{References|group=Script}} {{Navbox characters FOTV}} [[Category:Fallout TV series human characters]] [[Category:Vault 33 characters]] [[ru:Редж Макфи]]
