If your father were here, he'd... he'd do the right thing.|Steph to Norm MacLean|sound=Steph Harper.ogg}} '''Stephanie "Steph" Harper''' is a resident of [[Vault 33]] {{In|FOTV}} and former pre-War [[Vault-Tec Corporation|Vault-Tec]] employee from [[Vault 31]]. She later is appointed [[overseer]] of [[Vault 32]]. ==Background== Born on February 15, 2045, Steph was a citizen of [[Canada]] and was raised Catholic by her mother, [[Joan (TV series)|Joan]]. During the [[United States annexation of Canada|annexation of Canada]] by the [[United States of America]] in the 2070s, Steph and her mother were still living in Canada; Steph was issued a provisional U.S. citizenship card on September 1, 2071, listing her as a resident of the annexed territory of Canada.{{FOTV|2|4}}: See [[:File:StephHarperID.png|this image of her ID]] (timestamp ~39:33). The issuance date can be seen more clearly in "[[The Handoff]]" at timestamp ~36:27. [[File:FoTV Steph border guard.jpg|thumb|250px|right|Steph at the Canadian border before the Great War.]] Whether concurrently or later, Steph and her mother were interned at the [[Uranium City Internment Camp]]. They eventually escaped together with other imprisoned Canadians; however, they were cornered by a [[United States Marine Corps|U.S. Marine]] in power armor. A [[Canadian rebel]] rushed the Marine with an explosive, killing the Marine and injuring Steph's mother, but leaving Steph unharmed. Joan urged Steph to leave for the border and survive through any means necessary, including killing Americans, whom Joan said should be dehumanized. Steph crossed the border, killing a [[Slit throat victim|civilian man]] for his food, as well as killing a [[border agent]] in order to cross a border checkpoint into the U.S. She eventually made her way to [[Las Vegas]], [[Nevada]], where she became a maid for the [[Lucky 38]].{{FOTV|2|7}} One night while working at the Lucky 38 in 2077, Steph was called upon to escort a drunken [[Hank MacLean]] out of [[Cooper Howard]]'s hotel room. Knowing that Cooper was the face of Vault-Tec at the time, Steph asked him how to acquire a spot in the [[Vault]]s; Cooper told her to ask Hank. That night, Steph ingratiated herself to and seduced Hank MacLean until he proposed to her at 4 a.m. The two were eventually married. Hank got Steph into [[Bud Askins]]' executive assistant training-slash-Vault experiment program [[Bud's Buds]]; he may have done so without Bud's knowledge, as Bud was seemingly confused about Steph's presence in Vault 31 over the years.''[[Fallout: Join Brain On A Roomba Inside Vault 31]]'' Steph was aware of her husband's secret ties to and work for the [[Enclave]], though it is unclear to what degree she herself was involved.{{FOTV|2|8}} During her time at Vault-Tec, Steph's demeanor would often frighten her coworkers, including [[Betty Pearson]]. As a Vault-Tec employee and member of Bud's Buds, Steph was placed into [[cryonics|cryostasis]] in [[Vault 31]]; the program involved the [[Vault 31 dweller]]s being periodically thawed out and transferred to the connected [[Vault 32|Vaults 32]] or [[Vault 33|33]] to manage their dwellers and participate in controlled breeding (eugenics) under Askins' supervision.[[Norm MacLean]]: ''"Is this where my dad's from?"''
[[Bud Askins]]: ''"You'll never find out. Oh. He's gonna find out. These are Bud's Buds. My Buds. America outsourced the survival of this country to the private sector. But it would have been insane to keep a failed nation alive. So, we kept Vault-Tec alive instead. A well-trained staff of highly supervised junior executives from my own assistant training program. Because the future of humanity comes down to one word: Management."''
({{FOTV|1|8}}) [[File:FOTV Official Trailer Still 051.png|thumb|250px|left|Steph with her best friend [[Lucy MacLean]]]] Reactivated sometime in or before 2294, Stephanie was transferred to [[Vault 33]]. By the time that Steph was awakened, Hank had been awake for decades; he had remarried, and had a family with, a woman named [[Rose MacLean|Rose]] despite him and Steph still being married. Steph eventually married Vault 33 dweller [[Bert (TV series)|Bert]] on March 17, [[Timeline#2294|2294]].{{fotv|1|1}} She is fond of Bert, though her memory of their wedding night is spoiled by Bert's lack of stamina in bed.[[Lucy MacLean]]: ''"Hmm. Feels a little tight."''
Steph Harper: ''"Won't be for long. On my wedding night, that dress got off almost as fast as Burt{{sic}} did."''
({{FOTV|1|1}}) Regardless, she developed feelings for him (perhaps spurred by his love of shoe maintenance),Steph Harper: ''"He took great care of his shoes. You know, it was one of the few things he truly loved. Get him talking about shoe maintenance, and... he'd just carry on until everyone left the room. I loved him so much. And those monsters took him away from me."''
({{FOTV|1|4}}) and by 2296, they were expecting their first child. Steph kept active during her pregnancy, participating in the Young Pipefitter's Association and keeping on top of her regular Vault duties. By 2296, Stephanie had also become best friends with Hank's daughter [[Lucy MacLean|Lucy]] -- who was technically her stepdaughter -- even though Steph was closer in age to Lucy than to her first husband by this point. The two hoped to raise their children together once Lucy was married to a dweller from [[Vault 32]] during the Triennial Trade in 2296. {{clear}} ==''Fallout'' TV series== ===Season 1=== {{Quotation|A resident of Vault 33, Steph is Lucy’s best friend. She and her husband, Bert, were married in 2294. They are currently expecting their first child, but that doesn’t stop Steph from taking part in the Young Pipefitter’s Association or any of her other Vault duties.|[[Fallout season 1 Amazon overview|''Fallout'' season 1 character description]]}} ====[[The End (episode)|The End]]==== [[File:FOTV S01E01.The.End. (5).jpg|thumb|250px|left|Steph and Bert during Lucy's wedding]] Steph helps [[Lucy MacLean]] get ready for her wedding and shows Lucy where everyone writes their names and the date of their marriage. She and Lucy discuss the upcoming marriage, and Steph expresses excitement about raising their future children. Steph and other vault dwellers accompany Lucy and Hank to the connecting entrance between Vault 33 and 32, where Lucy and [[Monty (TV series)|Monty]] first meet. [[File:FoTV Sterling Mk IV The End Steph.jpg|thumb|250px|Steph firing an SMG at the raiders]] During the raid on Vault 33, Steph's husband Bert is killed in the cornfield. Steph cradles Bert's corpse before flying into a rage at the nearest raider. She is stabbed in the right eye with a fork during that fight, but she then uses a submachine gun to kill the raider who stabbed her before firing at several others. However, she is later captured by [[Lee Moldaver]]'s men, along with [[Chet (TV series)|Chet]] and several other vault dwellers, and are held hostage when Hank and then Lucy confront them at the entrance to Vault 32. She escapes from the situation along with everyone else after Moldaver leaves with [[Hank MacLean]] and detonates a bomb at the connecting entrance between Vault 33 and 32. ====[[The Head]]==== After the Vault decides what to do about the raiders, Steph tells Norm she agrees with his proposal to execute the raiders, as she is still vengeful over Bert's death. ====[[The Ghouls]]==== [[File:FOTV_The_Ghouls_Chet_and_Steph.png|thumb|240px|Chet and Steph kiss]] Steph is shown to have recovered from the fork in her eye, with an eyepatch over her wound. She turns to [[Chet (TV series)|Chet]] for comfort after the death of her husband Bert. She goes to his apartment, gives him Bert's clothes, makes him try them on, and starts kissing him before her water breaks and she goes into labor.{{FOTV|1|4}} ====[[The Past]]==== Norm asks how Vault 31 is different. Steph replies, "What did your dad tell you?" which hints that she does not want to say anything to contradict Hank's claims. Steph claims she does not know, but says the mashed potatoes were better. ====[[The Radio]]==== Steph, while she is recovering from having given birth in Chet's unit, is pinged on her Pip-Boy while applying ice she that she will be reassigned to Vault 32 in a starter home unit with Chet and her baby. Norm visits Chet's unit after the assignment announcements only to be greeted by Steph. She talks about the poisoned raiders and how terrible their deaths were, but Norm does not respond. Steph excuses herself to care for her baby but for Chet to not take too long. After sometime, Steph begins calling to Chet to finish the conversation. Before they leave, [[Betty Pearson]] announces that Steph has been granted the position of overseer of Vault 32. {{clear}} ===Season 2=== {{Quotation|Now the Overseer for Vault 32 after the post-raider attack reassignments, Steph continues to prove she knows how to get things done. She may now be a mother, but she's not going to let something as trivial as motherhood get in the way of her responsibilities as Overseer.|[[Fallout season 2 Amazon overview|''Fallout'' season 2 character description]]}} ====[[The Innovator]]==== In Vault 32, Stephanie is still settling into her new office and new role as overseer. She is seen trying to figure out her terminal while [[Davey (TV series)|Davey]] pesters her about being confused with Vault 32's layout. Exasperated, Steph asks what Davey wants her to do, and he eventually settles on asking her to commission a feasibility study for new signage before leaving. Chet soon enters with Steph's child, asking if she will assign him a role. Steph refuses, delegating childcare responsibilities to him, though he protests that the child is not his and he is not married to her. Disgruntled, but in a measured manner, Chet points out his situation and specifically mentions that the child still doesn't have a name, mentioning that their neighbors now call the child Chet Jr. Steph, peeling and ripping apart an [[orange]] with a hunting knife, accepts the name without a second thought, but Chet tries to protest, saying that the name Chet Jr. evokes unpleasant associations with his father's death during the Vault 33 famine of 2277. Steph suddenly stabs the knife into her desk, making it clear that she's not in the mood for an argument, and Chet reluctantly agrees to the name Chet Jr. Finally, Steph asks if Chet knows how to use computers, but he says that's [[Norm MacLean|Norm]]'s specialty. Stephanie decides to send a message to Vault 31, but finds that inter-Vault communications are unavailable (soon revealed to be the result of sabotage by Norm in Vault 31). ====[[The Demon in the Snow]]==== [[File:StephHarperID.png|thumb|333x333px|Chet finding Steph's pre-war ID card]] In the inter-Vault space, Steph meets with Betty, who investigated Vault 31 following the loss of communications. Betty informs her of Bud Askins' death and the seeming abandonment of Vault 31, with Norm being nowhere in sight. While initially surprised, Steph quickly comes to view this as an opportunity to consolidate her own leadership. When Betty asks Steph to have Vault 32 send some of its water supplies to Vault 33, Steph refuses, citing the needs of her Vault and her own child. She also rebuffs Betty's point that she should be more cooperative since Betty appointed her, hinting that she has lived through much worse circumstances than Betty had in the past. In the end, she agrees to consider trading water to Vault 33 if Betty agrees to bring her Hank MacLean's pre-War keepsake box. After being told that there won't be a Vault 33 if she doesn't help, she flips Betty's previous argument and tells her that the "experiment is over" and that they have to make their own decisions since [[Vault-Tec Corporation|Vault-Tec]] won't be here to save them. Unbeknownst to either overseer, the end of their conversation was overheard by [[Woody Thomas]]. Following the Vault's guidelines to the letter, Woody meets Steph in her own apartment to report her own violation of the Vault-Tec handbook's policies (her meeting in the inter-Vault space), while Chet listens in from nearby as he folds laundry. Steph thanks Woody and claims she will "escalate" a report to investigate herself, and when Woody protests, she reinforces her authority by telling him to call her Overseer Harper. At the same time, Chet finds a secret compartment in one of Steph's drawers which contains her wallet; Chet opens it to find a pre-War U.S. temporary ID card, revealing to him that Steph is both from the pre-War world and Canadian. Steph shuts down the discussion, and Chet puts her ID back while Woody heads for the door. Chet and Woody briefly make small talk, while Steph considers the situation with a troubled look. She then forces her way between Chet and Woody to open the door and make Woody leave. Naively, Woody further asks Steph about the experiment that she mentioned to Betty, which she downplays as "overseer stuff." When the door closes, she glares at Chet, who gives her a strained smile; Steph smiles in return. ====[[The Handoff]]==== Steph's history is revealed as she and [[Joan (TV series)|her mother]] escape from the [[Uranium City Internment Camp]] in Canada. They and other Canadian prisoners are chased and fire upon, before they are cornered by a [[Vertibird (TV series)|Vertibird]] and a U.S. Marine in [[T-45 power armor (TV series)|T-45 power armor]], who threatens to shoot them if they do not return to the camp. A [[Canadian rebel|suicide bomber]] kills the soldier, although Steph's mother is mortally wounded in the explosion. She tells Steph to go south and survive by any means necessary. Including forgetting her Catholic upbringing and to kill if needed, by not thinking of them as human beings, but Americans. Steph is distraught, but manages to escape. She is seen killing a [[Slit throat victim|man]] for a can of [[Pork n' Beans]] before later crossing the border into the United States after killing a [[border agent]] who catcalled her and asked to see her passport. In a later pre-War scene in the Lucky 38, [[Cooper Howard]] is seen talking with a Lucky 38 maid about dealing with Hank MacLean, who is passed out after having been drugged by Cooper in the previous episode. Cooper gives the maid a generous tip before it is revealed that the maid is Steph, who asks Cooper about how to get into a Vault after recognizing him from Vault-Tec advertisements. Cooper tries to talk her out of trying to get into a Vault due to his distrust of Vault-Tec, but she dismisses his concerns. Defeated, Cooper tells her to ask Hank. In 2296, Chet asks Steph about the wedding between the two she has organized without his knowledge. She is short with him, telling him she is working. After Chet discovers Woody's glasses in the garbage disposal, he asks about Woody, to which Steph frustratedly claims Woody was sent to Vault 31 for a "leadership exchange program" (the same excuse previously used by Betty to cover up Norm's disappearance from Vault 33). Chet destroys the glasses shortly after, hiding his discovery. Betty finally decides to give Hank's keepsake box from Vault 33 to Steph, in return for Vault 32's water to save Vault 33. During the handover, Betty hides and reveals herself after Steph has approached the box in anticipation, congratulating her on the wedding. Steph asks if Betty has spies in Vault 32, which Betty confirms. As Steph leaves, Betty tells her she wants nothing to do with whatever Steph has planned, and that she just wants for everyone in Vault 33 to live peacefully. As Steph leaves with the box, she tells her that their deal was for the water alone. During the wedding of Steph and Chet, Chet refuses to say "I do," to Steph's surprise. Instead, he reveals to the assembled audience of dwellers that he believes that Steph killed Woody, though she pointedly warns him not to. When Davey asks for proof, Chet is unable to produce Woody's glasses due to having destroyed them, so he continues the wedding, with Steph seemingly satisfied by Chet's failure. However, Chet then reveals Steph's pre-War U.S. citizenship card which proves she is both a pre-War citizen and a Canadian, which shocks the dwellers. This triggers a flight response in Steph, seemingly bringing back her memories of escaping from the internment camp, and she runs to lock herself inside the overseer's office. Chet and the other dwellers gather outside soon after, banging on the door and demanding answers, and Steph buries her head in her hands in stress. ====[[The Strip]]==== In a flashback at [[Camp McCarran|McCarran International Airport]] in 2077, Hank and Steph announce their engagement to a stunned [[Cooper Howard|Cooper]] and [[Barb Howard]], with Hank telling them he proposed on their first meeting, which was just the previous night in the Lucky 38. Hank expresses hope that he can get Steph into [[Bud Askins]]' [[Bud's Buds|program]]. In 2296, Steph is still inside her office in Vault 32. As the Vault 32 dwellers bang on the door with chants of "death to management," Steph opens Hank's keepsake box and dons an [[Enclave]] [[Pip-Boy]] contained within. Identifying herself as Hank's wife, Steph sends a message to the Enclave to initiate Phase 2. Before apparently wiping his own memory, Hank mentions that he had hoped to see Steph again in a manner suggesting that he still has feelings for her and recalls their time together fondly despite decades having passed for Hank. ==Personality== Steph is initially shown to be a typically upbeat woman who cares about Lucy and is excited about them raising their children together. When Bert dies, she seems to fall into grief and appears to use Chet to cope with Bert's passing. However, she is later shown to be somewhat cold after being assigned overseer of [[Vault 32]], not giving any thought to even naming her newborn child, using Chet simply for childcare, and forcefully shutting down any attempts by him to protest. She is also shown to be highly vengeful and calculating, wishing death on the raiders who killed Bert. After the raiders are mysteriously killed because someone slipped rat poison into their food, Steph is not concerned at all about the occurrence. The actual culprit behind the raiders' deaths is not revealed. When Vault 33 begins to run out of water, she attempts to use it for her own gain, effectively holding the Vault hostage unless she is provided with Hank MacLean's keepsake box. Steph is seductive, as she managed to get Hank to propose to her after just hours of "talking." Chet also falls for her very quickly. Her primary goal is to survive, no matter what she has to do. This comes from having grown up before the annexation of Canada and lived in a internment camp, as well as her mother's dying words to her, who told her to do anything to survive, even if it means killing others, and to not consider Americans as humans, but rather as tools. Steph is willing to use any means necessary for this goal. For this reason is that she is cold and distant with Chet despite being apparently a couple, disregarding any opinion he has to the point Chet is unable to even speak up against her and completely neglects her own child, being somewhat apathetic, and does not care for the lives of the people at Vault 32, killing Woody with no remorse at all. ==Notable quotes== * {{Inline quote|Cod ham cheese and rice!|Expressing frustration at a terminal|sound=Steph Harper Codham cheese and rice.ogg|"[[The Innovator]]"}} ==Appearances== Steph Harper appears {{in|FOTV}}. She also appears in the ''[[Fallout 2d20: NPC Pack - Hollywood Heroes]]'' expansion pack for ''[[Fallout: The Roleplaying Game]]''. {{FOTV appearances |1=101 |3=103 |4=104 |5=105 |7=107 |9=201 |12=204 |15=207 |16=208 }} ==Behind the scenes== Steph was originally described as a "native resident of Vault 33" in her character description on the [[Fallout season 1 Amazon overview|Prime Video site for ''Fallout'' season 1]]. This was corrected sometime not long after the first season's release. In [https://fallout-s2.amazonstudios.com/?ref_=atv_dp_exp_4968_hb_0_link "The World of Fallout" interactive extras], a behind-the-scenes photo of Lucy's wedding dress shows the date of Steph's wedding to be 2297 instead of 2294, as seen in the [[The End (episode)|"The End" episode]]. ==Gallery== ===Season 1=== Fallout Season 1 Amazon Steph.png|Profile image from Prime Video character overview FOTV Amazon Profile Picture Steph.png|Prime Video profile image FoTV Lucy marriage.jpg|Steph sitting beside Lucy Moldaver's elite guard Vault 33.png|Steph held hostage by Moldaver's raiders Steph trailer.png|Steph with eyepatch and bandages FOTV S1 Amazon promo 12.jpg|Steph, eyepatch and no bandages Steph with child.png|Steph with her child [[Chet Jr.]] Steph in bathrobe.png|"Maybe the mashed potatoes were better?" ===Season 2=== Fallout Season 2 Amazon Steph.png|Profile image from Prime Video character overview FalloutS2TBimage7_Steph Harper.jpg|Prime promotional image FTV S2E4 Still 172.png|Steph meeting with Betty FOTV S2E7 Steph episode banner.png|Steph in the overseer's office FTV S2E7 Still 007.png|Steph in her bathroom FTV S2E7 Still 009.png|Steph escaping to America FTV S2E7 Still 013.png|Steph escaping to America Steph Harper in Lucky 38.png|Steph as a maid in pre-War [[Lucky 38]] FTV S2E7 Still 149.png|Steph being married to Chet FTV S2E7 Still 147.png|Steph pressures Chet to go along with the marriage FTV S2E7 Still 154.png|Chet reveals Steph is Canadian and over 200 years old FTV S2E7 Still 157.png|Steph hiding in her office before sending a message to the Enclave ==References== {{References}} '''Supplementary''' {{References|group="Supplement"}} {{Navbox characters FOTV}} {{Navbox overseers}} [[Category:Fallout TV series human characters]] [[Category:Vault 32 characters]] [[Category:Vault 33 characters]] [[Category:Vault-Tec characters]] [[Category:Overseers]] [[category:Fallout: The Roleplaying Game characters]] [[ru:Стеф Харпер]] [[zh:斯蒂芬妮·哈珀]]

{{Infobox character |games =FOTV, FORPG |image =FOTV Woody Thomas.png |race =[[Human]] |gender =Male |affiliation =[[Vault 32]]
[[Vault 33]] (formerly) |role =Vault 33 governing council (formerly) |age =40s{{inline quote|Lucy is in the COUNCIL ROOM sitting before the High Council, who sit at a table. BETTY (70), WOODY, and REG (both 40s) are three sweet-faced people equipped with small chalkboards, on which they make notes.|[[The End script|"The End" script]], p. 10}} |age verified=Yes |status =Deceased (presumed) |dod =July [[Timeline#2296|2296]] |dod verified=yes |family = |TV actor =[[Zach Cherry]] |special ={{SPECIAL|5,5,5,5,5,5,6}} {{Icon|FORPG}} |tag skills =Medicine 2{{dot}} Science 3{{dot}} Speech 3 {{Icon|FORPG}} |level =1 {{Icon|FORPG}} }} '''Woody Thomas''' is a resident of [[Vault 33]] who is later moved to [[Vault 32]] {{In|FOTV}}. ==Background== Woody is a native resident of Vault 33. By 2296, he had become a member of the the Vault's three-person governing council alongside [[Betty Pearson]] and [[Reg McPhee]], under [[Hank MacLean|Overseer Hank MacLean]]. However, following the attack on the Vault by [[Vault 32 raider]]s that year, Hank was abducted, and a crisis erupted when the Vault's [[Water chip (TV series)|water chip]] broke. The governing council was disbanded, and Betty was elected overseer in Hank's absence, beating Reg and Woody. Woody was subsequently reassigned as part of the group sent to resettle [[Vault 32]], and was coerced into joining the group despite his initial objections. In Vault 32, Woody inadvertently discovered some of the [[Three Vaults]]' secrets when he overheard a conversation between Betty and Vault 32's new overseer, [[Steph Harper]], though he immediately tipped Steph off to the fact that he knew too much when he naively reported Steph's misbehavior to Steph herself. Woody went missing afterwards; it is implied that he was killed by Steph to ensure his silence, with Steph covering up his absence as him having been transferred to Vault 31 for a "leadership exchange program." ==''Fallout'' TV series== ===Season 1=== {{Quotation|Woody is a native resident of Vault 33, and a member of the Vault’s governing council. While Woody cares deeply for the Vault, his lack of experience and naïveté hold him back from being taken more seriously among his peers.|[[Fallout season 1 Amazon overview|''Fallout'' season 1 character description]]}} ====[[The End (episode)|The End]]==== [[File:FOTV S1 Amazon promo 16.jpg|thumb|250px|left|Woody on the Vault council with Betty and Reg.]] Woody, alongside his Vault 33 council associates Betty and Reg, listens to [[Lucy MacLean|Lucy]] give her speech request to be allowed to participate in the Triennial Trade with [[Vault 32]]. The council unanimously agrees to approve Lucy's marriage application. Sometime later, Woody is seen greeting the [[Vault 32 raider|Vault 32 dweller]]s and their new overseer, [[Lee Moldaver]], who introduces Lucy's new husband, [[Monty (TV series)|Monty]], to her. After the wedding ceremony is held, he and Reg are seen setting up the podium for Overseer Hank, who gives a poignant speech about his daughter's marriage. The two then stand and watch as the [[Vault 33 dweller]]s dance with their Vault 32 counterparts. [[File:FOTV Trailer 1 27.png|thumb|250px|Woody witnesses the Vault 32 raiders killing dwellers]] When the Vault 32 dwellers are revealed to have been [[Vault 32 raider|raiders from the surface]], Woody hides behind a doorframe. Upon seeing two people hauling in more food for the party, Woody tells them to take it away, but he is too late; he soon witnesses a [[shirtless raider]] kill one dweller and then shoot the two who were bringing food; Woody himself manages to avoid being shot. Rushing into a nearby classroom, Woody runs past some raiders who are beating up a Vault 33 dweller, and then hides behind another doorframe when another dweller in the distant corridor is shot and killed by one of [[Moldaver's elite guard]]s. With Hank having been kidnapped by the raiders, Reg, Woody, and Betty hold an emergency assembly with the surviving Vault 33 dwellers in their authority as the governing council. During the assembly, Lucy proposes sending a search team to the surface to save her father. However, none of the council members agree with her; Reg questions her plan, Woody tries to mediate, and finally, Betty stresses the importance of the Vault's security, which both Reg and Woody agree with. Lucy leaves, disconcerted, while Woody and the others continue the assembly. Lucy's brother [[Norm MacLean|Norm]] tells her that the three council members may have refused out of a desire to preserve their newfound authority. Soon after, Lucy leaves the Vault on her own to search for her father, aided by Norm and [[Chet (TV series)|Chet]]. ====[[The Head]]==== In the wake of Lucy's departure from Vault 33, Woody and the other two councilmembers hold disciplinary sessions to punish Chet and Norm, firing Chet from his role as gatekeeper. Woody introduces Norm to his session, during which he and Reg alternately lead the conversation, discussing Norm's involvement and the dangers of opening the Vault door. Woody points out that Norm's performance reviews for his various assignments have all listed him as "lacking enthusiasm," and Norm's confirmation displeases Woody. However, Betty seems to get the final say in Norm's punishment, and in response to a comment he makes, she reassigns him to deliver food to sixteen surviving raiders who have been imprisoned in the Vault. [[File:The Head meeting Betty Reg Woody.png|thumb|250px|Woody, Reg and Betty at the assembly]] Afterward, an assembly is held in the Vault to brainstorm what to do with the surviving raiders. After Woody announces their ethical dilemma, Reg chimes in, claiming that they have been given a prime opportunity to prove to the surface world the Vault's goal of repopulating and building a better world on the surface, though Woody calls this a "positive spin" on the situation. He asks for a collective decision, though Betty tells them to promote an idea for discussion. Thanks to a "conversation" that Woody had with one of the raiders, Reg suggests that the Vault 33 dwellers rehabilitate the raiders to integrate them into their society. A few ideas are then proposed by some Vault 33 dwellers, including [[Davey (TV series)|Davey]] and [[Marianne (TV series)|Marianne]]. Norm also raises a suggestion to kill the raiders as retribution, though this is shot down. At that moment, the [[Vault 33 engineer]] appears and tries to privately talk with Reg and Woody. However, the two insist that they talk in public, despite the engineer's objections. Reluctantly, the engineer reveals that the Vault's [[Water chip (TV series)|water chip]] was destroyed, leaving only two months of water for the Vault 33 residents to survive. Before the engineer could finish, Reg cut off the engineer, and the meeting was adjourned. ====[[The Ghouls]]==== [[File:FOTV Woody poster.png|thumb|250px|Woody hanging his election poster]] With Hank gone, an election is set to be held for the Vault's new overseer. Woody, Reg, and Betty are all running in the election, and Woody and Reg are seen hanging up posters for their electoral campaign. Later, they meet outside a cell where a semi-sedated Vault 32 raider is being held for interrogation about his background and the kidnapping of Hank. As they continued talking, the semi-sedated Vault 32 raider regained consciousness and tried to gnaw off his restraints, though Woody advises him against it. The Vault 32 raider curses at Woody and remains uncooperative, so Woody decides to retranquilize the raider and retry the interrogation tomorrow. ====[[The Past]]==== Betty ends up winning the overseer election with 98% of the vote. During the ceremony for Betty's victory, Woody and Reg are in the back, also clapping for Betty. Woody comments "better luck next time" to Reg, and he softly agrees. [[File:Davey and Woody.png|thumb|250px|Davey tells Woody that he voted for Betty]] Later, Woody stands in front of one of his campaign posters with a forlorn look. Davey walks by and compliments Woody for running a "great" campaign, though Woody notes that he only hung ten posters up. Davey sympathizes, admitting he once ran and lost an election against Hank, but understands that "When things look glum, vote for someone from [[Vault 31]]." Before leaving, Davey admits to Woody that he voted for Betty. Soon after, Betty announces that she and the [[Bud Askins|Vault 31 overseer]] have formulated a plan to resettle Vault 32, which will involve transferring many of Vault 33's dwellers into the new Vault. Woody tours Vault 32 along with many other Vault 33 dwellers, unaware that its newly-cleaned facade hides the violence and death that had occurred in the Vault. ====[[The Radio]]==== [[File:The Radio assignments.png|thumb|250px|left|Woody is displeased that he is going into Vault 32]] Woody and Betty are present when Norm tries to deliver food for the Vault 32 raiders only to discover they have all been fatally poisoned, with [[Veronica (TV series)|Veronica]] taking the blame. Immediately after Betty leaves scene, she sends out the Vault 32 reassignment notices. Woody learns that he is being sent to Vault 32, much to his dismay. [[File:Vault 33 guards and Woody.png|thumb|250px|Guards stopping Woody]] On the day when the new Vault 32 dwellers are to be sent to Vault 32, Woody tries to back out but is stopped by [[Vault 33 guard|security guards]]. Unable to bypass them, Woody shrinks back and decides to get back in line for his transfer. Before he leaves for Vault 32, Reg hugs him goodbye, and he is last seen as the Vault 32 door closes with him and his fellow new Vault 32 dwellers behind it. ===Season 2=== {{Quotation|A former member of the governing council of Vault 33, Woody's life was upended when he was reassigned to Vault 32 after the raider attack.|[[Fallout season 2 Amazon overview|''Fallout'' season 2 character description]]}} ====[[The Demon in the Snow]]==== Woody struggles to acclimate to Vault 32, as its layout mirrors that of Vault 33. While trying to find his quarters, he accidentally walks into Davey's. Davey sympathizes with his situation and reveals he accidentally entered the women's room earlier on, which was fortunately empty at the time. Soon after, Woody wanders near the Inter-Vault space and overhears Steph talking to Betty, including their mention of an "experiment." He quickly makes himself scarce as Steph returns to Vault 32. Woody later visits Steph in her quarters to inform her that he discovered her meeting with Betty, reminding her that the Vault-Tec handbook stipulated that the Inter-Vault space was for triennial trades only. He admits he is unsure how to proceed, as any violations are to be reported to the overseer, but in this case the violator was the overseer herself. Steph thanks him for his diligence and promises to escalate the report to the overseer (herself). Woody tries inquiring why she was in the Inter-Vault space to begin with, but she avoids the question and enforces her authority over him, ordering him to call her "Overseer Harper" and effectively ending the meeting. As Woody gets up, he notices Chet and asks how he is adjusting to the changes in their lives, pointedly glancing at Steph in the back, though Chet claims to be taking things in stride. Steph steps between them to break up the conversation and force Woody out. As he leaves their quarters, he turns back to Steph and asks about the "experiment" she discussed with Betty, but she passes it off as "overseer stuff" and shuts the door. ====[[The Other Player]]==== Woody does not appear in this episode. However, Davey is shown asking fellow Vault 32 dweller [[Irv]] about Woody, revealing that Woody had seemingly gone missing, as he missed their checkers game earlier that morning. Chet, aware of the implications after Woody's meeting with Steph, asks Davey about the details; Davey tells Chet that he only plays checkers to keep Woody happy. Irv suggests reporting his disappearance to Steph, though Davey dismisses this. ====[[The Handoff]]==== Woody also does not appear in this episode, but his fate is revealed. Later that same day, while Chet is cleaning up after dinner with [[Steph Harper]], he notices the sink in their room is clogged. When he tries to fix the clog, he discovers Woody's glasses in the sink, with what appears to be a bullet hole through one of the lenses. Chet conceals his finding from Steph, who is still sitting at the dinner table, and asks her where Woody went. Steph claims Woody was sent to [[Vault 31]] on a leadership exchange program. Seemingly not wanting to press the issue, Chet discreetly breaks Woody's glasses and puts the pieces back into the garbage disposal to be rid of them. Whether due to a change of heart or otherwise, Chet later reveals Woody's death to all of the Vault 32 dwellers as they are gathered for his wedding with Steph. They do not readily believe him due to him having destroyed the evidence; however, they do end up turning on Steph when Chet reveals she is [[Canada|Canadian]]. ==Personality== Woody is naive and portrays himself as optimistic and agreeable. While he attempts to assert himself as a governing voice, he is overshadowed by his governing peers, Betty and Reg, which causes his fellow Vault dwellers to not take him seriously. In truth, he is a coward, and his cowardice occasionally overcomes his positive and agreeable demeanor, such as when he objected to being reassigned to Vault 32. However, when he tries to back out of being reassigned to Vault 32, the vault security guards intimidate him into compliance, which causes him to capitulate and meekly obey the orders of his Overseer. ==Appearances== Woody Thomas appears {{in|FOTV}}. He also appears in the ''[[Fallout 2d20: NPC Pack - Hollywood Heroes]]'' expansion pack for ''[[Fallout: The Roleplaying Game]]'', where his gameplay statistics are listed. {{FOTV appearances |1=101 |3=103 |4=104 |5=105 |7=107 |12=204 }} ==Gallery== FalloutS2TBimage6_WoodyThomas.jpg|Prime season 2 promotional image Fallout Season 1 Amazon Woody.png|Profile image from Prime Video character overview (S1) Fallout Season 2 Amazon Woody.png|Profile image from Prime Video character overview (S2) ==References== {{References}} '''Script''' {{References|group=Script}} {{Navbox characters FOTV}} [[Category:Fallout TV series human characters]] [[Category:Vault 32 characters]] [[Category:Vault 33 characters]] [[category:Fallout: The Roleplaying Game characters]]

'''Veronica''' is a resident of [[Vault 33]] {{In|FOTV}}.

==''Fallout'' TV series==
===[[The Ghouls]]===
After the [[Vault 32 raider|raiders]] attack Vault 33, she is tasked with supervising the imprisoned raiders, alongside two armored [[Vault 33 guard|guards]].

Veronica sits at her desk, playing solitaire, until [[Norm MacLean|Norm]] arrives with a trolley tray with a Jell-O cake. The two greet each other, and Veronica became upset to learn that the raiders are getting the Jell-O cake, which Norm remarks, he's following his orders. To that, Veronica wondered what his [[Hank MacLean|father]] would have to say about this, which Norm claims he'd deliver the cake himself. Agreeing with Norm, she mentions that Hank was a saint and was allowed to have it by Veronica, who thankfully takes it away and remarking she'd put it in her fridge.

===[[The Radio]]===
[[File:Guards take Veronica.png|thumb|250px|Guards take Veronica away]]
As time passed, Veronica continued to sit behind her desk again, playing solitaire as Norm delivered the Vault 32 raiders their daily food.

Eventually, when the Vault 32 raiders all died from poisoning, Veronica was blamed for it. While being hauled away by two [[Vault 33 guard]]s, Veronica claimed she was innocent. 

==Personality==
Veronica is seemingly kind and cordial as displayed when she spoke with Norm about the Jell-O cake.

Davey (TV series).wikitext:
{{Infobox character |games =FOTV |image =FOTV Davey.png |race =[[Human]] |gender =Male |age = |age verified= |family = |affiliation =[[Vault 32]]
[[Vault 33]] (formerly) |role = |height =6'2.5" (189 cm)[https://www.leerleary.com/ Leer Leary's official website] |eye color =Blue |hair color =Dirty blonde |TV actor =[[Leer Leary]] }} '''Davey''' is a resident of [[Vault 33]] who moves into [[Vault 32]] in [[Timeline#2296|2296]] {{In|FOTV}}. ==Background== Davey is known to have lost to [[Hank MacLean]] in a previous [[Overseer]] election in Vault 33. He voted for [[Betty Pearson]] in the 2296 Overseer election. ==''Fallout'' TV series== ===Season 1=== ====[[The End (episode)|The End]]==== [[File:FoTV vault 33 anxious dwellers.jpg|thumb|250px|[[Reg McPhee]] and Davey concerned about Lucy leaving the Vault]] Davey is briefly seen sitting among other [[Vault 33 dweller]]s who survived the [[Vault 32 raider]]s' attack on their Vault when [[Lucy MacLean]] proposes sending a team to search for her father on the surface. Soon after, he appears more prominently, pushing a wheelbarrow and assisting in the initial cleanup of the Vault, and is seen to have sustained a small wound on his forehead. He reacts with confusion when Norm greets him, saying that his day is going as "bad as everyone else's." He gives Norm another look of disbelief, shaking his head as he leaves. Davey and [[Reg McPhee|Reg]] witness [[Norm MacLean|Norm]] and [[Chet (TV series)|Chet]] help [[Lucy MacLean]] leave [[Vault 33]]. They try to talk Lucy out of leaving, but fail to stop her. Davey comments blithely about this as Lucy leaves.{{FOTV|1|1}} ====[[The Head]]==== Davey offers to teach the captured prisoners from [[Lee Moldaver]]'s raiders about [[William Shakespeare]], as well as [[Christopher Marlowe]], "when they are ready."{{FOTV|1|3}} ====[[The Past]]==== [[File:Vault 33 election.png|thumb|250px|Davey is voting for Betty]] Davey participates in voting for a new Vault 33 overseer, and while in line, he apologizes to Reg and initially alludes to him that he's voting for [[Betty Pearson|Betty]] instead of him. On the other hand, Reg understands, and when Davey informs Reg that he's voting for Betty, Reg states that he had that impression.{{FOTV|1|5}} [[File:Davey and Woody.png|thumb|250px|left|Davey and Woody after the election]] Afterward, Davey would console a forlorn [[Woody Thomas|Woody]], who was reeling over his election loss to Betty. He'd relate with Woody over his election loss, detailing he ran once, but lost against [[Hank MacLean|Hank]]. Davey would then recite the [[Vault 31]] phrase, "When things look glum, vote for someone from Vault 31". Before leaving, Davey again confesses that he voted for Betty to Woody. {{clear}} ====[[The Radio]]==== Davey discovers he will be relocating to Vault 32, which he positively reacts to. He moves into it with [[Steph Harper|Steph]], Chet and Woody. ===Season 2=== ====[[The Innovator]]==== In contrast to his initial optimism, Davey reveals in a meeting with Steph, the new overseer, that he has been having difficulties navigating through the Vault due to its layout being a mirror of 33's, such as now having to take two left turns instead of two rights to reach the elevator. Despite Steph's attempt to end the meeting quickly, Davey continues by suggesting hanging some signage, then begins rambling about avoiding controversy by instead commissioning a feasibility study on signage, which the overseer frustratedly agrees to. As he leaves the overseer's office and makes small chat with [[Chet (TV series)|Chet]] holding [[Chet Jr.]], Davey remarks on his "good fortune" to have found a wife and a child to raise despite Chet's protests against both of those facts. Davey exits the office foyer but turns to face a wall where he thought there was a hallway and has to turn around. ====[[The Demon in the Snow]]==== Davey is reading a book in his quarters when Woody accidentally walks in. Woody apologizes, citing difficulties getting used to their new home's layout; Davey sympathizes, recalling that he once accidentally walked into the women's men's room, which was fortunately empty. He then remarks that he would prefer living back in Vault 33. ====[[The Other Player]]==== Davey asks [[Irv]] if he has seen Woody, as they were due to play checkers that morning but Woody is nowhere to be found. As Chet called him over, Davey asks him if he wants to know the truth. Pulling up a chair, he confesses that he doesn't even like checkers and only plays it to keep Woody happy. Irv suggests they report Woody's disappearance to the overseer, but Davey scoffs before quickly apologizing to Chet for offending his wife. Chet insists that Steph wasn't his wife, so Davey corrects himself to say that fiancee is more appropriate, giving Chet a knowing wink before walking off. Chet, in fact, did not know that Steph had arranged for him to be married to her the next day. ====[[The Handoff]]==== Davey later officiates Chet and Steph's wedding. However, when it comes time for Chet to say, "I do", he refuses, throwing off Davey, who misheard them at first and was about to pronounce them married. Chet admits he is only going through with the wedding in order to have witnesses to formally accuse Steph of killing Woody, claiming he found Woody's glasses in his and Steph's garbage disposal. Given the severity of the accusation, Davey asks to see his evidence, only for Chet to admit that he ended up destroying the evidence. Because of this, none of the dwellers believe Chet's accusation, with Davey attributing Chet's behavior to "cold feet." Chet then reveals that Steph was not born in Vault 31, that she is in fact over 200 years old, and that she is [[Canada|Canadian]], causing the vault dwellers to react with outrage; Davey snatches Steph's Canadian ID card from Chet's hand to examine for himself. Outed, Steph retreats to her office and seals herself inside, with Davey, Chet, and the other Vault 32 dwellers gathering outside soon after to demand Steph come out. ====[[The Strip]]==== Still gathered outside Steph's office, Davey tells the assembled Vault 32 dwellers that their actions will serve as a "strong message to management," and Irv declares after him that it should mean "death to management." Davey, Irv, and the other dwellers begin chanting this message, while Chet is left horrified, realizing that the situation is starting to resemble what happened to the previous residents of Vault 32. ==Personality== Davey presents himself as an educated man who is well-versed in the theatrical arts of [[William Shakespeare]] and [[Christopher Marlowe]], but he is also shown to be fretful and have a guilty conscience for even small acts of self-perceived betrayal. This is displayed when he confesses that he voted for Betty to Reg and Woody instead of them. After being transferred to Vault 32, Davey struggled to acclimate to his new surroundings, which were designed to mirror Vault 33, preferring to the familiarity of his old Vault. ==Appearances== Davey appears only {{In|FOTV}}. {{FOTV appearances|1=101|3=103|5=105|7=107|9=201|12=204|14=206|15=207|16=208}} ==Gallery== Davey's assignment.png|Davey learns of his new assignment ==References== {{References}} '''Meta''' {{References|group=Meta}} {{Navbox characters FOTV}} [[Category:Fallout TV series human characters]] [[Category:Vault 32 characters]] [[Category:Vault 33 characters]]

'''Marianne the Vault scholar''' is a resident of [[Vault 33]] {{In|FOTV}}.

==Background==
Marianne is a scholarly individual who resides in Vault 33.

==''Fallout'' TV series==
===Season 1===
====[[The Head]]====
Sitting at her desk, Marianne unlocks the door from her computer for [[Norm MacLean|Norm]], who delivers a tray of food for the [[Vault 32 raider]]s. As Marianne opens the door hatch to the raider's room, she passes the trays of food to them all while trying to be polite to them all. 

When a conference is held led by the Vault 33 governing council members [[Woody Thomas|Woody]], [[Reg McPhee|Reg]], and [[Betty Pearson|Betty]]. The topic of the discussion is what to do with the Vault 32 raiders and when it's decided to integrate them into their society. When [[Davey (TV series)|Davey]] suggests teaching the Vault 32 raiders [[William Shakespeare|Shakespeare]] and when they're ready, [[Christopher Marlowe|Marlowe]]. However, Marianne cuts in, stating that Shakespeare is too advanced for them, and suggests starting with a more moral framework with [[Immanuel Kant|Kant]], [[John Stuart Mill|Mill]], etc.

After a couple more suggestions are tossed out, Norm scoffs and Reg asks him if he has a suggestion, which he notes that it's not their obligation to help them. On the other hand, one [[Vault 33 dweller]] claims that they didn't know any better, while Marriane concurs, stating they don't have a formal education. Still, Norm suggests killing them all in retribution for what they did to them all, which earns him a disapproving reaction from the Vault 33 dwellers and council, causing Betty to mediate the situation as best as she can.

Just then, the [[Vault 33 engineer]] arrives and wants to say something to the council in private, but Reg insists he formally announces it to everyone. As it turns out, he notes that the [[Water chip (TV series)|water chip]] was destroyed, and they likely have less than two months' worth of water.

Once that was revealed, Marianne and the other Vault 33 dwellers headed off.

====[[The Past]]====
[[File:Vault 33 election.png|thumb|right|200px]]

On the day to vote for a new Vault 33 overseer, Marianne is seen passing out election ballots to the Vault 33 dwellers.

Afterward, once all of the votes are tallied, Marianne gives a formal announcement stating that 98% of the people had elected Betty as their new overseer. Marianne stands by as Betty gives a speech where she thanks everyone there and slices up the jelly cake for them all.

The next day, Marianne partakes in viewing [[Vault 32]], and learns from Betty that many of the residents of Vault 33 will be transferred over to Vault 32.

Genetic researcher |family =[[Cassandra Hawthorne]] - wife {{Icon|dead}} |TV actor =[[Eric Berryman]] }} {{Quotation|I want to reiterate that a society governed by scientists really is the ideal social structure!}} '''Lloyd Hawthorne''' was a leader of [[Hawthorne Medical Laboratories]], as well as the first [[overseer]] of [[Vault 4]] in the [[Fallout (TV series)|''Fallout'' TV series]]. ==Background== He was a [[Vault-Tec Corporation|Vault-Tec]] scientist, later overseer, specializing in the effects of radiation on human DNA. He, his family, and eighty volunteers participated in a five-year-long trial run of Vault 4 before the [[Great War]]. After the war, he and his wife [[Cassandra Hawthorne|Cassandra]] took shelter in Vault 4, where he served as Overseer of the Vault and conducted cruel human experiments, including hybridizing humans with radiation-resistant animals and creating [[Gulper (TV series)|gulpers]]. At least several years after the Vault was sealed, the test subjects of Vault 4 revolted against the Vault scientists, which led to his death. ==''Fallout'' TV series== ===[[The Trap]]=== [[File:The Trap Cooper at wrap party.png|thumb|right|250px|Bud and the Hawthornes attend the wrap party]] Before the war, Hawthorne and his family appeared in a Vault-Tec commercial alongside [[The Ghoul|Cooper Howard]] where he and his wife explained that they would be staying in the vault for a five-year trial period of the vault before the war. He and his wife also attended the wrap party at Cooper Howard's home alongside [[Bud Askins]]. ===[[The Radio]]=== In 2296, [[Lucy MacLean|Lucy]] was shown a holotape recording of Overseer Hawthorne's death alongside his wife in a room barricaded against a gulper that the revolting test subjects that Hawthorne and the Vault 4 scientists had been experimenting on released. In his final moments, he was unapologetic, insisting that, despite the failure of Vault 4's experiment, a society governed by scientists is "the ideal social structure" and that hybridizing humans with animals "still has potential" before a gulper killed him that the residents unleashed. ==Appearances== Lloyd Hawthorne appears only {{in|FOTV}}. {{FOTV appearances|6=106|7=107}} ==Gallery== S1E6 Character 20.jpg|Lloyd and Cassandra filming a Vault 4 advertisement Fallout Season 1 Amazon Vault-Tec.png|Lloyd and Cassandra filming a Vault 4 advertisement with Cooper Howard Hawthorne Final Words.png|Hawthorne just before his death {{Navbox characters FOTV}} {{Navbox overseers}} [[Category:Fallout TV series human characters]] [[Category:Overseers]] [[Category:Vault 4 characters]] [[ru:Ллойд Хоторн]]

'''Birdie''' is a leader of [[Vault 4]] refugees in [[Timeline (2250-2300)#2296|2296]] {{In|FOTV}}. She is the assistant of the [[overseer]] [[Benjamin (TV series)|Benjamin]].

==Background==
She claims that she was born on the surface and comes from [[Shady Sands]]. Her mother was a courier, and when she was 11, she traveled with her mother to [[Filly]]. 

When her hometown was nuked by [[Hank MacLean]] in 2283, Birdie could feel the heat of the blast from Shady Sands across the region. She eventually made her way to Vault 4, where other survivors of Shady Sands would live. Over time, she evidently became something of an authority figure for the Shady Sands refugees in Vault 4, leading them in cult-like rituals to honor their lost hometown and venerate the "[[Lee Moldaver|Flame Mother]]" as someone who can restore what they have lost.

==''Fallout'' TV series==
===[[The Trap]]===
Birdie welcomes [[Lucy MacLean]] and [[Maximus]] when they find themselves in Vault 4, explaining how they will receive medical examinations before being allowed inside the vault. She catches Maximus by the Vault's reactor and offers him a [[Pip-Boy 3000 Mark V|Pip-Boy]] that also serves as a key to a room he could stay in. Later, she leads a ritual with the other Shady Sands survivors in honor of their lost hometown and Lee Moldaver, before later arriving at level 12 to confront Lucy after she was caught there despite told not to go there.

===[[The Radio]]===
Birdie and Ben interrogate Lucy after she is caught sneaking around the restricted area. Birdie explains to Lucy how the Vault is trying to find cures to alleviate the suffering of those who were experimented upon by the original leaders.

==Personality==
Birdie is shown to usually have a calm and serious demeanor, as seen when talking to Lucy when welcoming her and Maximus to Vault 4. She retains her regular attitude even after she catches Lucy breaking the rules by trespassing on Level 12, despite showing disappointment and some anger over Lucy entering Level 12. She never breaks her calm demeanor even when revealing the troubled past of Vault 4 by explaining how its original overseers of Vault 4 experimented on its inhabitants, and accusing Lucy of being associated with Vault-Tec. 

==Notable quotes==
* {{Inline quote|Trust doesn't come easily to those of us with... a guilty conscience.}}
* {{Inline quote|To bring back Shady Sands, blood must spill! Blood must spill! Blood must spill!}}
* {{Inline quote|O [[Lee Moldaver|Flame Mother]], O Flame Mother, you will be our salvation.}}

'''Cassandra Hawthorne''' is a character {{In|FOTV}}.

==Background==
Cassandra was one of the many scientists assigned to work in Vault 4 to research the effects of [[radiation]] on [[human]] DNA.

==''Fallout'' TV series==
===[[The Trap]]===
Cassandra, her husband [[Lloyd Hawthorne]], and two unnamed children appear in a commercial advertisement for [[Vault 4]]. They appear eating dinner at their table, where [[The Ghoul|Cooper Howard]] joins them. He tells the viewers that she and her husband are both scientists who will be studying the effects of Radiation on Human DNA. Cassandra confirms it and notes that they'll be living in Vault 4, leading a community led by scientists.

The commercial continues, and a talk between Lloyd and Cooper occurs about how they, along with eighty other volunteer scientists, will be working there for the next five years. This is to ensure that regardless of what happens, [[United States of America|America]] will be ready for whatever happens. Hearing this, Cooper compliments the family for being the true heroes rather than him, who plays them in the movies.

Once the commercial ends, Cassandra notes how she and Lloyd were so nervous throughout it. A [[Vault-Tec employee (TV series)|Vault-Tech employee]] approaches their table and starts to talk to them.

[[File:The Trap Cooper at wrap party.png|thumb|right|250px|Bud and the Hawthornes attend the wrap party]]

That night Cassandra and her husband attend the wrap-up party held at Cooper's house.

===[[The Radio]]===
In a video recording featuring the final moments between Cassandra and her husband. As Lloyd records his self-confessed final words, Cassandra tries to barricade the doorway to protect them from the [[Gulper (TV series)|gulper]] just outside that broke in and devoured them both. The gulper was later found out to have been named [[Peter (TV series)|Peter]] and was Overseer [[Benjamin (TV series)|Benjamin's]] maternal Great Uncle.

==Personality==
On camera, despite claiming she was so nervous, she portrayed herself to be calm and confident, in contrast, to her husband.

==Notable quotes==
* {{Inline quote|That's right. And we'll be living and working right here in Vault 4, leading a community governed by scientists.|Cassandra talking to the TV camera}}

'''Overseer Benjamin''', or '''Ben''', is the [[overseer]] of [[Vault 4]] in [[Timeline#2296|2296]] {{In|FOTV}}.

==Background==
Benjamin's ancestors were survivors of the [[Great War]] who were accepted into Vault 4 by its original dwellers, scientists who adopted a policy of accepting refugees from the wasteland for use as test subjects. These subjects were put under genetic experimentation, including hybridization with radiation-resistant species. For example, Benjamin's maternal great-uncle, [[Peter (TV series)|Peter]], was (allegedly) turned into a [[Gulper (TV series)|gulper]] by the experiments. The test subjects eventually managed to break free and overthrow the scientists, and they have ruled the Vault ever since, continuing the Vault's refugee policy but for truly benevolent reasons.<ref>''Fallout'' TV series, season 1 episode 7: "[[The Trap]]"</ref>

==''Fallout'' TV series==
===[[The Trap]]===
While Lucy and Maximus are eating, they are introduced to him by [[Birdie]]. They are disturbed by his one eye, but do not wish to offend him by saying anything. He tells them to stay out of level 12 and mentions the Vault only has one foosball table.

Later, Lucy talks to Ben in his office about toilets. He refers to her as Goosey because her name is Goosey on his data sheet. Ben claims to be open-minded and discusses how troublesome surface refugees can be with their smelly food and weird ideas. When Lucy asks about level 12, he shuts down the conversation and orders her to leave.

===[[The Radio]]===
He and Birdie handcuff Lucy when they catch her in level 12. They explain to Lucy what the Vault's experiments are about.

Later, Ben sentences Lucy to death by exile and gives her two weeks of survival supplies.

==Personality==
[[File:FOTV Overseer Benjamin.png|thumb|250px|Benjamin]]
Polite and amenable on the surface, he secretly thinks little of the [[New California Republic|NCR]] refugees who have come to populate his birthplace. In the company of another Vault Dweller, he disparages the "surfies" as smelling bad and having strange, barbaric customs.

Despite harboring this ugly prejudice, he is not known to use his power as the overseer to mistreat or ostracize the immigrant population, and he stands out in the setting as a particularly benevolent and merciful ruler. His highest priority is keeping the grotesque post-human mutants of Level 12 secure and comfortable, especially because he has family among them. When Lucy disfigures an innocent caregiver while intruding on Level 12, her punishment is to be released unharmed to the surface with two weeks' worth of supplies, a measure that Benjamin considers extreme and borderline cruel.

Some of the other Vault 4 natives wear clothing that hides their [[mutations]], but the overseer does not. He appears to be oblivious when Lucy displays alarm at his own mutation, as if unaware in the moment that his appearance and concept of normalcy may be considered confusing or off-putting to outsiders. Benjamin is overall characterized as a highly hypocritical, naïve man who is nonetheless guided by compassion and a strong concept of human rights.

'''Dr. "Nose" Edmundson''' is a character {{In|FOTV}}.

==Background==
Dr. Edmundson is the resident clinician of [[Vault 4]]. His nickname appears to derived from his prominent mutation, a second nose on his forehead.

==''Fallout'' TV series==
===[[The Trap]]===
Dr. Edmundson extracts a tooth out of [[Maximus]]'s right arm, comments on the surface's ingenuity of ammo use, and informs [[Powell|Nurse Powell]] that they will need an antibiotic for him. He then closes Maximus's wound with a staple gun, and after bandaging his wound, Dr. Edmundson uses his [[Pip-Boy]] and leaves Maximus.

Afterward, he's seen at a picnic table taking off his shower cap and Lucy becomes bewildered after she notices the extra nose on his forehead. Dr. Edmundson would see Lucy looking at him and would smile at her and nod assuredly.

Later, when Lucy infiltrates Level 12 of Vault 4, Dr. Edmundson is seen checking on the subjects inside their cryo-stasis pods. He also noted his worry that one of them may have escaped when he saw the door there as open. As he writes something down on his clipboard, Lucy tries to escape, and one of her shoes makes a squeaky nose, which alerts the Dr., and he proceeds to set the alarm off and procure a [[Syringer rifle (TV series)|syringer rifle]]. Lucy would then confront Dr. Edmundson and splash a chemical on his face, causing him to scream in agony while fainting on the floor.

===[[The Radio]]===
Dr. Edmundson would be indirectly mentioned by [[Birdie]] when Lucy saw him in level 12 to what she thought was experimenting on them. In truth, however, he was trying to ease the pain of the test subjects.

Eventually, Dr. Edmundson, now with a gauze pad over his left eye, sat in attendance where Lucy was sentenced to death, by being banished to the surface with two weeks' worth of supplies, and cheers with the other dwellers to celebrate her release. Just as Lucy tries to reason with Overseer Benjamin and Birdie, Maximus arrives in his [[T-60 power armor (TV series)|T-60 power armor]] and demands that Lucy be released. He, along with an angry Vault 4 dweller with an ear on his head, would stand in awe as they saw a [[Nuka-Cola vending machine]] be tossed in the air.

==Personality==
Dr. Edmundson is shown to be an educated doctor when he treats Maximus' injury; other than that, he's seen to be a kind and friendly individual like the rest of the residents of Vault 4.

==Notable quotes==
* {{Inline quote|[Short chuckle] Glad you're alright. When I saw the door was open, I worried one of you might have gotten out|Talking to a subject in a cryo-stasis pod.}}

The '''freed ghoul''' is a [[ghoul]] wastelander {{In|FOTV}}.

==Background==
This ghoul was imprisoned with many others in a freezer in a [[Super Duper Mart (TV series)|Super Duper Mart]] in [[Los Angeles]] by [[Huey]] and [[Squirrel (TV series)|Squirrel]], who intended to later harvest his organs.<!--you can see the price tag on the freezer door-->

His head and hands are white, potentially due to the chilling effects of the freezer that he was in. He has black hair and a missing nose. He wears a black business-like suit, and a blue and red tie. 

==''Fallout'' TV series==
===[[The Ghouls]]===
[[Lucy MacLean]] is brought to the Super Duper Mart by [[the Ghoul]], who intended to sell her off for her organs to be harvested in exchange for Huey and Squirrel providing him with [[Inhaler vial|vials]]. However, Lucy manages to turn the tables by disabling and reprogramming [[Snip Snip]], the duo's [[Mister Handy]]. She uses Snip Snip to threaten the duo into releasing all of the ghouls, and the ones who are not yet feral all run away; this man stops and thanks Lucy before fleeing.<ref>{{FOTV|1|4}}</ref>

===[[The Beginning]]===
Later, Lucy sees the freed ghoul again at the [[Griffith Observatory]], where he's apparently seeking shelter with [[Lee Moldaver]]'s [[New California Republic|NCR remnants]] and works at a mess station. He recognizes Lucy, saying, "That's her!" as she passes, and Lucy also remembers him from before.<ref>{{FOTV|1|8}}</ref>

It is implied that he originally traveled west into New California to obtain a [[Fusion core (TV series)|fusion core]] so he could reactivate Fisto after the robot lost power sometime prior to or around 2296.{{FOTV|2|5}} ==''Fallout'' TV series== ===Season 1=== ====[[The Target]]==== [[File:FOTV Season1 ep1 Snake Oil Salesman 01.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Rescued from his attacker by "Knight Titus"]] Sometime after [[Titus|Knight Titus]]' death from a [[Yao guai (TV series)|yao guai]] attack, [[Maximus]], wearing his [[T-60 power armor (TV series)|T-60 power armor]], comes across the salesman being attacked by [[Chicken collector|an assailant]] and rescues him by threatening to crush the latter's head, believing he was saving an innocent. I can help you. Haven't run into many people traveling with a human head."''

({{FOTV|1|7}}) Thaddeus relents and offers the [[Fusion core (TV series)|fusion core]] he took from Maximus' armor in exchange for the needed medicine. The salesman agrees to the deal and concocts an "elixir" that he gives to Thaddeus. Upon drinking it, the two watch as the soldier's injured foot immediately regenerates. While preparing to continue his journey, Thaddeus inquires about the closest radio station and the salesman informs him of the [[KPSS radio station]] located in the [[Hollywood Hills]] past [[Shady Sands]]. After Thaddeus says that the area around the former capital city is highly irradiated, the salesman comments that Thaddeus will not have to worry about radiation anymore. He then bids Thaddeus farewell and departs.Thaddeus: ''"Do you know where I can find a radio tower? I have to make contact with my base."''

({{fotv|1|7}}) Later, after Thaddeus is mortally wounded by a crossbow trap at the KPSS radio station, he discovers that he has a remarkable regenerative ability that keeps him alive, which Maximus believes is due to [[ghoul]]ification, though this has yet to be confirmed. ===Season 2=== ====[[The Wrangler]]==== {{Quotation|Let's get lucky, shall we?}} With the fusion core bartered from Thaddeus in hand, the snake oil salesman hits the road with a jaunty saunter from Los Angeles to [[New Vegas]]. On his way, he skips merrily, gets attacked by a [[Radroach (TV series)|radroach]], and picks some desert flowers for his special someone. Upon arriving to the outskirts of Vegas, the snake oil salesman reaches his destination, an [[abandoned taco stand]], where he reunites with his beloved, [[Fisto]], through a late night date. While the date is underway, [[Hank MacLean]] arrives with a crowbar behind the snake oil salesman. The snake oil salesman regards him as a voyeur and tells him off. After turning back, Hank MacLean knocks him out with a strike to the back of the head and transports him to the [[Las Vegas management Vault]] to use him as a test subject in refining the [[brain-computer interface chip]] technology. When coming to, the salesman finds himself restrained at a table sitting across from Hank MacLean at a control box, the chip already implanted into the nape of his neck. He struggles against the restraints before MacLean asks him if he would like to forget all his memories while retaining his language and motor skills. The snake oil salesman answers "Please. Yes." Hank MacLean begins configuring the settings on the control box as the salesman makes various exclamations. As MacLean begins the final tuning, the salesman begins laughing and shouting "no" before MacLean reaches the max setting. However, unlike previous attempts, the salesman remains alive with his head intact. The salesman stares wide eyed, the chip having reached its full effect, and MacLean smiles at his first successful configuration. After some time, the salesman is cleaned up for his work and is sent to the surface to bargain with [[the Ghoul]] at the [[Atomic Wrangler Casino]] in [[Freeside]]. He waits with the Ghoul in a room until [[Lucy MacLean]] arrives and then introduces himself, explaining that Hank MacLean cannot be reached without permission from inside his underground facility. Lucy tells the salesman to take them to her father now. The salesman responds that he lacks permission and that Hank is watching over [[Janey Howard|Janey]] and [[Barb Howard]] in cryo chambers and will kill them if the Ghoul and Lucy do not cooperate. Lucy tries to convince the Ghoul not to listen to the salesman, but the salesman interjects that Hank is willing to make a deal: for leaving the Ghoul's wife and daughter unharmed, Hank wants the Ghoul to return Lucy to [[Vault 33]]. Lucy is confused by the deal and the salesman explains that Hank has plans in motion he would prefer for her to "wait out." Lucy cannot find the words before the salesman turns to the Ghoul asking if he accepts the terms. The Ghoul looks at the salesman, who looks around uncomfortably waiting for a response. The Ghoul and Lucy have a short exchange before the Ghoul shoots Lucy with her [[Tranq gun (TV series)|tranq gun]]. As Lucy stumbles to the ground, the salesman tells the Ghoul that he will inform Hank MacLean about his decision and leaves the room. ====[[The Other Player]]==== While Lucy has her father in handcuffs ready to take him back to Vault 33 to face justice, the salesman and another mind controlled man wheel out [[Biff (TV series)|Ranger Biff]] and a legionary asking what to do with them since they are yet to be "fixed." The salesman prompts himself by the button to enable the mind control chips. Hank allows Lucy to make the decision who answers no to enabling their chips, and the salesman acknowledges with a thumbs up. Hank orders him and the other man to release them, which leads to the legionary trying to kill Biff. I thought all you sardine-fucking dipshits were dead!|Ma June to [[Lucy MacLean]]|sound=Ma June.ogg}} '''Ma June''' is the proprietor of [[Ma June's Sundries]], a store in [[Filly]], and an associate of [[Siggi Wilzig]] {{in|FOTV}}. ==Background== Ma June implies that she has been in the [[Los Angeles]] area since at least the [[Fall of Shady Sands|destruction of Shady Sands]]. She was aware of both the [[New California Republic]] and the [[Enclave]].[[Norm MacLean]]: ''"So you met my sister?"''
[[Ma June]]: ''"Yeah, back in Filly. Before the Brotherhood of Steel burnt it down. Had her help a fella from the Enclave get through the Shithole to some folks from the NCR who weren't in town when Shady Sands blew up. Pretty slim odds. What with it being Khan country."''
({{FOTV|2|5}}) She was also familiar with the [[Vault]]s, and came to resent the Vaults and their residents for living sheltered lives compared to the rest of the surface. By 2296, Ma June had been operating a general store in the town of Filly, together with another person named [[Barv]]. Her store sold various supplies, including sundries, weapons, electronics, "rarities," and more. Around that time, she struck a deal with [[Lee Moldaver]], leader of an NCR remnant force in Los Angeles, to arrange for Enclave defector [[Siggi Wilzig]] to be transported to Moldaver's headquarters at [[Griffith Observatory]]. However, Filly was forcefully seized by the [[Knights of San Fernando]] as part of their manhunt for Wilzig, and they burned down the town after it had served its purpose for them. Ma June and Barv subsequently moved to the former [[Vault-Tec headquarters (TV series)|Vault-Tec headquarters]], where they began farming [[Radroach (TV series)|radroaches]] for a living.[[Claudia (TV series)|Claudia]]: ''"Can I ask you a question?"''
[[Barv]]: ''"Mm-hmm."''
Claudia: ''"What is making that noise in the elevator?"''
Barv: ''"Roach farm."''
Claudia: ''"How big are they?"''
Barv: ''"Not big enough for market yet, but they'll get there."''
({{FOTV|2|5}}) ==''Fallout'' TV series== ===Season 1=== {{Quotation|A trader in the small junk town of Filly, Ma June will trade with anyone — so long as they have the caps. Just remember, she didn’t establish her position by being a pushover. Cross her, and you’ll find yourself on the business end of rifle.{{sic}}|[[Fallout season 1 Amazon overview|''Fallout'' season 1 character description]]}} ====[[The Target]]==== [[Lucy MacLean]] encounters Ma June sometime after leaving [[Vault 33]]. Lucy points out that Ma June has [[Vault-Tec Corporation]] items in her store and assumes Ma June does business with criminals, mentioning she is searching for one. Ma June is amused that Lucy is a real [[Vault]] dweller and laughs in her face. Ma June's attitude hardens when Lucy mentions [[Lee Moldaver]], and she orders Lucy to leave immediately. Lucy asserts she wants to save her father, but Ma June is skeptical that Lucy will live long on the surface. Lucy mentions the Vaults' mission to save America, but Ma June denounces the Vaults as "a hole in the ground for rich folks to hide in while the rest of the world burned." Ma June says, "fuck the Vaults," and gives Lucy the finger. Lucy then leaves, despondent. [[File:FOTV S1 Amazon promo 9.jpg|thumb|250px|Outside her store with Lucy and Wilzig]] Ma June notes [[Siggi Wilzig]] speaking to Lucy outside. She asks Wilzig if he is Wilzig and tells him to get inside, while she orders Lucy to go. [[The Ghoul]] arrives since he is tracking Wilzig for a bounty. Ma June reacts with suspicion towards the Ghoul, telling him that his "kind" (ghouls) are not welcome in Filly. Ma June mentions she herself has been paid a lot of caps to transport Wilzig to his next destination. The Ghoul shoots off Wilzig's leg, making Ma June shout she has 1000 caps for whoever kills the Ghoul, but that no one will get anything if she kills him first. In the ensuing firefight, Ma June shoots the Ghoul, but he shoots her in the knee. When Lucy stands up for Wilzig, Ma June finds Lucy's articulate speech ridiculous. [[Maximus]] arrives to fight the Ghoul, letting Lucy bandage Ma June's knee. In the back room, Ma June tries to assist Wilzig with his leg injury by putting on a makeshift leg. She asks Lucy to take Wilzig to her client, who happens to be Moldaver and says Lucy can bargain with Moldaver with Wilzig. Ma June puts Moldaver's location into Lucy's Pip-Boy and tries to motivate Lucy before she leaves. It is unknown what happened to Ma June and Barv after Lucy and Wilzig left, as they aren't seen in their deserted storefront when the Ghoul entered looking for clues. It is also unclear if they returned after that before Filly was taken over by the [[Knights of San Fernando]], with their shop in particular being turned into an armory. ===Season 2=== ====[[The Wrangler]]==== After the Brotherhood acquired the cold fusion technology by defeating Moldaver's NCR remnants, according to Ma, they burned Filly down, forcing the survivors of their initial takeover to move elsewhere. Ma June and Barv found their way to the abandoned [[Vault-Tec headquarters (TV series)|Vault-Tec headquarters]] in Los Angeles and turned the lobby into their new home. They also created makeshift pens out of the old elevator shafts to support a [[Radroach (TV series)|radroach]] breeding farm. The pair left their new home at some point before the arrival of the [[Vault 31 dweller]] expedition led by [[Norm MacLean]], and came back shortly after they arrived, holding them at gunpoint until Norm was able to resolve the tension. In a private conversation with Norm, Ma revealed her previous encounter with his sister Lucy and tried to catch Norm up on current events until she is told he has no idea who groups like the Enclave, the NCR, or the Khans even are. She drops the matter to then tell him his sister is most likely dead. She and Barv head off again, before which Ma offers the expedition to take what they want from their stash. When Barv remarks on Ma June's sudden sense of charity, she says it's her attempt to be a better person, for what it's worth. ==Personality== Ma June is a stern and tough woman who does not establish her position by being a pushover. She will trade with anyone as long as they have the caps. However, she is also willing to threaten people with a gun if they betray her.[https://www.amazon.com/Fallout-Season-1/dp/B0CN4HV16N Amazon show description] She shares the common disdainful opinion of the [[Vault]]s and their inhabitants like most wastelanders, viewing Vault dwellers as naive idealists detached from the reality of the wasteland due to their isolation as well as, in her eyes, a living reminder that the underground bunkers were only ever intended to ensure the survival of the [[United States of America|American]] upper class at the expense of everyone else on the day the bombs dropped. She also has a prejudice against [[ghoul]]s, openly warning the Ghoul that "his kind" are not welcome in Filly when the bounty hunter comes for his target. After encountering Lucy and later losing her home, Ma's harsh attitude towards Vault dwellers seems to have softened a bit as she is more patient with Norm's inexperience with the wasteland, but is no less firm in telling him that he and his fellows "vaulties" won't be safe anywhere but in a Vault. ==Inventory== {{Inventory |game =FOTV |title =yes |apparel =[[Ma June jacket|Ma June's jacket]]

The vaults were nothing more than a hole in the ground for rich folks to hide in while the rest of the world burned.}} ==Appearances== Ma June appears {{In|FOTV}}. She also appears in ''[[Fallout Shelter]]'' (as of update 1.16.0) and in the ''[[Fallout 2d20: NPC Pack - Hollywood Heroes]]'' expansion pack for ''[[Fallout: The Roleplaying Game]]''. {{FOTV appearances|2=102|13=205}} ==Gallery== Fallout Season 1 Amazon Ma June.png|Amazon preview FOTV Amazon Profile Picture Ma June.png|Prime Video profile image Ma June and Barv The Wrangler.jpg|In "[[The Wrangler]]" ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox characters FOTV}} {{Navbox characters FOS}} [[Category:Fallout TV series human characters]] [[Category:Fallout Shelter characters]] [[Category:Fallout: The Roleplaying Game characters]] [[Category:Filly characters]] [[ru:Ма Джун]] [[zh:玛·琼]]
