'''Sorrel Booker''' is the president of [[the Govermint]] {{In|FOTV}}.<ref name="FalloutTV">{{fotv|1|6}}</ref>

==Background==
Sorrel Booker is an old associate of [[the Ghoul]]. By [[Timeline (2250-2300)#2296|2296]], he became the self-proclaimed president of the "[[Govermint]]," with several [[Sheriff (TV series)|sheriffs]] as his subordinates, and with such businesses as the organ harvesters at the [[Super Duper Mart (TV series)|Super Duper Mart]] under his protection in [[Los Angeles]].<ref name="FalloutTV" />

==''Fallout'' TV series==
===[[The Trap]]===
[[File:Cyst dish.png|thumb|250px|Sorrel Booker's cyst dish]]
While eating a meal at his table in the [[BBQ Shack (TV series)|BBQ Shack]] serving as the Govermint building, Sorrel noted his surprise that the [[ghoul]] he heard about that wrecked the Super Duper Mart was the legendary Ghoul himself. Sorrel went on to detail a bit of the Ghoul's history as a famous [[Bounty Hunter]] to the sheriffs [[Troy (TV series)|Troy]] and [[Rex (TV series)|Rex]]. The Ghoul then politely asks Sorrel for a needle and a thread, claiming there's one in his bag. Looking at Troy, Sorrel signals him to fetch it from his bag, and he does by placing the items on the table.<ref name="FalloutTV" />

The cloth that the needle and thread were wrapped under unraveled on the table, which Sorrel scoffed at its sight. The Ghoul then holds up his rope-bound hands and asks if he'd be so kind as to have them untied. This request makes Sorrel pause with a cold look on his face, which the Ghoul coaxes him, stating they're old friends. After a brief silent pause between them, Sorrel uses his knife to sever the ropes restraining the Ghoul. Sorrel then comments that after 200 years, he doesn't know what keeps him going and then takes a drag off of his cigarette. He goes on to guess if the Ghoul simply enjoys the good old [[State#California|California]] Sunshine on his wrinkly ass face. His next comment, noting that the Ghoul was still after "her," upsets the Ghoul as he sews his finger back onto his hand.<ref name="FalloutTV" />

[[File:Booker and The Ghoul.png|thumb|250px|Booker and the Ghoul]]
The Ghoul then snidely remarks that Sorrel can cross off one good reason for being off his list. He states that it's not to have unintelligent conversations with the likes of him, who had continued to his meal. Said remark made Troy whack the Ghoul in the head with the butt of his gun and reprimand him to respect, the "President" of the Govermint. Regaining his composure, the Ghoul quizzically asks if Sorrel is a president now, to which Sorrel answers he doesn't see why not. It was the Ghoul's suggestion that Sorrel hire a publicist to advertise the fact as it was the first he heard of it. He'd go on to mention that there's a woman named "[[Lee Moldaver|Moldaver]]."<ref name="FalloutTV" />

Hearing the name causes Sorrel to spit out what he was eating and state that she goes by the name of "Flame Mother"; further stating how that "bitch" is dangerous. On the other hand, the Ghoul comments that being dangerous is a prerequisite for being a good leader in modern times. Sorrel then claims that someone needs to step up and bring order to those parts and continues asking if the Ghoul knew why the "boys" brought him in. As the Ghoul sews his finger back on, he answers that it's because he ruined an organ trade business, and Sorrel confirms it.<ref name="FalloutTV" />

They'd then agree that they've always "liked" the other, but Sorrel couldn't overlook the ruination of the Super Duper Mart, which was under the Govermint's protection. Hence, if the Ghoul were released scot-free, then the people would lose faith in his protective services. Sorrel then asks the Ghoul what would happen, to which he answers anarchy in the streets, and Sorrel confirms it.<ref name="FalloutTV" />

Sorrel asks if the Ghoul has anything to say in his defense, who had finished sewing his finger back on, and answers, "Guilty as charged." The answer perplexed Sorrel about the blatant confession from the Ghoul, and he confirms it, then segueing into how he shot up [[Filly]] and killed nine to ten people there. Troy then remarks that his daddy lives in Filly, prompting Sorrel to warn him not to get caught up in what the Ghoul was saying, who had just disparaged his father as a possible coward. However, the Ghoul claims he's not trying to start anything, but discern whether or not Troy was a plausible coward like his father.<ref name="FalloutTV" />

Before Troy can shoot his rifle at the Ghoul, Sorrel orders Rex to disarm Troy of his weapon, which the Ghoul remarks was a "very presidential" thing for him to do. Sorrel then orders the two sheriffs to take the Ghoul out back and feed him to the [[hog]]s. However, as they do, the Ghoul kills the two of them all while Sorrel watches and curses what he has witnessed.<ref name="FalloutTV" />

After that, the Ghoul noted he had one question for Sorrel; from there, he pulled a wanted poster of Moldaver from his wall and asked why he had her picture on his wall. Sorrel answered Ghoul's question and asked why she was Moldaver. Astonished to hear Sorrel's answer, the ghoul claimed that it was not how he remembered her. Sorrel followed up, asking the Ghoul how he remembered her, earning him a cold glare from him.<ref name="FalloutTV" />

==Personality==
[[File:Sorrel Booker and Sheriff Troy.png|thumb|250px|Sorrel Booker and Sheriff Troy]]
Sorrel is shown to be a very talkative and gluttonous man. As an old associate of the Ghoul, he appears to have some respect and trust for the Ghoul, given his reputation as a [[bounty hunter]]. He is also level-headed enough not to be provoked by the Ghoul's remarks, which are meant to throw opponents off their guard. However, he is also ruthless enough to kill anyone who threatens his position of power, old friend or not.<ref name="FalloutTV" /> Despite this, he seems only moderately upset when the Ghoul shoots his two sheriffs, and appears completely unafraid, and continued in calm conversation, suggesting that he was willing to let the Ghoul go at that cost since it would maintain his reputation. As he states, if he lets someone go after knocking over an operation under his protection his authority would be undermined, so the Ghoul escaping at the cost of two of his subordinates lives would allow him to save face. 

==Notable quotes==
* {{Inline quote|You boys know who you just brought in? This sumbitch right here used to be the best bounty hunter to ever shoot a man in the ass. Kids these days don't know their goddamn history|Sorell talking to Troy and Rex about the Ghoul's history as a Bounty Hunter}}

==Appearances==
Sorrel Booker appears only {{in|FOTV}}, where he is portrayed by [[Glenn Fleshler]].
{{FOTV appearances|5=105}}

==Behind the scenes==
Sorrel Booker's name and character are a reference to actor [[wikipedia:Sorrell Booke|Sorrell Booke]] and specifically his role as [[Wikipedia:Boss Hogg|Jefferson Davis "JD"/"Boss" Hogg]] in the 1979 original series ''[[wikipedia:The Dukes of Hazard|The Dukes of Hazard]]''. In that series, like Booker, "Boss" Hogg is a low-level authority figure who suffers the loss of several subordinates to the actions of the protagonists, Unlike Booker, Hogg maintains a certain code of ethics, such as refusing to get involved in the drug trade or endanger others' lives with his schemes, whereas Booker helps protect the operations of organ harvesters.

'''Monty''' is a [[Vault 32 raider|raider]] {{In|FOTV}}. In [[Timeline#2296|2296]], he infiltrated [[Vault 33]], posing as a dweller of [[Vault 32]].

==Background==
===Post-War===
Monty was one of [[Lee Moldaver|Moldaver]]'s raiders, during their invasion and occupation of [[Vault 32]]. He posed as a Vault 32 resident and was the "breeder" in the Vaults' Triennial Trade in 2296.

==''Fallout'' TV series==
===[[The End (episode)|The End]]===
[[File:FOTV wedding.png|thumb|left|270px|Lucy and Monty's wedding]]
Monty was the choice for [[Vault 32]]'s Triennial Trade with [[Vault 33]], being the "breeder" exchanged for farming equipment from Vault 33. He was married to [[Lucy MacLean]] as part of [[Lee Moldaver|Moldaver]]'s infiltration of Vault 33 and ate with Lucy and [[Steph Harper]] during the wedding banquet. During the banquet, Lucy asked him about his sperm count; Monty did not understand her, but Steph moved the conversation away, interpreting Monty's silence as due to the awkwardness of the question.

[[File:FOTV Lucy and Monty kissing.png|thumb|250px|Monty kissing Lucy]]
After the wedding, he took Lucy back to her apartment bridal style. While Lucy was contemplating their family's future, Monty undressed, and with a statement of simply "Okey dokey then" from Lucy, they had sex. Afterwards, Monty left the bed and cleaned himself off with the apartment's curtains.

Once Moldaver's attack on the Vault began, Lucy, suspicious of Monty's behavior, discovered that he was from the surface after detecting his radiation levels using her Pip-Boy's Geiger counter. Monty expressed disappointment and attacked Lucy, throwing her across the room and attempting to kill her with a kitchen knife. Lucy managed to disarm him and wound him with the knife, but he quickly recovered and stabbed her in the stomach before choking her against the kitchen counter. Lucy managed to survive by grabbing a nearby glass pitcher and smashing Monty across the face with it, knocking him unconscious. Lucy then left after treating her wounds.

Monty later attacked Lucy again in the Vault atrium, where it was revealed that the right side of his face had been maimed and cut open by the glass pitcher. Right as he had her cornered, [[Hank MacLean]] hit him on the head with a shovel, making him fall to the floor. Hank then dragged Monty over to a barrel of pickles in vinegar and drowned him in it.

Monty appears only {{in|FOTV}}.

[[Knights of San Fernando]] |TV actor =[[Brendan Burke]] }} '''Petty Officer{{FOTV|1|3}}, ~10:26 Shortsight''' is a character {{In|FOTV}}. ==Background== Shortsight is a member of the [[Knights of San Fernando]] chapter of the [[Brotherhood of Steel]] at their [[Brotherhood base|base]] somewhere on the West Coast in [[Timeline#2296|2296]]. ==''Fallout'' TV series== ===[[The End (episode)|The End]]=== Shortsight was one of the officers present when the Knights of San Fernando received their mission to apprehend [[Siggi Wilzig]]. He fetches [[Dane (TV series)|Dane]], presumably to have their superiors inform them that they will be Knight [[Titus]]' [[Brotherhood of Steel ranks|squire]]. After Squire Dane's maiming, Petty Officer Shortsight escorts [[Maximus]] to a [[vertibird]], where he is to be interrogated by Elder Cleric [[Quintus]] and a Brotherhood knight who intimidates Maximus to speak truthfully. After Maximus is cleared of all charges, Maximus becomes [[Titus|Knight Titus]]' squire in Dane's place. As Quintus briefs the Brotherhood's knights and the squires of their mission to recover Siggi Wilzig, Shortsight nudges [[Thaddeus]] and an aspirant who were distracted in their duties of handing out pictures of the search parties' targets. ===[[The Head]]=== After Maximus' confrontation with [[The Ghoul]], Maximus's [[power armor]] is damaged. He tows his power armor to a nearby stand. As he is checking its condition (finding a damaged component while doing so), Petty Officer Shortsight talks over the radio, attempting to check up on Knight Titus' condition after having missed a check-in. Maximus deepens his voice and pretends to be Knight Titus. He lies to the Brotherhood by telling them that the squire assigned to him (Maximus) had died while in a confrontation with an "abomination"; however, his plan goes wrong as the other party suggests sending a replacement squire. Maximus tries to convince them not to send one, as this would blow his cover. After failing to convince the Brotherhood not to deliver a replacement squire, Maximus intentionally destroys the power armor's radio to cut off communications with the Brotherhood. ===[[The Beginning]]=== Petty Officer Shortsight is part of the main assault force sent to capture [[Griffith Observatory]]. He is part of the first Brotherhood group that makes it inside the observatory building alongside Maximus, three knights, and at least seven others. He is present when they are attacked by [[the Ghoul]], who removes the area's [[Fusion core (TV series)|fusion core]] to disable the lights and exploits a flaw in the chest plating of the [[T-60 power armor]] to briefly incapacitate one of the knights, stunning everyone else present. The Ghoul then disables the area's lights and takes advantage of the ensuing chaos to shoot the knights and the other soldiers numerous times. Partway into the skirmish, Shortsight is seen being shot in the chest, after which the Ghoul is then seen killing a knight with a hand grenade. The rest of the group's fate, apart from Maximus, remains unknown.{{FOTV|1|8}}, ~42:34
The surviving five unarmored soldiers, including Maximus [[:File:FOTV s1 ep8 Maximus during Ghoul fight.png|can be seen at ~42:45]]. Shortsight is not among them, indicating the man shot 10 seconds earlier was indeed him. ==Personality== Shortsight seems like a disciplinarian to his subordinates and thinks that squires are easily replaceable since they have plenty of squires. ==Notable quotes== * {{Inline quote|Aspirant Dane? You're being summoned. Come with me.|Shortsight to Dane about their summonings}} ==Appearances== Petty Officer Shortsight appears only {{in|FOTV}}. {{FOTV appearances|1=101|3=103|8=108}} ==Gallery== FOTV knights in observatory.png|Shortsight and co. confront [[the Ghoul]] FOTV s1 ep8 Shortsight.png|Stunned at the sight of the Ghoul downing a knight FOTV Shortsight shot 1.png|Shortsight, seconds before getting shot FOTV Shortsight shot 2.png|Shortsight, shot by the Ghoul ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox characters FOTV}} [[Category:Fallout TV series human characters]] [[Category:Brotherhood of Steel characters]]

And may the shape of the future be cut by your sword!}} |content2={{Quotation|If our rebellion is righteous... the way will be paved for us.}} }} '''Elder Cleric Quintus''' is the leader of the [[Knights of San Fernando]], a chapter of the [[Brotherhood of Steel]] that operates in [[New California]] in [[Timeline#2296|2296]]. He [[Fallout TV series crew|appears]] as a supporting character {{in|FOTV}}, where he is portrayed by [[Michael Cristofer]]. ==Background== [[File:Shady Sands Knight and Maximus.png|thumb|250px|Quintus and young Maximus]] Little is known about Quintus' past, including whether he was recruited or born into the Brotherhood. When the [[New California Republic|NCR]] capital city [[Shady Sands]] was [[Fall of Shady Sands|destroyed with a nuclear weapon]] by [[Hank MacLean]] circa [[Timeline (2250-2300)#2283|2283]], Quintus, at the time a ranking [[Knights|knight]], was nearby and entered the destroyed ruins. When he arrived at the edge of the crater, he found a young boy named [[Maximus|Max]] who had survived after his parents [[Joseph (TV series)|Joseph]] and [[Julia (TV series)|Julia]] put him in their [[refrigerator]].[[Quintus|Elder Cleric Quintus]]: ''"I found you in the ruins of Shady Sands. Kill me, and the world will continue just-- just as you see it."''
({{FOTV|2|4}}) {{Small|'''Note:''' This line indicates that Quintus was the one who found Maximus at Shady Sands. This retroactively establishes that the power armored knight seen in Maximus' flashbacks in season 1 is Quintus.}} Quintus brought the boy to join the ranks of the Knights of San Fernando, where he was given the name Maximus and became an [[Aspirant (TV series)|aspirant]]. Maximus came to idolize the knight that discovered him as a father figure, enshrining his idealism towards the Brotherhood as a force for good in the [[wasteland]]. By 2296, Quintus had advanced to the rank of elder cleric and ruled the Knights of San Fernando with a firm hand. He nominally accepted the dominance of the [[Brotherhood of Steel (Fallout 4)|Commonwealth Brotherhood of Steel]], but was secretly displeased with the state of the Brotherhood and sought to reunify the various disorganized Brotherhood chapters across the wasteland, with his own chapter at the top of the hierarchy, as a response. The opportunity to do so presented itself when the Commonwealth Brotherhood ordered Quintus' chapter to hunt down [[Siggi Wilzig]], a scientist who had deserted from the [[Enclave]] with the [[cold fusion diode]], a crucial technology that could promise infinite energy to whoever controlled it. Under Quintus' orders, the chapter sent out teams of knights and [[Squire (TV series)|squires]] to search the wastes for Wilzig. One of these squires was Maximus, who had recently come under suspicion of wounding his fellow aspirant [[Dane (TV series)|Dane]] to receive his position, but who convinced Quintus to let him try to prove himself. This paid off, as events led to Maximus ultimately returning to give Quintus the location of the cold fusion diode. Maximus had initially tried to deceive the Brotherhood and was nearly executed for it, but his conviction at having acted for the ideals of the Brotherhood led Quintus to consider him as an asset for his plans to come. With Maximus' information, the Brotherhood was able to seize the cold fusion diode from its recipients, the NCR remnants under [[Lee Moldaver]] at [[Griffith Observatory]]. ===Quintus the Unifier=== With the cold fusion diode in hand, Quintus began making overtures to break away from the Commonwealth Brotherhood's authority. On his orders, the Brotherhood claimed [[Area 51]] to act as their new headquarters and set up a cold fusion reactor there to start producing an infinite supply of [[Fusion core (TV series)|fusion cores]]. He further invited three other western Brotherhood chapters (the [[Coronado Brotherhood of Steel|Coronado]], [[Grand Canyon Brotherhood of Steel|Grand Canyon]], and [[Yosemite Brotherhood of Steel|Yosemite chapters]]) to Area 51 with the intent of forming an alliance against the Commonwealth, luring them in with the promise of endless fusion cores for their arsenals. Up to this point, Maximus had played a major role in Quintus' plans, having been promoted to the chapter's top knight due to his actions at Griffith Observatory. However, Quintus' plans unraveled from there. The Commonwealth Brotherhood, somehow aware that Quintus was plotting rebellion, sent a liaison, [[Xander Harkness|Paladin Xander Harkness]], to Area 51 to prevent civil war and receive the cold fusion diode for their own use. Harkness' arrival caused Quintus' allies to back out of the deal, leaving Quintus stuck, as he understood that Harkness had to be kept alive, as his death would signal the beginning of active war with the Commonwealth. However, Harkness ended up being killed by Maximus to save the lives of a group of [[ghoul]] children; though Quintus dispatched forces to bring them back, they were too late to prevent this. Maximus, also realizing the gravity of his actions and with his faith in the Brotherhood wavering, decided that the only way to prevent a costly civil war with the Commonwealth would be to kill Quintus. However, his own feelings towards Quintus as a father figure left him unable to pull the trigger. He ended up telling Quintus why he had killed Harkness, which caused Quintus to denounce him as a heretic, effectively severing their ties, with Maximus locking Quintus in his office and then fleeing with the cold fusion diode. The theft of the cold fusion diode caused the four western Brotherhood chapters to fracture into civil war at Area 51. Realizing that his plans for reunifying the Brotherhood were doomed, and vengeful at the rest of the Brotherhood, Quintus seemingly now intends to destroy the Brotherhood, with blueprints for [[Liberty Prime|Liberty Prime Alpha]] factoring into his new goal. ==In the TV series== ===Season 1=== ====[[The End (episode)|The End]]==== [[File:Quintus interrogating Maximus.png|thumb|250px|Interrogating Maximus]] Quintus first appears during [[Maximus]]' interrogation after he was brought in on suspicion of causing [[Dane (TV series)|Aspirant Dane]]'s maiming. The elder questions Maximus about his reason for joining the Brotherhood, which Maximus says is for revenge on those who have hurt him. When Quintus informs him that his fellow aspirants have accused him of causing Dane's injury due to jealousy over their recent promotion to the rank of [[Brotherhood of Steel ranks|squire]], Maximus denies doing it. When Quintus asks him why he would not do it since his ambitions to advance in the Brotherhood are known, [[Titus|a knight]] looms over Maximus to pressure him to speak truthfully. Maximus admits he wanted it to happen but maintains he wasn't the culprit. Quintus states his belief that violence against a fellow member of the Brotherhood is a sign of weakness and asks Maximus if he is weak. He is left amused when Maximus claims that he tries not to be. When Quintus gives Maximus a chance to speak in his defense, he is surprised to hear Maximus not only tell the truth but expresses his gratitude for everything the Brotherhood has given him and his desire to do anything to help them in their mission to improve the world. Before leaving, Quintus clears Maximus of the charges and declares Maximus the new squire of knight Titus's. Quintus then oversees his anointment as Titus uses the gauntlet of his [[T-60 power armor (TV series)|armor]], heated by flames, to brand Maximus.{{FOTV|1|1}} [[File:FOTV S01E01 Quintus 01.jpg|thumb|250px|Giving the mission briefing]] Quintus is later seen giving a speech in front of the assembled forces of the Knights of San Fernando. He informs them about the details of their mission, to find and capture an escaped [[Enclave]] scientist, [[Siggi Wilzig]], who is in possession of an extremely powerful [[Cold fusion|artifact]]. He instructs the knights to go forth with honor before sending them out on their missions, each covering a select section of [[the Wilds]] to find Wilzig. ====[[The Beginning]]==== Quintus appears again in [[Filly]] after its occupation by the Brotherhood of Steel. He observes Maximus' return as he hands over the [[Critic|supposed head]] of the target to him. However, Quintus has his men scan the head, and they discover it to be a fake, as it lacks the artifact within. Quintus immediately accuses Maximus of lying about the artifact just as he supposedly lied about his culpability in Dane's maiming. The Brotherhood knights restrain Maximus and point a gun to his head, with Quintus demanding a confession in the face of execution. Maximus implores Quintus to spare his life, promising to lead the Brotherhood to the artifact's location if they do so. Fearing for their fellow squire's life, Dane then interjects, confessing that their original injury was self-inflicted, and pleads for Quintus to listen to Maximus for the sake of the Brotherhood. Quintus commends such a rare display of loyalty and orders the knights to release Maximus.{{FOTV|1|8}} Quintus and Maximus later have a private talk away from the others, where Quintus asks Maximus about the circumstances of Titus' death. After finding out that Titus died running like a coward, Quintus disappointingly admits that the Brotherhood has "lost its way," before reminiscing about the time when they ruled the [[wasteland]] on the West Coast. He expresses his firm belief that power must be "taken and not given," which is a lesson that he believes Maximus has learned from his travels. He continues by saying that, by leading the Brotherhood to the relic, the two of them will be able to take power in a manner that will allow them to start "a new Brotherhood," with Quintus as its leader and people like Maximus, who seek the power to change the world for the better, as its sword. He then reminds Maximus about his lifelong search for a home and offers him a chance to build one together. Regardless of what was said, Quintus directly assigned Maximus to the Brotherhood vanguard, whereas Dane was assigned as a means of punishment for their self-sabotage. On Quintus' order, the Brotherhood deploys in force to the [[Griffith Observatory]], beginning [[Battle of Griffith Observatory|a battle]] against the military remnants of the [[New California Republic]] led by the pre-War scientist [[Lee Moldaver]], who was also attempting to reactivate the cold fusion artifact. After Moldaver's death and the defeat of the NCR forces, the Brotherhood gains control of the cold fusion artifact, and Maximus is officially promoted to knighthood. ===Season 2=== ====[[The Golden Rule]]==== Quintus stands on the flight deck of the ''[[Caswennan]]'' to greet Maximus after his return from acquiring the [[control panel]] needed to access the San Fernando chapter's "new home." He later observes as scribes work to activate the pre-War wind turbine array that blows away the sand layer preserving the pre-War military base of [[Area 51]] which they intend to claim, promising Maximus that their efforts will be rewarded by fixing their "fallen world." He then expresses his approval to Maximus, calling him his "son." He remains onboard while Maximus leads an exploration team to investigate the contents of the central warehouse. In a private conversation with Maximus later, Dane expresses their concerns that Quintus deliberately excluded the Commonwealth chapter from an upcoming meeting with other chapters on the West Coast as the first step towards starting a rebellion to seize power, which the dominant Commonwealth chapter won't accept without a fight. Later, Quintus sits at the head of the table where he has assembled the elders of the [[Grand Canyon Brotherhood of Steel|Grand Canyon]], [[Coronado Brotherhood of Steel|Coronado]], and [[Yosemite Brotherhood of Steel|Yosemite chapters]]. His overtures of unity are cut short by the [[Coronado elder]] loudly demanding to know why he left out the Commonwealth; Quintus counters that if they had come, they would have taken the cold fusion relic for themselves and left the other chapters with nothing. The Grand Canyon elder agrees about the unfairness of their situation while the Yosemite elder says what Quintus is planning amounts to civil war within the Brotherhood and leaves them fighting against the Commonwealth's martial superiority. In response, Quintus props up their chances of defeating the Commonwealth now that his chapter has acquired the cold fusion technology. As the elders begin to quarrel with each other and expose their cultural differences, Quintus bangs his cane on the table to regain control of the conversation. He states that, while he acknowledges that each part of the Brotherhood is set in its ways, they are united by one common desire: power. He shows how his chapter has harnessed the cold fusion relic to generate an allegedly limitless amount of fully charged [[Fusion core (TV series)|fusion core]]s, a rarity on the West Coast by the present, serving as the final impetus for the other elders to declare their support of Quintus in his rebellion. The four elders later observe from afar as the celebrations of the unified alliance take place with a violent spectacle of two knights in T-60 power armor having a boxing match. Quintus particularly watches silently as Maximus is confronted by an aggressive [[Coronado knight]], demonstrating his intent not to interfere as Maximus is challenged to a bareback fight. During the match, as Maximus is brutalized and soon threatened by the knight taking out his [[Combat knife (TV series)|combat knife]], he again looks to Quintus for help, but the elder cleric leaves him to resolve the fight himself. He silently admires Maximus for his subsequent victory over the knight. Quintus and the other elders are surprised at the arrival of the vertibird carrying [[Xander Harkness]], with the elder cleric coldly acknowledging the paladin's arrival and his barb directed at Quintus about not receiving an invitation to their discussion of a civil war. ====[[The Profligate]]==== {{Quotation|Behold, the dimness of the sword.|Elder Quintus after hearing Maximus' suggestion}} At [[Area 51]], in the aftermath of Harkness' arrival, Quintus fields a private meeting with the Yosemite chapter's [[McRae|Elder McRae]], with [[Maximus]] in attendance, where the Yosemite leader reveals that the alliance of the four West Coast chapters has been shaken due to renewed fears of reprisal by the [[Brotherhood of Steel (Fallout 4)|Commonwealth chapter]]. The elder cleric continues to prop up the possibility of organizing against the dominant chapter, but McRae refutes him and declares her chapter is abandoning the alliance, citing the [[Codex]] and the prohibition against violence between brothers. As McRae continues to rebuke him, Quintus resorts to invoking the name and story of [[Roger Maxson]], preaching that the Brotherhood founder started the organization out of an act of rebellion when he chose loyalty to "God" over loyalty to his [[United States government|government]] after discovering they were supporting [[Forced Evolutionary Virus|unethical biological research]] being conducted on human test subjects at a [[Mariposa Military Base|research center]], and executed the offending scientists and anyone who tried to stop him as a result; Quintus tries to equate Maxson's rebellion to his as a righteous one that will bring about a better world. However, the Yosemite elder maintains her stance, reiterating that she does not care for the "religious stuff." She chooses to stay out of the elder cleric's rebellion and leaves the meeting with a final warning to hand over the [[cold fusion]] relic to the Commonwealth. In the silence after, Maximus, taking inspiration from the story of Roger Maxson, makes the suggestion that he kill Xander. Quintus mocks his shortsightedness since Xander's death would in all likelihood ignite war with the Commonwealth, and since the alliance of the four chapters is finished, the war would end with "all our heads on spikes." Maximus argues that their cause is righteous, but Quintus angrily dismisses him as a "sword" and orders him to leave. Maximus subsequently is convinced by Paladin Harkness to join him on a trip into the wastes, and ends up killing him to protect [[Thaddeus]] and his [[ghoul]] child workers at a [[Sunset Sarsaparilla factory]]. ====[[The Demon in the Snow]]==== Maximus is told separately by both [[Gnatius|Knight Gnatius]], who picks him up from the Sunset Sarsaparilla factory, and by Dane when he returns to the ''Caswennan'', that Quintus is furious with him for his unauthorized "hunting trip" with Xander. Dane particularly becomes more concerned with Maximus' intentions after realizing Xander had died (due to [[Thaddeus]]' poor attempt to impersonate him) and Maximus revealing that he intends to prevent war with the Commonwealth by killing Quintus and taking the cold fusion relic. After Maximus enters the meeting room, Quintus dismisses his clerics to talk privately with Maximus. He figures out that the incident with Xander went wrong, correctly deducing that the paladin was killed, which Maximus confirms, and that the knight intends to kill him too as Maximus draws his [[Laser pistol (TV series)|laser pistol]] and aims it at the elder cleric. Quintus is unfazed, walking right up to Maximus, who hesitates to shoot him, while lambasting the knight for his weak will and seeming failure to think about what his actions would do to the Brotherhood and the future they are building, He questions Maximus about what turned him against the man who brought him into the Brotherhood from the ruins of Shady Sands. Quintus softens somewhat when Maximus confesses that he feels he has been forced into all of his choices without being able to decide for himself. Quintus even seems perturbed when Maximus explains that he killed Xander to stop him from killing kids. However, any sympathy he felt turns to shock when Maximus reveals that the children he protected were ghouls. This quickly turns to anger as he launches into a tirade about his subordinate protecting "abominations" in defiance of the Codex, spitefully telling Maximus he should have never helped him. The elder cleric draws a [[10mm pistol (TV series)|10mm pistol]] from a hidden drawer and tries to attack Maximus, loudly decrying him as a "heretic," but fails to hit him before the ex-knight escapes the room and chains the door shut, trapping Quintus inside. He continues to hurl accusations of heresy at Maximus through the door as Maximus escapes after getting the cold fusion relic from Dane, and the base falls into chaos as infighting breaks out between the West Coast chapters. ====[[The Strip]]==== {{Quotation|Out of the virtue in my heart... I tried to unify the Brotherhood. And look what it got me. No matter. No matter. Quintus the Unifier is dead. Quintus the Destroyer... is born.|Quintus unveiling the plans for Liberty Prime Alpha}} At a later point, with the chaos of the civil war triggered by Maximus' actions still ongoing, Quintus dispatched [[Dane (TV series)|Dane]] on a mission to obtain a set of pre-War blueprints for [[Liberty Prime|Liberty Prime Alpha]]. Once they return with the document, the elder cleric laments that he had sought to unify the Brotherhood out of the virtue in his heart, only to be "rewarded" with betrayal and conflict further fracturing the organization. He declares that "Quintus the Unifier" is dead, replaced by "Quintus the Destroyer" as he looks over the plans for the superweapon. ==Personality== In his position as Elder Cleric, Quintus has seen enough misery and hardship to develop a keen insight into the nature of man, and a cynical attitude to the reality of the wasteland. He is a strong believer in loyalty and strength of character,[[Maximus]]: ''"Please... Please, I know where the head is!"''
[[Dane (TV series)|Dane]]: ''"For the sake of the Brotherhood, please listen to him!"''
Quintus: ''"Such a display of loyalty. Don't see that much anymore. You think you're the first squire who coveted his Knight's armor? How did Titus die?"''
Maximus: ''"He died running."''
({{FOTV|1|8}}) seeing violence as a tool to impose order on the wastes, though he condemns any actions of violence against fellow members of the organization, even willing to execute those if they appear to be responsible.[[Maximus]]: ''"I didn't. I didn't do it. I did not. I... I wanted it to happen. Is that wrong?"''
Quintus: ''"Yes. Yes. Violence... is merely a tool. We use it to bring order to the Wasteland, but violence against a Brother of Steel is a sign of weakness. But are you? Weak?"''
({{FOTV|1|1}}) Above all, Quintus wants to see his chapter of the Brotherhood restored to a position of absolute authority over the wasteland on the West Coast, and over the Brotherhood as an entire continental power. With the [[cold fusion]] technology, he believes that the Brotherhood can be rebuilt with him at the head and those loyal to him, ready to take power where possible, as the sword.Quintus: ''"The Brotherhood has lost its way. We once ruled the Wasteland... And yet power is taken, not given. A lesson you seem to have learned. So, if what you say is true, and you can lead us to the relic, then together, you and I, we will take power. And with it... we will start a new Brotherhood. With me as its head, and the likes of you as its sword. Your entire life, you've been looking for a home. Build one with me."''
({{FOTV|1|8}}) In the wake of the Brotherhood's victory against the NCR remnants at [[Griffith Observatory]] and obtaining the cold fusion relic, Quintus reveals more of his true nature as a manipulative power-hungry tyrant, using his charisma and loaded reassurances of finding a home to keep Maximus content in helping him with his plans to secure dominance in the wider Brotherhood. He boasts to the other elders he assembles for his rebellion that the cold fusion serves as their key to victory over the supremacy of the Commonwealth chapter and bettering the wasteland, though [[McRae|Elder McRae]] correctly deduces that Quintus' ultimate goal is to install himself as the leader of the new Brotherhood he intends to create, effectively putting himself in the position of the Commonwealth he despises. Quintus demonstrates that he is not ashamed to exploit the Brotherhood's core beliefs for his own ends such as invoking the name and story of its founder [[Roger Maxson]] to justify his grab for power by painting it as a righteous cause akin to Maxson's rebellion against the pre-War U.S. that led to the Brotherhood's creation. Despite his willingness to break the Codex's rules against fighting between Brotherhood members in his plan to rebel against the Commonwealth, Quintus also shows that he still holds parts of it in high regard, especially the dictations involving the extermination of abominations, leading him to violently rebuke Maximus and excommunicate him as a "heretic" after the knight reveals that he killed the Commonwealth's emissary Xander Harkness for threatening the lives of innocent ghoul children. ==Notable quotes== {{Notable content | {{Inline quote|Our mission comes from the highest clerics in [[the Commonwealth]]. It is believed that a denizen of the Enclave has escaped. And that he has with him an object… of profound potential… to harm our nation or to save it. Each knight in this legion will search a section of [[the Wilds]] for this target. Brothers… we exist for moments such as these. Go forth with honor! And may the shape of the future be cut by your sword!|sound=Maximus cut by your sword.ogg|Speech when Maximus is sworn in as a squire in "[[The End (episode)|The End]]"}} | {{Inline quote|Violence… is merely a tool. We use it to bring order to the Wasteland, but violence against a Brother of Steel is a sign of weakness.|sound=Quintus sign of weakness.ogg|Quintus when questioning Maximus in "The End"}} | {{Inline quote|The Brotherhood has lost its way. We once ruled the Wasteland… And yet power is taken, not given. A lesson you seem to have learned. So, if what you say is true, and you can lead us to the relic, then together, you and I, we will take power. And with it… we will start a new Brotherhood. With me as its head, and the likes of you as its sword. Your entire life, you’ve been looking for a home. Build one with me.|sound=Quintus build one with me.ogg|Speech to Maximus after delivering the false head in "[[The Beginning]]"}} | {{Inline quote|The Brotherhood has become scattered, broken, into dozens of rival chapters. But now, we have the strength to unify them under one banner, here, with the mightiest arsenal in history at our disposal. Together… we will fulfill our promise… to make better this-this fallen world… My son.|sound=Quintus make better this fallen world.ogg|Quintus to Maximus after inserting the [[control panel]] and watching the windmills come up revealing [[Area 51]] in "[[The Golden Rule]]"}} | {{Inline quote|But the Brotherhood began as an act of rebellion. And when he saw what they were doing there… depraved experiments on human subjects, well, then, Roger Maxson had to ask himself, who did he serve? His God? Or his government? He chose his God. He shot the scientists. He shot the people who tried to stop him. His government had defied God, and for that, he defied his government. But he wasn’t punished. He was saved. So that he could found our noble order. If our rebellion is righteous… the way will be paved for us.|sound=Quintus paved for us.ogg|Quintus during a meeting with [[McRae]] in "[[The Profligate]]"}} }} ==Notes== In the [[The End script|script]] for "[[The End (episode)|The End]]," Quintus is referenced as being in his 60s.{{inline quote|As Shortsight leaves the room, Maximus sees a figure in RED ROBES by the window. Maximus has never spoken to a man this important in his entire life.|[[The End script|"The End" script]], p. 41}} ==Appearances== Elder Cleric Quintus appears {{in|FOTV}}, played by [[Michael Cristofer]]. {{FOTV appearances|1=101|2=102|5=105|8=108|10=202|11=203|12=204|16=208}} Quintus is also the knight seen in [[Maximus]]' flashbacks of Shady Sands in "[[The Target]]," "[[The Past]]," and "[[The Beginning]]." This scene seems to be Maximus' knighthood ceremony, though it appears to have been cut as it is not featured in any episode of Season 1. ==Gallery== Quintus.png FOTV S01E01 Quintus 02.jpg|Quintus watches Maximus' initiation as a squire ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox characters FOTV}} [[Category:Fallout TV series human characters]] [[ru:Старший клирик Квинтус]]

I got a two-ton irradiated bear on my back, and you're standing there... You stupid motherfucker, you know this is all your fault.|sound=Titus.ogg|Titus berating [[Maximus]]}} '''Knight Titus''' is a [[Brotherhood of Steel ranks#Knights|member]] of the [[Brotherhood of Steel]] {{In|FOTV}}. ==Background== {{Quotation|A gruff, no nonsense Knight of the Brotherhood of Steel, Knight Titus has an itchy trigger finger and sees trips to the Wasteland as an opportunity to dish out heaping servings of violence from his suit of T-60 power armor.|[https://www.amazon.com/Fallout-Season-1/dp/B0CN4HV16N ''Fallout'' Season 1 description]}} ===Coming to New California=== In [[Timeline#2296|2296]], Titus arrived at the [[Brotherhood base]] on a ''[[The Prydwen|Prydwen]]''-class airship used by the [[Knights of San Fernando]]. There, he was assigned [[Dane (TV series)|Dane]] as his [[Brotherhood of Steel ranks#Squire|squire]]. An incident caused Dane to be injured and unfit for the mission, so [[Maximus]] is made his new squire. Titus was present and participated in his promotion ceremony, including branding his "T" initial onto his body from his armor's heated gauntlet.{{FOTV|1|1}} After being deployed to track down [[Siggi Wilzig]], an [[Enclave]] defector, Titus forced the [[vertibird]] they were flying in to land in [[the Wilds]] because he was "bored and wanted to shoot something." Though they happened upon Wilzig's campsite, Titus ordered Maximus to walk ahead of him into a [[Yao guai (TV series)|yao guai]] den, only to end up getting attacked by the mutated bear himself from behind. A brief melee ensued between the beast and Titus, during which his assault rifle was destroyed. After being disarmed by the yao guai, Titus fled out of the yao guai cave in fear, only to trip and slam his head on a rock with the full momentum and weight of his power armor, temporarily knocking himself unconscious. He was then pinned down by the yao guai and mauled, during which he regained consciousness and screamed at Maximus to help him and shoot the bear.{{FOTV|1|2}} Once Maximus finally managed to kill the yao guai with a shot to the head, Titus ordered him to remove his helmet and demanded that he be given a [[stimpak]] to heal his wounds. The damage to Titus' head and neck area was seemingly caused by his fall, as the beast could scratch the suit but could not penetrate it. Titus begins to verbally abuse Maximus and blame him for his sustained damages. Titus reveals he is contemptuous of the Brotherhood of Steel's purpose and his superiors; he complains of being sent to face the dangers of the [[wasteland]] for a "toaster oven." Further verbal abuse and mockery of Maximus enraged the squire. Titus threatened to punish Maximus with a torturous death for failing his duties as a squire. Maximus judged Titus antithetical to the Brotherhood's purpose of bettering their fallen world and found him unworthy of his power armor. Seeing Titus as an embarrassment to his ideal of the Brotherhood that saved him as a child, Maximus decides to withhold the stimpak from Titus and watch him die. As a result of Maximus' inaction, Titus passed away from his wounds. From then on, Maximus took Titus' red-colored jumpsuit and T-60 armor, referring to himself as "Knight Titus" when meeting others in the wasteland like [[Lucy MacLean]] while living out his dream of being a knight. ==Personality== Though initially coming off as aloof and duty-minded, Titus quickly showed off a streak of brashness and an inflated sense of importance as he forced Maximus to clean off his armor's codpiece as the answer to Maximus' question about whether tempered lining helped with mobility. He also arrogantly believes that because he was a knight, he could treat the squires serving under him however he pleased due to their rank. It is also possible that Titus deliberately treated Maximus with hostility due to his presumed involvement in the injury of his previous squire, [[Dane (TV series)|Dane]]. Regardless, Titus seems disillusioned with the Brotherhood of Steel, lacking morale, respect, and discipline. During his mission with Maximus, he openly insults the Brotherhood's leadership, referring to the clerics' orders as "bullshit." Another example can be seen when Titus is tasked with searching the town of [[Filly]] for the Enclave deserter. Instead of proceeding to his objective, he ordered the vertibird to drop him and his squire off miles from his target because he "was bored and wanted to shoot something." He later puts his squire's life in deliberate danger by ordering him to enter a radioactive area without armor when he could have easily done it safely. When he was later facing down a yao guai, he displayed a lack of courage and confidence, despite being clad in Brotherhood-issue [[T-60 power armor]]. When Titus was disarmed of his assault rifle, he engaged briefly in a melee with the abomination. Still, after landing a few significant blows, he began to lose his composure when the creature did not falter. Following this, due to the shock of the situation, his squire failed to attack upon his order. Titus then further revealed his cowardice as he attempted to flee from the mutated bear, screaming one explicate after another until he tripped and slammed his head into a rock, knocking himself unconscious. He was then pinned down and mauled by the beast. Once Maximus finally saved him, he continued insulting, demeaning, and even threatening his squire with execution. These actions disgusted Maximus, as he believed Titus did not embody the Brotherhood's values, which made him unworthy of his rank in Maximus' view. This cost Titus his life when he continued threatening Maximus after Maximus refused to provide him with medical assistance; poor judgment, since he had thus removed any incentive for Maximus to treat his injuries. When [[Quintus|Elder Cleric Quintus]] learns from Maximus that Titus had died running, the elder seemed disappointed yet unsurprised, implying that he was possibly aware of Titus' cowardly and foolish behavior. ==Notable quotes== * {{Inline quote|Set us down. I'm bored and I want to shoot something.}} * {{Inline quote|You earn the suit through acts of bravery. This is an act of bravery.}} * {{Inline quote|This wasteland fucking sucks. The clerics, too. With their bullshit. Sending me on stupid missions for remnants that turn out to be... ...a fucking toaster oven. You know what you could do with a fucking toaster oven? Do you have any idea?}} * {{Inline quote|What the fuck are you doing, man? Can you get me a fucking stimpak instead of just standing there? I’m asking you for a stimpak and you’re looking at me… you’re looking at me like you don’t know what the fuck to do. I got a two-ton irradiated bear on my back, and you're standing there... You stupid motherfucker, you know this is all your fault.}} ==Appearances== Knight Titus appears {{in|FOTV}}. He also appears also in the ''[[Fallout 2d20: NPC Pack - Hollywood Heroes]]'' expansion pack for ''[[Fallout: The Roleplaying Game]]''. {{FOTV appearances|1=101|2=102}} ==Gallery== Fallout Season 1 Amazon Titus.png Maximus and Titus.webp|Titus with [[Maximus]] FOTV Season1 ep2 Titus 01.jpg FOTV Season1 ep2 Titus 02.jpg ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox characters FOTV}} [[Category:Fallout TV series human characters]] [[Category:Brotherhood of Steel characters]] [[category:Fallout: The Roleplaying Game characters]] [[ru:Рыцарь Титус]]

{{Infobox character |name =Cleric Felix |games =FOTV |image =FOTV Season1 ep1 Cleric Felix.jpg |race =[[Human]] |gender =Male |rank =[[Clerics|Cleric]] |family = |location = |affiliation =[[Brotherhood of Steel]]
[[Knights of San Fernando]] |TV actor =[[Jacinto Taras Riddick]] }} '''Cleric Felix''' is a character {{In|FOTV}}. He is a member of the [[Brotherhood of Steel]] chapter known as the [[Knights of San Fernando]] in 2296. ==Background== It's unknown how or why Felix joined the Brotherhood of Steel; however, he had proven himself worthy to be raised into the ranks by becoming a [[Clerics|Cleric]]. ==''Fallout'' TV series== ===[[The End (episode)|The End]]=== Felix first appears during a class where he educates [[Aspirant (TV series)|aspirants]], such as [[Maximus]], about their purpose as members of the Brotherhood of Steel. That, of course, is to find and preserve [[Great War|pre-war]] [[technology]]. He asks Maximus to identify one such relic and strikes him as punishment for wrongly identifying it as a rotor instead of a circuit. His class is then interrupted by the arrival of [[the Prydwen]], as aspirants run out to gaze upon the airship. He is later seen conducting Maximus' anointment ceremony. There, he informs Maximus about his most sacred duties as a newly promoted squire, which include protecting the Brotherhood, its mission, and his new lord, Knight [[Titus]]. ==Personality== Felix is shown to be a strict and didactic person toward the aspirants he teaches and isn't against acting physically against them either, as shown by his interaction with Maximus. ==Notable quotes== * {{Inline quote|It is the duty of the Brotherhood of Steel to secure the Wasteland. One day as squires, you will help knights find and identify prewar tech.}} * {{Inline quote|The ability to defend yourself is but one part of your training. We are the finders and the preservers. [[Overseer]] |TV actor =[[Joe Castle Baker]] }} '''George Yaffe''' is an employee of the [[Vault-Tec Corporation]] {{In|FOTV}}. ==Background== George Yaffe was a Vault-Tec employee who worked in and around [[Hollywood]]. He and [[Sarah Clements]] received [[Cooper Howard]], a famous actor, at [[California Crest Studios]] when he was convinced to film an advertisement for Vault-Tec on the urging of his wife [[Barb Howard|Barb]], one of the company's executives. Cooper told them that he had never filmed any ads before this one, which George and Sarah laughed off. Later, after Cooper put on a [[Vault jumpsuit]] for the ad, he asked them if it was protective against radiation. Barb gave George and Sarah a side-eye, and they hesitated before Sarah claimed that the jumpsuit did, in fact, do so. They proceeded to watch Cooper pose for the ad.''Fallout'' Season 1 Episode 3: "[[The Head]]" George was later accepted into [[Vault 31]] as part of [[Bud Askins]]' experimental pet project and [[Cryonics|cryonically]] frozen, surviving the [[Great War]]. He was later de-frozen and sent into [[Vault 33]] in one of the Triennial Trades. He became Vault 33's overseer from 2121 to 2125, succeeding [[Ava West]].''Fallout'' Season 1 Episode 5: "[[The Past]]," ~18:55 The overseer who came directly after him is unknown, and the next known overseer of Vault 33 was [[Patricia Peters]]. ==Appearances== George Yaffe appears only {{in|FOTV}}. {{FOTV appearances|3=103}} ==Gallery== FOTV s1 ep3 George and Sarah.png|George and Sarah greet Cooper Howard FOTV s1 ep3 George and Sarah 2.png|George and Sarah lie about the Vault jumpsuits ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox characters FOTV}} {{Navbox overseers}} [[Category:Fallout TV series human characters]] [[Category:Vault-Tec characters]] [[Category:Vault 33 characters]] [[Category:Overseers]]

That's thinking in three dimensions, and I'm talking about four. Because what is the ultimate weapon to destroy your competition? It's not outselling them. It's not outsmarting them. It's time. Time is the ultimate weapon.|Bud explains his ideology}} '''Bud Askins''' is a former senior junior vice president of the [[Vault-Tec Corporation]] and [[overseer]] of [[Vault 31]] {{In|FOTV}}. ==Background== The archetypal Vault-Tec executive, Askins is a corporate zealot, single-minded in his devotion to the corporation,[[Barb Howard]]: ''"Bud Askins... he licensed them from RobCo. We're integrating them with the Vault-Tec admission systems."''
[[Cooper Howard]]: ''"Bud Askins."''
Barb Howard: ''"Bud Askins. Trust me, I know. The company's filled with guys like him. But Vault-Tec exists with or without me. Doesn't do anyone any good to complain from the sidelines."''
Cooper Howard: ''"All I'm saying is we have this one life. Do you really want to spend your nine-to-fives working with these assholes?"''
Barb Howard: ''"I need this job, Coop. It guarantees us a spot in the vaults."''
Cooper Howard: ''"We got money. We can buy a spot in the vaults."''
Barb Howard: ''"One of the good vaults."''
Cooper Howard: ''"What's that supposed to mean?"''
("[[The Trap]]") and likes vanity [[license plate]]s (JST ASKIN). Before coming over to Vault-Tec to oversee operations in Southern California, he spent a decade working at [[West Tek]] as part of their product management team. He oversaw the initial rollout of the [[T-45 power armor]] in 2067, ignoring design flaws in favor of pushing out the product as fast as possible. While he joked that at least they looked great, he also completely ignored that these flaws had resulted in numerous American soldiers being killed. After leaving West Tek, he switched from Product Management to Human Resources research at Vault-Tec, pursuing what he called "workflow optimization of management timelines," based on the principle of destroying the competition by outlasting them.Bud Askins: ''"Mr. Howard, great work today."''
[[Cooper Howard]]: ''"Ah. Oh, thanks. Thanks, man."''
Bud Askins: ''"Bud Askins. I oversee our Southern California operations."''
Cooper Howard: ''"Ah."''
Bud Askins: ''"I, uh, came over to Vault-Tec in Q3 after a ten-year stint at West Tek."''
Cooper Howard: ''"West Tek."''
Bud Askins: ''"It's a defense contractor."''
Cooper Howard: ''"Oh, I'm, uh, very familiar with you guys. You designed the T-45 power armor."''
Bud Askins: ''"First of its kind. No, I-I oversaw the-the rollout. You know, the design flaws were ridiculous, but they sure looked great."''
Cooper Howard: ''"I wore the T-45 when we almost lost the great state of Alaska to the Reds. Those design flaws of yours cost a lot of good men and women their lives."''
Bud Askins: ''"Yeah. Product management was never my bag. I'm more focused on HR R&D now. Overseeing workflow optimization of management timelines. I'm all about scale. Most people think scale means increasing global market share. That's thinking in three dimensions, and I'm talking about four. Because what is the ultimate weapon to destroy your competition? It's not outselling them. It's not outsmarting them. It's time."''
Cooper Howard: ''"Hmm."''
Bud Askins: ''"Time is the ultimate weapon."''
Cooper Howard: ''"Uh-huh."''
Bud Askins: ''"Yeah. Sounds complicated, but the future of all humanity comes down to one word."''
Cooper Howard: ''"Yeah, what's that?"''
Bud Askins: ''"Management."''
Cooper Howard: ''"Well, I'm awful happy for you, Buck."''
Bud Askins: ''"Bud. Bud Askins."''
("[[The Trap]]") Bud's competence was unquestionable; his social skills very much were, as he routinely failed to identify social cues, such as boasting about the T-45 power armor to [[Cooper Howard]], a veteran who witnessed the [[power armor]] fail and kill his comrades in arms. Undeterred, he consistently tried to buddy up with Howard, despite the actor detesting him.{{fotv|1|6}} He also continued to work with Howard's wife, helping implement the [[Societal Preservation Program]], or rather, its subversion: the grand Vault experiments. While Barb told her husband that she was only reluctantly working with Askins, in reality, she was one of the main architects of the experiment, pitching the Vault experiments to other potential corporate partners alongside Askins. As another one of his contributions to the Vault program, he was responsible for licensing the [[Pip-Boy]]s from [[RobCo Industries]] for use in Vault admissions systems. ===Bud's Buds=== Askins himself had designed the [[Three Vaults]] of [[Santa Monica]], [[Vault 31|Vaults 31]], [[Vault 32|32]] and [[Vault 33|33]], intended to carry out the pinnacle of his human resources research: his executive assistant training program "[[Bud's Buds]]."{{fotv|1|8}} Reasoning that trying to save a failed nation was a doomed prospect, Askins outlined a plan to keep Vault-Tec alive using the network of Vaults for an eugenics program; this program involved mixing junior Vault-Tec employees who had been selected to join Bud's Buds, kept in [[Cryonics|cryonic suspension]] at [[Vault 31]],Norm MacLean: ''"Is this where my dad's from?"''
Bud Askins: ''"You'll never find out. Oh. He's gonna find out. These are Bud's Buds. My Buds. America outsourced the survival of this country to the private sector. But it would have been insane to keep a failed nation alive. So, we kept Vault-Tec alive instead. A well-trained staff of highly supervised junior executives from my own assistant training program. Because the future of humanity comes down to one word: Management."''
("[[The Beginning]]") with the dwellers of two other Vaults acting as breeding pools for his "Buds" to create a class of super managers to inherit the wasteland after the inevitable [[Great War]]. The resulting [[Reclamation Day (event)|Reclamation Day]], when Bud's assistants would be unfrozen to reclaim the wastes for Vault-Tec, would occur after the war and any further action had wiped the surface clean of all competitors.[[Norm MacLean]]: ''"So what's Vault 32 and 33? Just people to be controlled?"''
Bud Askins: ''"What? No! When you put it like that, it sounds downright morally questionable. They're our breeding pool, the ultimate expression of HR R&D. Genetically selected to breed with my Buds to create a class of super managers. People with positivity, people who make lemonade. People who will inherit the Earth after we've wiped the surface clean."''
Norm MacLean: ''"We wiped the surface clean?"''
("[[The Beginning]]") This was not the end-all of Bud's experiment. Bud sought to create a proprietary, "designed" future that would allow for civilization to experience unlimited growth.[[Bud's Buds!]] To that end, Bud's Vault 31 trainees were expected to set in motion Phase 2 of the program after their return to the surface, though it is currently unclear what this consists of, except that the other two Vaults would also be involved, as well as "Future Enterprise Ventures" -- actually referring to the [[Forced Evolutionary Virus]]. Bud himself discussed these plans before the Great War with the investors behind his Vault experiment (members of the [[Enclave]]).[[Ronnie McCurtry|Ronnie]]: ''"Hey, boss. Now that we've found food, it's time for phase two?"''
[[Norm MacLean]]: ''"What is your name?"''
Ronnie: ''"Oh, um, I'm Ronnie. McCurtry."''
Norm MacLean: ''"I decide the next steps up here, Ronnie."''
Ronnie: ''"I know, yeah, you're the-- you're the boss. I know you call the shots. Just thought I'd introduce myself, 'cause I was Bud's personal assistant."''
Norm MacLean: ''"Hm, so?"''
Ronnie: ''"So, uh, let's just say I was the guy who took the lunch orders when Bud was meeting with the Vault investors. 'Future Enterprise Ventures'? The whole plan for Vaults 32 and 33?"''
Norm MacLean: ''"What do you know about that?"''
Ronnie: ''"Like I said, I was just the guy who got the lunch orders, but I do know that Phase 2 was very important to the experiment."''
({{FOTV|2|4}}){{FOTV|2|5}}{{FOTV|2|7}}: The scene with Wilzig reveals the Enclave to be controlling Vault-Tec from the shadows; this is further confirmed by the following episode, "[[The Strip]]," where Robert House explains that the Enclave were Vault-Tec's "investors," and Phase 2 is explicitly revealed to be part of the Enclave's plans. When the plan was set in motion, Bud would become the overseer of Vault 31 (and secretly the mastermind behind the events in all three Vaults), implementing the project over the next hundreds of years by having his brain extracted and placed in a robotic shell. Rather than a full-sized [[Robobrain]], he elected for a small, rechargeable platform described as a [[Brain bot#Rollerbrain|Rollerbrain]] or "brain-in-a-Roomba," a sacrifice he made simply to reduce costs for the company. This worked for over two centuries, with Bud overseeing generations' worth of developments under his Vault-Tec trainees in the two connected Vaults from his own position in Vault 31. However, things went awry for Bud in 2296 when he was tricked into allowing [[Norm MacLean]], the son of [[Hank MacLean]], one of Bud's trainees, into entering Vault 31 and discovering its secrets. Though Bud tried to stop Norm from escaping and revealing the truth, Norm subsequently sabotaged Bud's robotic chassis, resulting in his death, and escaped with a group of Vault 31 dwellers. Bud's death left his two incumbent overseer subordinates, [[Betty Pearson]] and [[Steph Harper]], directionless, though Harper did not mind.[[Steph Harper]]: ''"Empty. You're positive?"''
[[Betty Pearson]]: ''"Evacuated cryo pods. No sign of Norman. My god, Steph. I found Bud Askins upside-down in a mop bucket."''
Steph Harper: ''"So, 31 has been abandoned. It's just you and me now, Bets."''
Betty Pearson: ''"I suppose it is. A brave new world. So, we need to cooperate. The water crisis in 33 is getting worse."''
Steph Harper: ''"If I give you access to our Vault's water supply, it would taint the work we're doing here."''
Betty Pearson: ''"Bud is dead. What work are you talking about?"''
Steph Harper: ''"The same work we've always been doing, Betty. Trying to survive."''
({{FOTV|2|4}}) Still, Bud's experiment may not have ended for good, as his former personal assistant [[Ronnie McCurtry]] was privy to the details of Phase 2 (even if just incidentally) and attempted to continue the program after the Vault 31 dwellers' journey to the surface under Norm MacLean. Ronnie's attempt failed, but Steph Harper managed to contact the Enclave "investors" to request the start of Phase 2. ==''Fallout'' TV series== ===Season 1=== ====[[The Trap]]==== [[File:The Trap Cooper at wrap party.png|thumb|right|250px|Bud and the Hawthornes attend the wrap party]] Bud is introduced in the sixth episode, during the filming of the promotional video for [[Vault 4]], awkwardly introducing himself to [[Cooper Howard]]. After failing to make a good first impression, he tries his elevator pitch ("The future of humanity is Management"), but is interrupted by Barb, who snatches Cooper away. Askins is later seen at the wrap party, trying to attract Cooper's attention, but fails to do so.{{Clear}} ====[[The Beginning]]==== [[File:Bud Askins robobrain.png|thumb|Bud Askins as a brain bot in 2296]] In flashback, Cooper Howard drives [[Barb Howard|Barb]] to the [[Vault-Tec headquarters (TV series)|Vault-Tec headquarters]] and soon after, Bud arrives and parks his car next to them. As Barb's Pip-Boy is acting up due to being bugged, Bud suggests that she have it checked out, which she refuses as she can fix it herself. He then talks to Cooper about his "Bud's Buds," program, before heading inside with Barb. Later, Bud and Barb chair a roundtable summit of several corporate leaders, including [[RobCo Industries]] CEO [[Robert House]], [[West Tek]] researcher [[Leon Von Felden]], business magnate and [[Sierra Madre|casino owner]] [[Frederick Sinclair]]. Bud appears for the first time in the post-War era, after [[Norm MacLean|Norm]] infiltrates Vault 31 after tricking him into letting him into the vault by posing as Betty using her overseer terminal. His robot chassis has gotten trapped by a fallen mop and Norm frees him. After an initial scan, Bud realizes that Norm wasn't Hank or Betty. Scanning the young man, he determined he had half of Hank's DNA and began to panic. Proclaiming the initiation of Protocol 53, Bud attempted to sedate him, who easily evades the chassis' built-in syringe by simply stepping back. Desperate to keep Norm from discovering his secret, Bud tried ordering him not to open the door ahead but the young man ignored him and discovered the cryonic chamber. Powerless to stop him, Bud reveals the grand plan to Norm, before sealing the cryonic chamber and forcing Norm to choose between slow death by starvation or climbing into one of the cryopods to enter suspension, like his father, to only be thawed at a time of Bud's discretion. ===Season 2=== ====[[The Innovator]]==== In [[Vault 31]], [[Norm MacLean|Norm]] is still locked in the cryo facility with Bud Askins. Bud begins to panic upon discovering that Norm had disabled inter-Vault communications and goes to check on him. Bud is unable to reach Norm as he has sequestered himself down the stairs into the cryopod area, now littered with emptied ration cases. Bud tries to persuade Norm with his "two rational choices": either entering Hank's cryo-chamber, telling him about [[Reclamation Day (event)|Reclamation Day]], which, according to Bud, will occur when everyone on the surface who could challenge Vault-Tec's monopoly on life is eradicated, or starve to death. Norm stubbornly refuses to be Bud's prisoner and insists that someone would come for him, but Bud asserts that Vault-Tec had prepared for every contingency, including when a vault dweller goes missing, promising that [[Betty Pearson]] will cover up his disappearance. To further demoralize Norm, Bud shuts off the lights, making it harder to find more food, certain that he'd be more "reasonable" when he grows hungrier. Bud later checks on Norm again as the young man was lying on the floor. As Bud tried once again to encourage him to take Hank's pod, Norm ignored him, and asked what his father was like and why he was frozen in the first place. Bud boasted that Hank was an ambitious man and that becoming one of Bud's Buds was a highly coveted position in the pre-war era. Then noticing Norm spotted a two-headed centipede, he cautioned that consuming the mutated insect would cause him a slow, painful death, and instead offered to inject him with an unnamed poison that will give Norm a quick and painless death, as an alternative to cryo, and that when he dies, his body will dissolve and be filtered from 31 through the ventilation system into the crops for the other Vaults. Norm refuses Bud's false dichotomy of "two rational choices" and asserts there are plenty of "irrational" ones. Norm approaches Bud and kicks off the syringe limb Bud had threatened him with. Norm tells Bud that he is releasing all his junior executives as he connected his [[Pip-Boy]] to the console. Bud tried to stop him but Norm simply held him back with his foot. As all the active cryopods started to thaw, Bud protested that his Bud's Buds were only meant to awaken once every 30 years and that Norm has no plan at all and had caused nothing but chaos. Norm agreed, saying that while plans are hard, chaos was easy. ====[[The Golden Rule]]==== Bud is shown to have had his roller brain body rendered inoperable by Norm, who stripped out his robotic body's wiring and left him upside down in a bucket, but his brain case and [[Bio med gel]] appear intact. The [[Vault 31 dweller]]s awakened by Norm soon ask for Bud's whereabouts; Norm informs them of his death and then tricks them into following his orders to escape the Vault, claiming that this was Bud's last test for his trainees. ====[[The Demon in the Snow]]==== Bud does not appear, but Betty Pearson mentions to Steph Harper that she discovered Bud when investigating Vault 31 and confirms that he is dead. ====[[The Other Player]]==== {{Section|FOTV}} ==Personality== Bud Askins is a visionary with a unique mindset, but also blindly loyal to Vault-Tec. He believes that the ultimate weapon of mass destruction in the world is time, and using that mindset, they can beat all competition that stands in the way of Vault-Tec. He strongly believes in management and its key role in the future of humanity. Bud is also known for his overwhelming personality, which Cooper, another character from the show, experiences when he meets Bud for the first time. Likewise, Bud was able to cultivate a loyal following amongst his trainees, who, when unfrozen by Norm, were quick to look for his leadership and immediately thrown into disarray when hearing of his passing. However, despite his complete confidence in his plans, he is quick to panic when things go horribly awry. He both vastly overestimates his own capabilities and authority and vastly underestimates Norm's ability to circumvent and overpower him, which ultimately leads to his death. Bud may have gone through some form of mental degradation spending two centuries as a Rollerbrain, while he is largely chipper he is found talking to himself while failing to navigate past a mop, talking about the issue in terms of 'conflict' resolution. He also claims that he wishes he had the capacity for sleep, and envies the ability to wait out time in a cryo-pod. ==Notes== As seen in the credits sequence for "[[The Other Player]]," Bud Askins has several toys inside his office, including a [[Grognak the Barbarian]] action figure, several comics, and a [[Giddyup Buttercup]]. There is also a Rollerbrain user manual on his desk. ==Appearances== Bud Askins appears {{in|FOTV}}, where he is portrayed by [[Michael Esper]] both in person in pre-War flashbacks and with his voice in post-War scenes as a Rollerbrain. {{FOTV appearances |6=106 |8=108 |9=201 |10=202 |14=206 }} Bud also appears in the ''[[Vault Seller's Survival Guide]]'', and his voice can be heard in "[[The Ghouls]]," in a fragment of the ''Vault Seller's Survival Guide'' episode "[[Bud's Buds!]]" playing in [[Vault 32]]. As of July 18, 2024 (version 1.18.0), a [[Fallout Shelter pets#Other drone|rollerbrain]] was added to ''[[Fallout Shelter]]'' as a [[Fallout Shelter pets|pet]], but it is not explicitly specified to be Bud. ==Gallery== FOTV The Winning Team! '''Jorge''' was an actor in the pre-[[Great War|War]] era {{In|FOTV}}.

==Background==
Jorge worked alongside [[The Ghoul|Cooper Howard]] as actors in the movie ''[[The Man from Deadhorse]]''. Jorge played a villain named Joey Toro, who ends up killed in the film's climax by Howard's character.

==''Fallout'' TV series==
===[[The Head]]===
Jorge is seen on the film set of ''The Man from Deadhorse'' at [[California Crest Studios]] in a pre-War flashback. They are filming the climax of the film, where Jorge's character is on the ground, begging for his life from Cooper Howard's character, who is supposed to then shoot him. When Cooper breaks character, expressing discomfort with the scene, Jorge also breaks character and is seen looking around before Cooper offers him a hand and lifts him up off the ground. Jorge then walks away.

===[[The Ghouls]]===
In 2296, the Ghoul (Cooper) watches ''The Man from Deadhorse'' on a television in a [[Super Duper Mart (TV series)|Super Duper Mart]] along [[Santa Monica Boulevard]]. Jorge appears as his character, Joey Toro, in the climax of the film, and is seen being shot by Cooper's character.

==Appearances==
Jorge appears only in the ''Fallout'' TV series.
