Even something bad.|Charlie's speech to the [[American Veteran Entertainment Alliance]]|"[[The Profligate]]"}} '''Charles "Charlie" Whiteknife''' is a [[Native Americans|Native American]] actor and close friend of [[The Ghoul|Cooper Howard]] in the pre-[[Great War|War]] era. ==Background== During the [[Sino-American War]], Charlie Whiteknife served in the [[United States Marine Corps|Marine Corps]] alongside [[The Ghoul|Cooper Howard]], eventually attaining the rank of corporal.[[Robert House]]: ''"Corporal Charlie Whiteknife."''
[[The Ghoul|Cooper Howard]]: ''"Yeah. Yeah, Charlie."''
Robert House: ''"Rumor has it, he's a bit of a pinko. Is that right?"''
({{FOTV|2|3}})Insignia on Whiteknife's uniform, seen [[:File:Fallout-S2-ghoul-pre-war-2048x1365.jpg|here]]. The two of them served together on the [[Alaska]]n front during the [[Battle of Anchorage]], and in one occasion, Charlie saved Cooper's life during an attack on their squad.Charles Whiteknife: ''"Now, remember, these are the 45s. They're hard as hell to walk in. And this Power Armor's so goddamned hot from the fires that it's melting the snow beneath my feet. And I'm dragging this guy, you know, just dragging him through the mud and the slush. And I don't know if this poor damn grunt is dead or alive. So, the first chance I get, I take cover, take a knee, open up that visor. And who do I see staring right back at me? It's Cooper Howard. That's right. You know what he said to me? Coop. You remember?"''
[[The Ghoul|Cooper Howard]]: ''"Uh, 'How do I look?' "''
Charles Whiteknife: ''"That's a lie, ladies and gentlemen. That is a lie. I mean, the movie star Cooper Howard, he probably would have said that. But the man I was looking at... he looked up at me and he said, 'How are the others?' Nearly burnt alive... and he was worried about our squad. Fuckin' Marines, huh?"''
({{FOTV|2|3}}) After his discharge, he started a career as a [[Hollywood]] movie actor but found he was often typecast as Native American characters in Westerns, many of which he co-starred in with Cooper.[[Fallout (TV series)|''Fallout'']] Season 1 Episode 6: "[[The Trap]]," ~20:40 By 2077, he lived in [[Tarzana]], [[Los Angeles]], where he owned five acres of land.[[Fallout (TV series)|''Fallout'']] Season 1 Episode 6: "[[The Trap]]," ~21:00 At some point, he became affiliated with [[Lee Moldaver|Kate Williams]] and her anti-capitalist, supposedly [[Communism|communist]] group. When this information got out to the public, Charles was blacklisted as a "Hollywood Red," but he no longer cared.[[Sebastian Leslie]]: ''"Fucking Hollywood Reds. I'm telling you, radicalism is sweeping through Hollywood like a bad case of the clap. Even got your friend, Charlie Whiteknife."''
[[The Ghoul|Cooper Howard]]: ''"Are you kidding me? Charlie?"''
Sebastian Leslie: ''"Mm."''
Cooper Howard: ''"I served with that guy."''
Sebastian Leslie: ''"They have meetings and everything. It's a shit show."''
({{FOTV|1|6}}) Through his interactions with Williams, he came to perceive the rise of corporate power and its many influences in society and the government with special attention to the [[Vault-Tec Corporation]]'s joint collaboration with the government to build the [[Vault]]s. ==''Fallout'' TV series== ===Season 1=== ====[[The Trap]]==== Charlie is first mentioned during a conversation between Cooper Howard and [[Sebastian Leslie]] at a wrap party at the [[Howard residence]], in which Sebastian mentions Charlie as being a "Hollywood Red." This surprises Cooper, given that they had served together in the Marines. Later, Charlie and Cooper meet up at a bar, where Cooper (half-jokingly) calls out Charlie for skipping the wrap party to attend one of his "Communist meetings," as Cooper describes it. Cooper expresses disapproval towards Charlie for being a part of something they fought against during the [[Sino-American War]]. Charles rebuts that the cause they fought for was meaningless, though Cooper still believes in it (the American Dream). Jokingly, Charlie says that said dream has him getting "shot in the ass by [Cooper] all day." In response, Cooper points out that Charlie is well off by the standards of the American Dream, but Charlie claims that this is meaningless in the face of Vault-Tec, which he calls the devil. Defensively, Cooper notes that his [[Barb Howard|wife]] works at Vault-Tec and asks if Charlie is by extension calling Barb the devil. Charlie clarifies that he considers Vault-Tec a problem because of its "fiduciary responsibility:" the [[United States government]] had outsourced its survival to Vault-Tec, a corporation which has a fiduciary responsibility to make money for its investors, by selling Vaults. Cooper sees no problem with this, calling it standard capitalism, but Charles argues that if the peace negotiations to end the Sino-American War continue, then Vault-Tec can't continue selling Vaults. Hence, it is Vault-Tec's fiduciary responsibility to ensure that peace never comes. Cooper asks how Vault-Tec would accomplish this. Charles doesn't know, but offers an analogy, asking Cooper if he remembers a movie they did with a man named [[Johnny Morton]] and reminisces about his role in the movie as a generic [[Native Americans|Native American]]. Cooper tries to upsell Charlie's performance, saying that Charlie played the character Tallhand Mudlake with "grace and dignity." Charlie continues: Morton's character was a rancher who owned half of [[Missouri]] and had more power than the town sheriff played by Cooper; Cooper understands what he means: that when the rancher has more power than the sheriff, the "whole town burns down." Charlie makes his point: Vault-Tec is effectively the rancher, and the U.S. government is the sheriff, and the United States will suffer unless the people do something about the situation. Cooper downplays Charlie's words as a conspiracy theory and compares him to cultist. However, Charlie argues that Cooper sounds more like a cultist given how fervently he is defending a system that could, in Charlie's view, destroy the world. Before leaving, Charlie leaves Cooper a card for the [[Hollywood Forever]] group and tells him to attend a meeting just to learn about the company where his wife works, for her sake. The following day, Charlie meets Cooper at Hollywood Forever, just outside of the meeting place, and thanks Cooper for attending. Though Cooper is still uncertain, Charles confidently claims that he'll stay and says there is someone he should meet. The person in question, [[Lee Moldaver|Kate Williams]], arrives just then to greet Cooper. ====[[The Radio]]==== Charles sits beside Cooper as Miss Williams talks to the [[Hollywood Forever meeting attendee]]s about the falsehoods of the American Dream. Once Miss Williams starts to talk about the soldiers who fought abroad, Cooper loses his cool and abruptly tries to leave, though Charles tries to stop him. Miss Williams stops him instead, leading to a debate between her and Cooper. As it starts to get heated, Charles apologizes, claiming it was a mistake bringing Cooper there, and tries to leave with him, but Miss Williams stops him. She states that she was glad that Charles brought Cooper, as she knows Cooper's wife. ===Season 2=== ====[[The Profligate]]==== In the Ghoul's flashbacks, Charlie and Cooper attend an event hosted by the [[American Veteran Entertainment Alliance]] where the former is being honored. During the event preparations, the two privately discuss the mission Cooper was given by Kate Williams about getting close to Robert House; Charlie claims he was not told the method, but they both acknowledge, to Cooper's reluctance, that she most likely expects Cooper to assassinate House. Charlie tries to assure his friend that their time in the military has adjusted them to taking a life, that Robert House is just "one man," but Cooper remains uneasy. Later on, Charlie takes the podium after being introduced by [[Diane Welch|Representative Diane Welch]] and entertains the audience by recalling a war story where he helped save Cooper's life. He laughs off a joke Cooper makes about it and tells the real story about how his comrade, despite being severely injured, asked after the fates of his fellow soldiers first. He then uses that story to give a speech about doing one's duty for the protection of the ones they love, serving as a subtle message to Cooper directly about fulfilling his role in the plan to take down Robert House. After he finishes his speech, he receives a commemorative lighter as an award from Representative Welch. As the audience leaves, Charlie exits the stage and sits by Cooper. He gives the lighter to Cooper as a gift, saying that he got the award for saving one man (Cooper), not for having killed three people in order to do so, indicating he should reconsider helping their group with the plan against House if it means protecting his family. ====[[The Demon in the Snow]]==== A flashback to Cooper's military service in Alaska shows that Charlie was deployed with him to a recovery mission on one of the Alaskan islands, outfitted with suits of [[T-45 power armor (TV series)|T-45 power armor]]. However, by the time they reached their objective, a combination of combat damage and malfunctioning hardware resulted in their armor starting to show its flaws, including Charlie's entire left arm locking up and preventing him from using his [[T60 pistol (TV series)|weapon]]. Cooper tried to radio their superiors to abort the mission, but unbeknownst to Charlie, he was denied. Cooper lied and told Charlie they were ordered to retreat, and telling Charlie to leave first. Though doubtful, Charlie obliged but warned Cooper to stay close, joking that he dreaded having to face Barb's wrath. Charlie still went on his own, and so he did not see Cooper subsequently being ambushed by PLA soldiers and saved by the intervention of a [[Deathclaw (TV series)|deathclaw]]. ==Personality== During his service in the Marines with Cooper during the Sino-American War, Charlie looked out for him as both a soldier and a friend; on one mission to an Alaskan island, he joked to Cooper that he had to keep them both safe, or else incur Barb's wrath. After starting his Hollywood career, Charles was elevated to a celebrity lifestyle, garnering enough wealth to buy land for himself, but was gradually worn down by his frequent typecasting in Hollywood productions. Once he met Kate Williams and bought into her anti-capitalist rhetoric, he no longer cared about how he would be perceived by the public, as his focus instead turned to the increasing influence of corporate interests in government. He saw Vault-Tec's joint work with the government to create the [[Vault]]s as an omen of the end of the world due to the concept of fiduciary responsibility requiring them to oppose any potential peace negotiations that would end the ongoing war, thus ensuring that people would continue investing in the Vaults. Despite knowing that his friend Cooper would be highly distrustful of the group's reputation as communists, Charlie still believed that he could be swayed to see the danger of Vault-Tec's influence like he had, seeing Williams' plan to take down [[Robert House]] as a necessary evil and trusting that Cooper would also come to share their view. ==Appearances== Charlie Whiteknife appears only {{in|FOTV}}. {{FOTV appearances |6=106 |7=107 |11=203 |12=204 }} ==Gallery== FOTV Charles Whiteknife.png|Whiteknife in "[[The Trap]]" Fallout-S2-ghoul-pre-war-2048x1365.jpg|Whiteknife (left) in a season 2 pre-release image FOTV S2E3 Charlie Whiteknife closeup.png|Whiteknife in "[[The Profligate]]" ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox characters FOTV}} [[Category:Fallout TV series human characters]] [[Category:United States Marines]] [[Category:Pre-War actors]] [[ru:Чарли Уайтнайф]]

Even Vera's voice will not unlock it. Know that on the night of the Gala Event I shall raise my glass and whisper, "Fortunato".|[[Sierra Madre vault terminal entries#Sinclair's Personal Accounts|"Sinclair's Personal Accounts" entry on Sierra Madre Vault terminal]]}} '''Frederick Sinclair''' was a pre-[[Great War|War]] businessman, serving as the founder and financier of the [[Sierra Madre]] and a close affiliate of the [[Big MT (company)|Big MT]] research company. He is mentioned in the ''[[Fallout: New Vegas]]'' [[Fallout: New Vegas add-ons|add-ons]] ''[[Dead Money]]'' and ''[[Old World Blues (add-on)|Old World Blues]]'', and makes an appearance {{In|FOTV}}. ==Background== ===Financial recovery=== Though a wealthy businessman with a boastful and egotistical disposition, Frederick Sinclair suffered many crippling financial losses around the 2070s, but nonetheless managed to hold on to the remainder of his fortune and even expand it. It was believed that his near-poverty affected Sinclair deeply to the point he remained obsessed with security for years to come.[[Fallout: New Vegas loading screens#Dead Money|''Dead Money'' loading screens]]: ''"Sinclair, the financier and architect of the Sierra Madre casino was obsessed with security, believed due to his own financial losses."'' One of Sinclair's biggest prospects was as a major client of the [[Big MT (company)|Big MT]] think tank, which developed much of the technology he utilized in his ventures.[[Y-0 research center terminal entries#Requisition Order: Dispensers|Y-0 research center terminal entries; Terminal; Requisition Order: Dispensers]][[Y-0 research center terminal entries#Dispenser Funding Update|Y-0 research center terminal entries; Terminal; Dispenser Funding Update]][[Z-38 lightwave dynamics research terminal entries#Requisition Order: Holograms|Z-38 lightwave dynamics research terminal entries; Terminal; Requisition Order: Holograms]][[Z-38 lightwave dynamics research terminal entries#Vera Keyes: Hologram Progress Report|Z-38 lightwave dynamics research terminal entries; Terminal; Vera Keyes: Hologram Progress Report]] ===Meeting with Vault-Tec=== At some point before the Great War, though previously known as simply an affiliate of the company,[[Z-43 innovative toxins plant terminal entries#Requisition Order: Chemical Suits|Z-43 innovative toxins plant terminal entries; Terminal, Requisition Order: Chemical Suits]] Sinclair was apparently chosen to represent Big MT at a corporate executive meeting held at a [[Vault-Tec headquarters (TV series)|Vault-Tec building]] in [[Boneyard|Los Angeles]] alongside other industry heads: [[Vault-Tec Corporation|Vault-Tec]]'s [[Barb Howard]] and [[Bud Askins]], [[REPCONN Aerospace]]'s [[Julia Masters]], [[West Tek]]'s [[Leon Von Felden]] and [[RobCo Industries]]'s [[Robert House]]. He was informed of Vault-Tec's protracted plans to extend their network of [[vault]]s across the nation and heard their offer of selecting some vaults to be used for [[Vault#True purpose|social experiments]] at the behest of the corporate heads, which he participated in.{{FOTV|1|8}} :''See: [[#TV series inconsistencies|TV series inconsistencies]] for more information about the [[Retroactive continuity (TV series)|contradictions]] between Sinclair's portrayal in the [[Fallout: New Vegas]] add-ons and the [[Fallout (TV series)|TV series]].'' ===The Sierra Madre=== Sinclair was once friends with lounge singer [[Dean Domino]], who introduced a fellow performer, [[Vera Keyes]] to him. From that moment, Sinclair fell in love with the starlet,[[Dean Domino's blackmail evidence]]The [[Courier]]: ''"Why did you need her?"''
[[Dean Domino]]: ''"Because she could get closer to Sinclair than I ever could. He built this place for her... well, after the two 'chanced' to meet."''
([[NVDLC01Dean.txt|Dean Domino's dialogue]])The [[Courier]]: ''"Can you tell me about her?"''
[[Dean Domino]]: ''"Vera was a big star, back before the Bomb. Not the best actress, but... well, she had other talents. Nice voice, nice legs. For some reason, Sinclair... he built this place... she caught his eye. {{Tooltip|Once he was hooked, that was it, had to have her.|{Shrugs} }} So made the introductions, and guess what? He builds this place for her, like some kind of Cleopatra obsession. {{Tooltip|Wasn't always a deathtrap.|{Beat, looks around} }}"''
([[NVDLC01Dean.txt|Dean Domino's dialogue]]) and thus started on his greatest project to create an impenetrable safe haven in which she would be protected from the impending nuclear apocalypse, the [[Sierra Madre Casino & Resort]].[[Extracted holotape]] Despite every measure taken to ensure its outcome, Sinclair did not anticipate that his plans were compromised from the very beginning.[[Sierra Madre vault terminal entries#To Vera.|Sierra Madre vault terminal entries; Vault control terminal, Vera, To Vera.]] In truth, Domino had introduced Sinclair to Vera, with whom Domino once had a torrid affair if the tabloid press was to be believed, as part of a plot to break into the casino [[Sierra Madre vault|vault]] and take the [[Gold bar (Dead Money)|treasures]] that lay within for themselves. Upon learning the truth, Sinclair's heart was shattered and filled with bitterness and a desire for revenge. He set about preparing a trap, and had the builders design the casino so that the vault, once accessed, would be impossible to escape.[[Sierra Madre vault terminal entries#Elevator Protocols: Warning.|Sierra Madre vault terminal entries; Vault security terminal, Elevator Protocols: Warning.]][[Sierra Madre vault terminal entries#Vault Security System Protocols: Warning.|Sierra Madre vault terminal entries; Vault maintenance access terminal, Vault Security System Protocols: Warning.]] However, after Vera confessed her betrayal to him, overcome by guilt, Sinclair, remorseful, decided enough was enough, and it was time that the casino returned to its original purpose. Although he would never again love her like he did, left hollow by her betrayal, Sinclair could not bear to condemn Vera to the death he planned for her after hearing her genuine guilt and remorse. Sometime shortly before the [[Great War]], he returned to the vault and removed the terminal entry he wrote for her, replacing it with an apology. Subsequently, Sinclair attempted to jury rig the shelter's electronics to remove the trap by directly accessing them from the pipes, but due to a leak in the system, he succumbed to the effects of [[Cloud|lethal toxins]] that had been amassing in the ventilation. For the next 200 years, his remains lay undisturbed in the bowels of the Sierra Madre resort, separated from his once-true love Vera forever, while the grand resort was turned into a nightmarish city of the dead that lured countless wasteland treasure hunters to their doom choking on the poisonous miasma that blanketed it. ==Notes== * When inside the vault during [[Heist of the Centuries]], Sinclair's skeletal remains can be found lying on a set of pipes next to a [[Duffle bag (Fallout: New Vegas)|duffle bag]] near the vault door (below where the [[extracted holotape]] is found) ** If one approaches the corpse, they are identified as "The Founder's Remains." ** While having the appearance of a skeleton, the Founder's Remains are actually a container, albeit with nothing inside it.Container functionality, or using a Moveable Static, is required for nameplate displaying. * Since most of the technology found at the Sierra Madre was developed there, Sinclair is mentioned in numerous terminals across [[Big MT]] during ''Old World Blues''.[[Y-0 research center terminal entries#Requisition Order: Dispensers|Y-0 research center terminal entries; Terminal; Requisition Order: Dispensers]][[Y-0 research center terminal entries#Dispenser Funding Update|Y-0 research center terminal entries; Terminal; Dispenser Funding Update]][[Z-38 lightwave dynamics research terminal entries#Requisition Order: Holograms|Z-38 lightwave dynamics research terminal entries; Terminal; Requisition Order: Holograms]][[Z-38 lightwave dynamics research terminal entries#Vera Keyes: Hologram Progress Report|Z-38 lightwave dynamics research terminal entries; Terminal; Vera Keyes: Hologram Progress Report]] * Sinclair possessed a nostalgic and sentimental appreciation for the Art Deco era, which factored into his designs and the aesthetic of the Sierra Madre.[[Fallout: New Vegas loading screens#Dead Money|''Dead Money'' loading screens]]: ''"Sinclair was drawn to the nostalgic Art Deco era, and it's reflected in the architecture of the casino."'' ==Appearances== Frederick Sinclair's skeletal remains appear {{In|FNVDM}} and he is mentioned in the add-on ''[[Old World Blues (add-on)|Old World Blues]]''. He appears in a pre-War scene in the [[Fallout (TV series)|''Fallout'' TV series]], where he is portrayed by [[Michael Mulheren]]. {{FOTV appearances|8=108|9=201|14=206}} ==Behind the scenes== * The quote attributed to Sinclair, ''"Know that on the night of the Gala Event I shall raise my glass and whisper, 'Fortunato.'"'' is a [[Fallout: New Vegas cultural references#The Cask of Amontillado|direct reference]] to "[[The Cask of Amontillado]]", a short story by [[Edgar Allan Poe]]. * [[Chris Avellone]] stated that the character's last name is a nod to [[wikipedia:Upton Sinclair|Upton Sinclair]].[https://archive.md/ke6f Chris Avellone]: ''"It was a nod to Upton Sinclair. In essence, the Villa and Sierra Madre was supposed to be a safe village in the event of war."'' ====TV series inconsistencies==== * In ''[[Dead Money]]'', Sinclair is stated to merely be a client of Big MT, whereas his appearance in the [[Fallout (TV series)|''Fallout'' TV series]] presents a characterization that differs from that of the game, as he is shown to be the company's representative at the executive meeting with Vault-Tec and willfully offers up unethical suggestions for the Vaults' experiments. His exact relationship with the company and his role within it that would lead to this is currently unclear. * Sinclair's physical appearance and characterization in the TV show is very different from how it is depicted in ''Dead Money''. In the TV show, Sinclair is portrayed as portly, past middle age, and is rather rude and condescending with a stereotypical greedy businessman personality. In ''Dead Money'', Sinclair is portrayed as a younger man of average weight with brown hair and a mustache (albeit only on pre-War murals), and has a much more youthful and regretful personality. Additionally, he seems to be far more morally upstanding than his TV show counterpart. * After reviewing the TV series, Chris Avellone, the project director on ''Dead Money'', publicly questioned the depiction of Sinclair, saying that the character's physical appearance on-screen "didn't really mesh with his appearance in the Sierra Madre," seemingly indicating that the murals found in the Sierra Madre during ''Dead Money'' were intended to be an accurate portrayal of Sinclair. Avellone also commented that Sinclair representing Big MT was "weird" and disputed his characterization as a willful participant in advocating for cruel experimentation in the Vaults."[https://web.archive.org/web/20240523155629/https://chrisavellone.medium.com/fallout-apocrypha-tv-series-review-part-2-1744b68fe4f2 Fallout Apocrypha: TV Series Review Part 2]" by [[Chris Avellone]] ==Gallery== Michael Mulheren as Sinclair.png|Frederick Sinclair as seen in the ''Fallout'' TV series ==References== {{References}} '''External''' {{References|group=Ext}} {{Navbox Dead Money}} {{Navbox characters FOTV}} [[Category:Fallout TV series human characters]] [[Category:Dead Money mentioned-only characters]] [[Category:Old World Blues mentioned-only characters]] [[de:Frederick Sinclair]] [[es:Frederick Sinclair]] [[ru:Фредерик Синклер]] [[uk:Фредерік Сінклер]]

Prior to the [[Great War]], House was the founder and CEO of [[RobCo Industries]], who used life-preservation [[technology]] to survive the bombs from within the [[Lucky 38]]. He later emerged from hibernation to become the self-styled president, CEO and sole proprietor of the [[New Vegas Strip]], uniting various [[Tribals|tribes]] and using his [[securitron]]s to form the post-War city-state of the [[Free Economic Zone of New Vegas]] by [[Timeline#2281|2281]]. House appears as a central character {{in|FNV}} who can facilitate one of the game's major [[Fallout: New Vegas endings|endings]]. His [[Robert House's double|body double]] appears in the [[Fallout (TV series)|''Fallout'']] TV series' [[Fallout TV series season 1|first season]], and he fully appears in its [[Fallout TV series season 2|second season]] in a more prominent role. The pre-War House also appears in ''[[Fallout Shelter]]''. ==Background== {{Quotation|Robert House is an enigmatic, all-powerful technocrat dedicated to the pursuit of his own interests, by any means necessary.|[[Fallout season 2 Amazon overview|''Fallout'' season 2 character description]]}} ===Pre-War=== Robert House was born on June 25, [[Timeline#2020|2020]],[[A tragedy has befallen all mankind]] and grew up around [[New Vegas|Las Vegas]], Nevada,The [[Courier]]: ''"What was Vegas like before the war?"''
Robert House: ''"It was a place of splendor. As magnificent as today's Strip may seem, it's but a shadow of the neon paradise that was Las Vegas. I grew up not far from here, and though I traveled the old world extensively, I never found another place like it."''
([[MrHouse.txt|Robert House's dialogue]]) but was orphaned at the age of two when his parents died in a freak accident involving an autogyro and a lightning strike. Cheated out of his inheritance by his half-brother, [[Anthony House|Anthony]],''[[Fallout: New Vegas Official Game Guide]] Collectors Edition'' p.305: ''"[2.06] H&H Tools Factory''
''Long before the war, H&H Tools Company provided Nevada and California high-quality robotics equipment. Owned by the half-brother of Robert Edwin House (the founder of RobCo, and—were it not for the 200 year gap—the same man who lives in the Lucky 38 Casino). When their father was killed in an accident, the elder brother swindled Robert out of the family fortune, and assumed control of the company.''
''Robert went on, through his dealings with RobCo and their lucrative contracts, to become one of the wealthiest men on earth. His half-brother meanwhile, became increasingly paranoid, seeking to guard himself against a vengeance that never came, and inflicting all manner of strange HR rules on his workforce. The remains of this factory still stand, surrounded by husk-like remains of North Vegas' industrial area."''
([[Fallout: New Vegas Official Game Guide Collector's Edition Tour of the Mojave Wasteland]]) he nevertheless managed to achieve attendance to the [[The Institute|Commonwealth Institute of Technology]] and later went on to found [[RobCo Industries]] in 2042, at the age of 22. Under Robert's leadership, it soon became one of the most profitable corporations in the world, which House credited mostly to his own technical genius and business acumen. Whatever the case, House's success led to him being regarded by his peers with envy, by the public as a "genius" and a "captain of industry," and by the tabloids as the nation's most infamously eccentric businessman.The [[Courier]]: ''"Can you tell me anything about Mr. House?"''
[[Raul Tejada]]: ''"Just how old do you think I am, boss? Because I can pretty much guarantee I'm older than that. Let me tell you a story from before the Great War: Everybody knew Robert House. Even from there, we could see House's defensive rockets shooting down the incoming missiles. Everybody assumed he died in the War. Maybe he did. ([[REPCONTourGuide.txt|Tour guide's dialogue]]) the [[Lucky 38|Lucky 38 Hotel & Casino]] on [[New Vegas Strip|Las Vegas Boulevard]], and the [[H&H Tools Company]], the family business that would have been his before being usurped by his half-brother (although the factory on the outskirts of Vegas was still under the elder House's control in [[Timeline#2077|2077]]).[[Lucky 38 VIP keycard]] Feeling a deep love for his home city and wishing to bring it into his vision as a city of "luxury without decadence, refinement without elitism, [and] class without snobbery,"''[[Fallout: New Vegas Official Game Guide Collector's Edition Tour of the Mojave Wasteland|Fallout: New Vegas Official Game Guide]]'' Collector's Edition p.341-343: ''"Lucky 38"

([[RaulTejada.txt|Raul Tejada's dialogue]]) Despite being a highly public figure, House chose to remain highly reclusive, employing a [[Robert House's double|body double]] to represent him in all public appearances,{{FOTV|2|5}} to the point that House himself was not widely recognized when he appeared in public.{{FOTV|2|1}} Another use of House's time while running his company was regularly designing and running mathematical paradigms based on global political and socioeconomic conditions in an effort to predict future events. By April 14, [[Timeline#2065|2065]], at 5:17 a.m., these projections led him to the inexorable conclusion that the world would be engulfed in a nuclear war within fifteen years. This was, to him, a mathematical certainty, and it led him to seek preparations.The [[Courier]]: ''"You say that you saved Las Vegas. How?"''
Robert House: ''"By 2065 I deemed it a mathematical certainty that an atomic war would devastate the Earth within 15 years. Every projection I ran confirmed it. I knew I couldn't "save the world," nor did I care to. But I could save Vegas, and in the process, perhaps, save mankind. I set to work immediately. I thought I had plenty of time to prepare. As it turned out, I was 20 hours short."''
([[MrHouse.txt|Robert House's dialogue]])[[Cooper Howard]]: ''"You said you knew everything."''
Robert House: ''"I routinely design and run mathematical paradigms based on global, political, and socioeconomic conditions in an effort to... predict future events. And one spring morning, the data coalesced, and it told me, in no uncertain terms, that the world would... well, end."''
Cooper Howard: ''"Calculator told you that?"''
Robert House: ''"The date of the end of the world may not interest you, Mr. Howard. But the date the data coalesced might. April 14th, 2065, at 5:17 a.m. Is that date of any interest to you?"''
Cooper Howard: ''"That's my daughter's birthday."''
Robert House: ''"Oh, that is vexingly curious, isn't it? More curious is that you were not meant to come to Vegas this weekend. Your wife Barbara was meant to come alone. The moment that you bought your ticket to Las Vegas, the date the world was going to end... jumped forward by one month."''
Cooper Howard: ''"What are you, a f-fortune teller now?"''
Robert House: ''"I am a mathematician, a roboticist, and a casino owner. And I don't know yet how you figure into all of this, but you most certainly do. And I don't like unknown variables. Irksome. Not knowing exactly how you play a part in ending the world."''
({{FOTV|2|5}}) ====Preparing for the war==== {{Quotation|Like yourself, [[The Ghoul|Mr. Howard]], I am an apex competitor. We are the very best at what we do. And what I do, is I know everything.|House to [[The Ghoul|Cooper Howard]] in "[[The Wrangler]]"}} Armed with his knowledge of the coming war, House devoted the next twelve years making preparations to ensure his home city would survive the apocalypse and that he would live to see the world after the war. While the primary goal of his countermeasures was to disable incoming nuclear warheads by remotely transmitting disarm codes, House included contingencies for directly destroying any that managed to get through using laser detonations and defensive missiles or rockets.The [[Courier]]: ''"What preparations did you make to save Las Vegas?"''
Robert House: ''"On the day of the Great War, 77 atomic warheads targeted Las Vegas, [[Hoover Dam]], and its surrounding areas. My networked mainframes were able to predict and force-transmit disarm code subsets to 59 warheads, neutralizing them before impact. Laser cannons mounted on the roof of the Lucky 38 destroyed another 9 warheads. The rest got through, though none hit the city itself. A sub-optimal performance, admittedly. If only the Platinum Chip had arrived a day sooner..."''
([[MrHouse.txt|Robert House's dialogue]]) House also acted to prevent other factions from taking over Vegas: though he allowed Vault-Tec to build a [[Las Vegas management Vault|specialized management Vault]] underneath the city, he also sabotaged it to ensure it would not be able to serve its intended purpose. House took equally drastic steps to preserve his own life: biologically, House planned to place his physical body within a [[Life support chamber|life-support device]], removing House's physical presence but wiring his brain directly into his vast information network via an enormous supercomputer to ensure he could continue to influence the world after the bombs.The [[Courier]]: ''"You appear to be a computer, not a man."''
Robert House: ''"Don't let the video screens and computer terminals fool you. I'm flesh and blood, not silicon."''
The Courier: ''"The lifespan you're claiming is impossible, except for ghouls and super mutants."''
Robert House: ''"[SUCCEEDED] I see you've made a study of the topic. My knowledge of the science of longevity would fill several text books... Perhaps, after a decade or two of economic reconstruction, I can commercialize these technologies and offer to others, such as yourself."''
The Courier: ''"How have you stayed alive all this time?"''
Robert House: ''"Let's just say it was very... {{Tooltip|costly|beat}}. But I was willing to make the sacrifices longevity entailed, financial and otherwise."''
([[MrHouse.txt|Robert House's dialogue]])[[Lucky 38 terminal entries#Terminal (control room)|Lucky 38 terminal entries; control room terminal, Disable Cerebral Interface]] As another plan, House also sought to develop a [[Artificial personality|digitized version of his consciousness]] through his brain scanning technology which would persist in his supercomputer network, though this would require an immensely powerful energy source. He also worked to acquire any and all technologies that he considered relevant to his plans, while also using his unique position to continue collecting any and all knowledge of the key situations in the world.Robert House: ''"Like yourself, Mr. Howard, I am an apex competitor. We are the very best at what we do. And what I do, is I know everything. I know who is making what technology, and I acquire that technology at the most lucrative moment in its span of functionality. This week, I'm acquiring Cold Fusion from Vault-Tec."''
[[Cooper Howard]]: ''"From my wife."''
Robert House: ''"Correct. It will allow me to stay alive indefinitely in roboticized, non-biological form and protect Las Vegas from the coming nuclear war."''
Cooper Howard: ''"Initiated by my wife."''
Robert House: ''"Hmm. Unclear."''
Cooper Howard: ''"By Vault-Tec, then?"''
Robert House: ''"No, I doubt that, despite what we've both heard in that meeting. Vault-Tec is a collision of bureaucrats. Your wife, though... I don't know."''
({{FOTV|2|5}}) Sometime during the [[Battle of Anchorage]], House gained access to the [[T-45 power armor]] worn by [[United States Marine Corps|U.S. Marine]] [[The Ghoul|Cooper Howard]] via a piece of software he had licensed to [[West Tek]]. Through this, House was able to observe the situation on the [[Alaska]]n frontline, including Cooper's encounter with a "[[Deathclaw (TV series)|demon in the snow]]." House recognized that this "demon" was a piece of biotechnology developed by some unknown party, and came to believe that this was heavily intertwined with the future of the United States, as well as to Vault-Tec through Cooper's wife [[Barb Howard]], a high-ranking Vault-Tec executive.Robert House: ''"Mr. Howard, I was there with you in Alaska."''
[[Cooper Howard]]: ''"I doubt that very much."''
Robert House: ''"Not physically, of course. I'm not insane. But I did license a piece of software to West Tek, which gave me access to the T-45 Armor you wore. So, I saw what you saw. I saw it all. I saw the demon in the snow. And I believe that it's connected to the future of this great nation. And to your wife."''
({{FOTV|2|5}}) Whether or not he had realized by then, House eventually came to recognize that Cooper Howard was heavily involved in the Great War according to his projections: in fact, the very date that his data coalesced around the prediction of nuclear war, April 14, 2065, was the date that Cooper and Barb's daughter [[Janey Howard|Janey]] was born. This was House's first indication that he was not the only one planning to survive and take power after the war, though he would not fully recognize this until much later on. Later in the 2070s, House and RobCo Industries developed a [[brain-computer interface chip]], which possessed mind control capabilities. House himself conducted a field test of the chip in [[Los Angeles]], [[California]] on a construction worker named [[Bill (TV series)|Bill]], successfully ordering the man to attack and kill his friends. Although the field test went awry when House cranked up the power of the chip using a remote control device, causing Bill's head to explode, House still saw it as remarkable progress. By 2077, House had instead set his sights on a different technology: Vault-Tec's proprietary [[cold fusion diode]], which he intended to use to power his digitized consciousness backup. House brokered a deal with Vault-Tec's leadership to trade his brain-computer control chip technology in exchange for the cold fusion diode, which he would then receive from Barb Howard during a defense contractors' summit in Las Vegas later in the year.[[Robert House's double]]: ''"RobCo presents the automated man. Spent a lot of time trying to make my machines more lifelike, but, hey, works the other way around, too."''
[[Barb Howard]]: ''"Mr. House, Vault-Tec and RobCo have always had a special arrangement. You have multiple Vaults to do with as you wish. If this is the research you'd like to pursue in the Vaults, you--"''
Robert House's double: ''"You must have missed the telegram. You're paying me for this. In exchange, I get Cold Fusion to power my little project in Vegas."''
({{FOTV|2|6}}) [[File:Robert House TV series.png|thumb|left|200px|Robert House's body double attending the meeting]] That same year, not long after informing Barb Howard of his deal for cold fusion, House was invited to a secret Vault-Tec meeting led by Barb Howard and [[Bud Askins]], also attended by American corporate representatives Frederick Sinclair, [[Julia Masters]], and [[Leon Von Felden]], where Barb Howard indicated Vault-Tec was willing to detonate the bombs themselves to ensure their profits. However, House did not trust these figures or their plans, merely sending his body double to the meeting, whom he used via earpiece to call out the plan's flaws. Viewing the plan as unsound from the very start, House came to believe that none of the figures present, nor Vault-Tec itself, would be the ones to launch the bombs. Instead, he suspected that the war would be caused by a hidden party -- the same one which created the "demon in the snow" he had seen in Alaska. He feared that this other entity was also making plans to outlast the war, and that they would ultimately claim victory over his plans given how successfully they had hidden their existence from him.[[Cooper Howard]]: ''"You know, the person who wanted me to kill you, you know what they think? They think that you are gonna end things by selling Vault-Tec the weapons it needs."''
Robert House: ''"No. The bombs will not be dropped by me or any of the idiots at that meeting. What I believe... I believe there is a... another player at the table. The same unknown entity responsible for your demon in the snow."''
Cooper Howard: ''"Who?"''
Robert House: ''"I don't know. It's like I said. Irksome. As you see, I live my life by one simple maxim."''
Cooper Howard: ''"The House always wins, right?"''
Robert House: ''"And it does. I'm making sure of it using every single piece of technology at my disposal. But what if I'm not the House? What if someone else is?"''
({{FOTV|2|5}}) =====The cold fusion deal===== Barb Howard's trip to Las Vegas, during which she would deliver the cold fusion diode to House, was set to take place not long after this meeting. However, [[Lee Moldaver|Kate Williams]], the inventor of this cold fusion technology, had been tracking Vault-Tec's plans due to her seeming suspicion that Vault-Tec intended to start nuclear war, and she somehow acquired the details of House's trade for cold fusion. She concluded that House was working with Vault-Tec and would give them the weapons that would enable them to kick-start nuclear war in exchange for the cold fusion diode, and subsequently convinced Cooper Howard to visit Las Vegas alongside his wife to assassinate Robert House and retrieve the cold fusion diode. This quickly caught House's attention, as his predictions indicated that Barb was supposed to come to the meeting alone; as soon as Cooper bought his ticket, his predicted date for the occurrence of nuclear war jumped forward by one month, indicating that Cooper was also an unknown variable of interest. To scope out Cooper, House visited an [[American Veteran Entertainment Alliance]] awards ceremony in Los Angeles ahead of Barb's trip, posing as a civilian to get a sense of Cooper's loyalties and beliefs.{{FOTV|2|3}} Subsequently, when Cooper arrived to the Lucky 38 during Barb's trip, House took the opportunity to call Cooper directly to his penthouse, where he revealed that he knew why Cooper had come; that they both knew about the "demon in the snow" and Vault-Tec's conspiracy; that he considered Cooper a significant person of interest for his influence over House's calculations of nuclear war; and that he believed some other party -- the same one which created the "demon in the snow" -- would ultimately be responsible for dropping the nukes. Cooper rejected House's claims, calling him a lunatic; House in turn derided Cooper as a "killer" and possibly the one who directly would end the world as Cooper left.[[Cooper Howard]]: ''"What if you're just a fucking lunatic?"''
Robert House: ''"I'm a lunatic?"''
Cooper Howard: ''"Yeah."''
Robert House: ''"I would encourage you to gaze inward, Mr. Howard, to your small life, spending your days pretending to be a cowboy, while your wife is making apocalyptic proposals at board meetings, and I'm building a missile system to defend this glorious city from what's coming. But from whom, Mr. Howard? From whom? Who ends the world? Is it you? WHat if it is you? I don't think you're a cowboy at all, no. I think you're a killer! I think I know exactly who you are!"''
({{FOTV|2|5}}) Cooper's interference resulted in House never receiving the cold fusion diode. Not believing House's claims, Cooper convinced Barb to help him stop Vault-Tec by stealing the cold fusion diode, which he then handed over to the [[Last President of the United States|U.S. president]], assuming that the government would use it to end the [[Resource Wars]]. This did not happen: what Cooper did not know was that the president was a member of the [[Enclave]] -- the same hidden player which even House was unaware of. House only became aware of Cooper's action after it happened; finding that the government was about to arrest Cooper to discredit him, House called the actor just beforehand to warn him and set the record straight that House was not responsible for Cooper's impending arrest.Robert House: ''"I want you to know that it wasn't me."''
[[The Ghoul|Cooper Howard]]: ''"What wasn't you?"''
House: ''"Whatever it is that's about to happen. I told you, there are far worse people than I, Mr. Howard. I commend you for trying to play the hero. I really do."''
({{FOTV|2|8}}) {{Small|This is House's phone call to Cooper at [[Camp McCarran|McCarran International Airport]].}} ===The Great War=== Though the loss of the cold fusion diode ruined House's ability to use his non-biological backup plan, he was still able to preserve himself biologically inside the Lucky 38. However, House still could not guarantee the successful execution of his plans without one key item: the [[platinum chip]], a computer chip containing a vital OS upgrade for his Securitrons and the Las Vegas anti-missile laser defense network. The chip was to be delivered to him in the afternoon of October 23, 2077. However, a miscalculation of mere hours by House prevented its arrival in time.The [[Courier]]: ''"Why didn't the Platinum Chip arrive on time?"''
Robert House: ''"The Platinum Chip was printed in Sunnyvale, California on October 22nd, 2077 - the day before the Great War. It was to have been delivered by courier the following afternoon... but by then, the world had ended. The Chip contained vital software upgrades, but not just for my Securitrons. Every aspect of the missile defense grid would have been upgraded, too. Given that I had to make do with buggy software, the outcome could have been worse. I nearly died as it was."''
([[MrHouse.txt|Robert House's dialogue]]) 20 hours before the chip's scheduled delivery, the [[Great War]] occurred, resulting in the chip being lost in the ruins for the next 200 years. Forced to work with an inferior OS, House endured numerous system crashes but was still able to protect Las Vegas from most, though not all, of the nuclear warheads aimed at the city. The strain on his systems nearly killed him, but House managed to survive.The [[Courier]]: ''"How did you nearly die, defending Vegas?"''
Robert House: ''"Software glitches set off a cascade of system crashes. I had to take the Lucky 38's reactor offline, lest it melt down. For nearly five years I battled power outages and more system crashes until I finally managed to reboot my data core with an older version of the OS. I spent the next few decades in a veritable coma. But I survived, obviously - and eventually thrived."''
([[MrHouse.txt|Robert House's dialogue]]) He spent the next five years struggling against power outages and frequent crashes until he rebooted his data core with a downgraded version of his software. This left House in a coma for the next several decades, allowing the remains of Vegas to be picked over by the people of the surrounding wasteland. ===Post-War=== ====Creating New Vegas==== {{quotation|Mr. House is the mysterious overlord of the Strip. He controls his small empire from the confines of the Lucky 38 casino, where no other living person has set foot for over two hundred years.|[[Loading screen]]}} [[file:The House Always Wins.jpg|right|thumb|House in his penthouse, a sight very few were privy to.]] House regained consciousness from his coma in [[Timeline#2138|2138]].''[[Fallout: New Vegas Official Game Guide]] Collector's Edition'' p.454: ''"2138: Mr. House regains consciousness."''
([[Fallout: New Vegas Official Game Guide/Behind the Bright Lights & Big City]]) Instead of immediately revealing himself, he opted to stay hidden and wait for signs of an organized civilization having returned. Eventually, he entered the world stage once again in 2274, when [[Securitron]]s under his command emerged from the [[Lucky 38]]. This action was prompted by the detection of [[New California Republic]] scouts arriving at [[Hoover Dam]]. In order to establish his rule, House enlisted the help of three of the [[Tribals|tribes]] who had descended from [[Vault]] dwellers and were now living in the Las Vegas ruins.[[Fallout: New Vegas Official Game Guide]] Collector's Edition p.42: ''"Freeside"''
''"Las Vegas wasn't heavily damaged during the Great War, but people didn't immediately "settle" into the remnants of the old city. The various Vault tribes that emerged years later, hunted and fought among the ruins, but it was not until the "return" of Mr. House that they ceased (most) of their hostilities. Mr House directed the tribes to use his sizable quantities of pre-war construction materials to build the crude (but effective) outer walls that separate The Strip and Freeside from the rest of New Vegas. While Mr. House valued the area around Fremont Street, he ultimately viewed it as secondary in importance to the Strip itself and he had a second, inner wall that separated the two areas. When NCR prospectors (and eventually the army) arrived in the region, people typically went straight for The Strip, leaving Freeside (as it had become known by locals) as an informal stopping point. Eventually Mr. House recognized that he could use Freeside as a filter for undesirables, and pulled his favored tribes and all Securitrons into the Strip, leaving Freeside to fend for itself."''
([[Fallout: New Vegas Official Game Guide faction profiles]]) These three tribes became the [[Three Families]]: the [[Chairmen]], the [[Omertas]], and the [[White Glove Society]]. Under House's guidance, they forced out all of their rivals and rebuilt the [[New Vegas Strip]], establishing the [[Free Economic Zone of New Vegas]] and accepting House's rule as its president, CEO and sole proprietor. Those forced out of the Strip were left to fend for themselves in surrounding areas such as what would later become [[Freeside]]; House purposefully left these areas alone, realizing that they were useful filters for people he did not want on the Strip.[[Courier]]: ''"How have the Khans been kicked around?"''
[[Yes Man]]: ''"They were one of the tribes the Three Families pushed out of Vegas! A whole bunch got killed! So they settled at Bitter Springs, but they kept being so obnoxious, the NCR had to kill a whole bunch more of them! So then they settle at Red Rock Canyon! There's just no getting rid of them!"''
([[VMQTopsYesMan.txt|Yes Man's dialogue]])The [[Courier]]: ''"How did the Three Families defeat you?"''
[[Papa Khan]]: ''"They allied with Mr. House, the self-proclaimed master of New Vegas. He supported them with the resources of New Vegas: weapons, technology, caps. They were better equipped, and we could not stand against them."''
([[VRRCPapaKhan.txt|Papa Khan's dialogue]])[[Courier]]: ''"What can you tell me about Freeside?"''
[[The King]]: ''"To understand Freeside, you have to look back a few years. Originally, we were all just tribes making a living in this area. That all changed when Mr. House came around. He made an offer to the three biggest tribes that were willing to listen to him. Today, everyone calls those tribes the Three Families, and they live in luxury and run their own casinos in the Strip. The rest of us were left to fight over the crumbs, living in the shadow of those more fortunate. Things got pretty nasty for a while. But we wanted more. A place of our own. A place where no one could tell us what to do. And we didn't want to go elsewhere to find it. So we took control of this place, and made it our own. And that's really all Freeside is, the best of a bad situation."''
([[VFSTheKing.txt|The King's dialogue]]) House's consolidation of power came just in time for the arrival of the [[New California Republic Army]]'s advance forces, with House sending his Securitrons and tribal "employees" to occupy Hoover Dam as a show of force. This forced the NCR to negotiate with House as an independent power; in the end, the NCR agreed to recognize House's sovereignty over New Vegas in exchange for permission to use Hoover Dam and the defunct [[Camp McCarran|McCarran International Airport]] as military bases and divert 95% of the power and water generated by the dam for their own use, ensuring cooperation with the NCR in the near term. By [[Timeline#2281|2281]], House's efforts led to the establishment of New Vegas as a major power in the Mojave Wasteland through lucrative trade with the New California Republic and exploitation of the NCR's citizens as customers, guided by his aims to use the NCR's conflict with [[Caesar's Legion]] to further expand his control of the region. House continued to reside in the Lucky 38 and control the Securitrons as his envoys. At some point after emerging from stasis, House gambled with the residents of [[Vault 21]] for ownership of their Vault, followed by stripping it of all useful technology, and had planned to permanently seal the Vault away by filling it with cement.[[Sarah Weintraub]]: ''"All right! Please, follow me. We'll head into the vault right away. This bunker protects the entrance to the vault - solid stone outside and thick steel on the inside! Above us there's the control center for this level of the vault's life-support systems, electric grid, radioactive shields and all that jazz. Don't get lost! My vault has many corridors and rooms - although it is no longer symmetrical, after Mr. House threw us out. This is the main game-hall. Here we settled the big disputes among the vault's levels. Chosen representatives gambled against each other here. The winner earned the right to settle the dispute as wished by the collective. We used to have such parties in this diner! A bitch to clean later... but well worth it! This hall leads to our guest rooms. You can use the first room on our left. But no snooping next door! That's my room, always was. Down there is the game room! Each side of the vault had one... but the other is filled with concrete now. Okay, that wraps it up. I'll see you soon!"''
([[SarahWeintraub.txt|Sarah Weintraub's dialogue]]) However, House was convinced by [[Sarah Weintraub]] to leave the top section of Vault 21 intact and convert it into a hotel to serve visitors to the Strip.The [[Courier]]: ''"What does Mr. House have to do with Vault 21?"''
[[Sarah Weintraub]]: ''"Mr. House has everything to do with Vault 21. He tried to get us out before he filled it with concrete. I almost went ape! So, we convinced him - okay, Sheldon and I, right? We convinced him to leave the top level mostly intact!"''
([[SarahWeintraub.txt|Sarah Weintraub's dialogue]]) ====Recovering the platinum chip==== Even after bringing some of Vegas' luster back to the wasteland, Mr. House's top priority remained acquiring the platinum chip. For decades before the NCR's arrival, House spent cumulative millions of caps on scavenger teams and prospectors to dig it out of the ruins of [[Sunnyvale]], California, where it had been made.The [[Courier]]: ''"What do you know about the courier Benny shot?"''
[[Yes Man]]: ''"{{Tooltip|I knew {{Tooltip|he|Male}}/{{Tooltip|she|Female}} was carrying the Platinum Chip! And I knew right where Benny should wait for {{Tooltip|him|Male}}/{{Tooltip|her|Female}}! That's why Benny put me here! To monitor Mr. House's data transmissions. They're all encrypted, of course|{sunny} }} - {{Tooltip|but I'm quite a decrypter!|{swelling with pride} }} Did you know that Mr. House spent 812,545 caps hiring salvage teams to find the Platinum Chip- just in the last year alone? {{Tooltip|Of course you didn't!|{delighted} }} Or that there were seven couriers, but six of them were carrying junk? How about their exact routes, and the mercenary teams that screened them? I knew all that. Pretty smart, huh?"''
([[VMQTopsYesMan.txt|Yes Man's dialogue]]) This massive expenditure ultimately paid off in [[Timeline#2281|2281]] when the platinum chip was found after 204 years. Mr. House contracted the chip's delivery to the [[Mojave Express]]; to cover up the importance of the package, he arranged for a layered plot involving multiple couriers, most carrying packages with miscellaneous junk items to throw off potential risks,[[Mojave Express delivery order (6 of 6)]] and [[Mojave Express delivery order (4 of 6)]] additionally paying mercenary teams to screen the routes to be taken. Yet again, however, the platinum chip's delivery was halted. [[Courier|Courier Six]], the courier with the actual platinum chip, was intercepted by the Chairmen's leader and House's right-hand man, [[Benny]], around [[Goodsprings]] after Benny learned of the chip's existence and its route from the modified Securitron [[Yes Man]], who had backdoor access to House's datastream. Benny intended to leverage the chip to gain control of the Strip and make it an independent power in the wasteland, free of his employer's machinations.The [[Courier]]: ''"If the Chip's so valuable, why use a single courier to transport it?"''
Robert House: ''"You realize you were just one of many couriers, the rest of them {{Tooltip|dummies|beat}}, so to speak? Add to that many thousands of caps worth of mercenary protection to screen your avenue of approach. Had I used an armed caravan to transport the Chip, I might as well have been announcing to the world "this is important. Attack this!" I didn't want to attract the attention of groups like the Great Khans or the Brotherhood of Steel. Alas, the real threat was closer to home."''
([[MrHouse.txt|Robert House's dialogue]]) Though not initially aware of Benny's involvement, House learned the truth after a Securitron, [[Victor (Securitron)|Victor]], he had planted in Goodsprings reported the chip's theft back to him.The [[Courier]]: ''"Why didn't you intervene sooner when Benny ambushed me?"''
Robert House: ''"Why didn't {{Tooltip|Victor|emphasis}} intervene sooner, you mean? Goodsprings is a bit too far away for me to reliably control a Securitron agent by remote. I can send and receive packets of data, at best. Victor's combat algorithms determined the proper course of action. Benny and his thugs were more than a match for a lone Securitron. When he alerted me, I instructed him to approach the site after Benny and the others had departed.''"
([[MrHouse.txt|Robert House's dialogue]]) Incensed at the betrayal, as he considered Benny a potential protégé, House nevertheless had to mask his knowledge of Benny's duplicity until the time came that he could act on it through a new agent.The [[Courier]]: ''"Tell me about Benny."''
Robert House: ''"Benny has led the Chairmen ever since I recruited his tribe seven years ago. Until his recent misbehavior, I'd planned to make him my protege. Maybe if I'd begun grooming him sooner, none of this would've happened..."''
The Courier: ''"What use would you have for a protege?"''
Robert House: ''"To achieve my aims, I require a capable human agent to perform certain... {{Tooltip|tasks|choosing word}}. I knew Benny was ambitious, even ruthless. But I believed he would do the job, so long as he was incentivized appropriately. Obviously, I miscalculated his drive for supremacy. But in any case, you've come along - a more-than-suitable replacement."''
([[MrHouse.txt|Robert House's dialogue]]) After learning through Victor that the Courier had survived and was making their way to the Strip, Mr. House began planning to invite them into the [[Lucky 38]] in hopes of using their desire for revenge on Benny to reclaim the platinum chip at long last.The [[Courier]]: ''"What terms are you offering?"''
Robert House: ''"My only concern is the recovery of the Platinum Chip. What happens to Benny, I leave to your discretion. When you bring the Chip to me, I will pay you four times the delivery bonus stipulated in your contract. How's that?"''
([[MrHouse.txt|Robert House's dialogue]]) In the event that the Courier proved reliable, House further sought to use them as his new agent to fully seize power over the Mojave amidst the upcoming [[Second Battle of Hoover Dam]]. ====2290s==== While the exact outcome of the Second Battle of Hoover Dam remains unclear, the New Vegas Strip also collapsed within this period, becoming overrun by [[Deathclaw (TV series)|deathclaws]]. The exact circumstances of House's fate after 2281 are unconfirmed, but according to him, his physical body had supposedly been targeted by "wandering travelers with something to prove" over the years, causing him to be poisoned, shot, bludgeoned with a crowbar, and possibly more.Robert House: ''"Well, hello, old chum! What did I tell you when we first met?"''
[[The Ghoul]]: ''"The House always wins. Winnin' might be overrated, Robert. 'Cause them swimming pools outside used to be full."''
House: ''"Well... I will say this much. It's good to be alive again. Over the years, my body became something of a target for wandering travelers with something to prove. I have been poisoned, shot, bludgeoned with a crowbar..."''
({{FOTV|2|8}}) Around July 2296, [[the Ghoul]] (Cooper Howard in his post-War persona) came to the Mojave Wasteland in pursuit of his wife's former assistant [[Hank MacLean]], whom he suspected was trying to get in touch with Robert House; the Ghoul suspected that his family may have survived in the management Vault underneath Las Vegas and believed that House was still alive and would be able to lead him to it. However, evidence suggested otherwise: at [[Camp Golf]], the Ghoul met Victor, who claimed that House was "gone," implying his eventual fate was tied to Cooper preventing him from receiving cold fusion before the war.[[The Ghoul]]: ''"Where's Robert House?"''
[[Victor (Securitron)|Victor]]: ''"He's gone. He had all the money in the world. But all he really wanted was to live forever. Life just ain't fair, I guess."''
The Ghoul: ''"Well, typically, I would agree. But you should know better than anyone that House had a knack for plannin' ahead."''
Victor: ''"Oh, he had plans, alright. But he needed the Cold Fusion doodad from before the war. Didn't you have somethin' to do with all that?"''
({{FOTV|2|3}}) Through a series of events, the Ghoul reacquired the cold fusion diode and was able to reach the Lucky 38 penthouse. There, he placed the diode in the hidden generator House had showed him centuries ago. Where previously his digital display in the penthouse was offline, the Ghoul's actions reactivated some version of House, though it is unconfirmed if this was the true living House or the [[artificial personality|roboticized, non-biological consciousness]] representation of him which he had told Cooper about in 2077.{{FOTV|2|7}}'''This cliffhanger scene finally reveals the answer to the season-long question of, who, what or where is Mr. House in the future. It also reveals the real reason why he sought the cold fusion diode from Barb and Vault-Tec (the same one Cooper ended up giving to POTUS).'''
[[Geneva Robertson-Dworet]]: ''"It did seem to us like a version of himself powered by cold fusion would be sort of the ultimate possible incarnation of Robert House. And as someone who is interested in robotics and artificial non-biological versions of selves, it made a lot of sense to us that this would've been something that he would've developed and sort of be the ultimate version of him. I've always seen it as something that allows for many players' experiences to have happened, but still Robert House had this other version of himself, that he was always ready to create and what he needed was the diode."''
'''But can we trust that this is, in fact, House's final final form?'''
Geneva Robertson-Dworet: ''"That's an interesting question. I'm not answering that, but I'm very intrigued by the question."''
([https://archive.ph/YZuZz Entertainment Weekly: "Viva New Vegas: Fallout stars go all in for an exclusive peek at season 2's 'explosive' finale"]) The Ghoul negotiated with House to gain access to the Las Vegas management Vault to find his family, in exchange for agreeing to don a [[Pip-Boy]] and work for House. House, guiding the Ghoul from his Pip-Boy, explained that he had failed to account for the Enclave's plans before the Great War, including the fact that the Las Vegas management Vault was actually intended for the Enclave and that they remained an active threat even in 2296. House seemingly intended to use the Ghoul against the Enclave, revealing that Hank MacLean, who was using the management Vault to develop the brain-computer interface chips, was an Enclave operative. The Ghoul subsequently helped neutralize Hank before House guided him to the room where his wife and daughter were supposed to be [[cryonics|cryonically]] preserved. When their cryopods were revealed to be empty, House belittled Cooper for having "bet on hope" and lost. However, Cooper actually found a clue for the first time ever since the war that his family could still be alive; as such, he rejected House and left, refusing House's claim that he still had to cooperate to deal with the rest of the Enclave.Robert House: ''"If your family is here, I'll be happy for you. But what is your plan? How will you protect them? With the Enclave still out there, there is no safety, as I tried to warn you all those years ago. [...] Shall I open it, Mr. Howard?"''
[[The Ghoul]]: ''"Open it."''
House: ''"What a shame. You bet on hope, Mr. Howard. And you lost. [...] You've been searching all this time. You're still living in a world of fiction. A world that isn't real."''
The Ghoul: ''"You're wrong about that. For the first time in 200 long-ass years... I know my family is alive."''
House: ''"What are you doing? The Enclave is still out there. We're not done, Mr. Howard. We have business."''
The Ghoul: ''"Not with me, you don't."''
({{FOTV|2|8}}) ===Personality=== {{Quotation|I have no interest in abusing others, just as I have no interest in legislating or otherwise dictating what people do in their private time. Nor have I any interest in being worshipped as some kind of machine god messiah. I am impervious to such corrupting ambitions. But autocracy? Firm control in the hands of a technological and economic visionary? Yes, that Vegas shall have.}} Mr. House is a very reclusive individual. Even in the pre-War era, he personally shunned overt public appearances, using a body double for all of his public affairs. Eventually, he became a total recluse, making him the subject of rumors; this may have been due to his integration into his life support technology shortly before the Great War. House remained just as reclusive after the Great War, never directly appearing in public even through a robotic medium and never allowing anyone into the Lucky 38. Mr. House seeks to restore [[New Vegas]] to its pre-War glory as a crown jewel of technological innovation and a bright neon paradise of business and fortune. Having experienced pre-War Vegas first-hand, he has long been enamored with the city's beauty and grandeur. His vision of autocracy and disillusionment with democratic society stems from his resentment towards the attitudes and actions of the increasingly desperate pre-War [[United States of America|United States]], whose decline was precipitated by the failure to adequately research and develop alternative [[Technology|technologies]]. His ultimate goal is to guide civilization's progress and forge a new future for mankind, free of the corrupting influences of the past. House's unwillingness to allow his life's work to be ruined by what he perceives as an increasingly unstable world has cemented, in his mind, the fate of democracy and human civilization itself. His contempt for most post-apocalyptic institutions, from bottle capsThe [[Courier]]: ''"I have a right to know more."''
Robert House: ''"That's simply not true. I am the only person to hold any rights pertaining to the Chip. I designed it, and I paid for it - dearly. To develop that Chip, I spent a sum of U.S. dollars - not the bottle caps that pass as currency these days - but a sum beyond counting. For decades, I paid salvagers to comb the ruins for it. And when it was finally discovered, tens of thousands of caps spent to have it brought here. We know how that turned out. Complete your contract and it will be the last time I pay for the Chip. Save your questions for then."''
([[MrHouse.txt|Robert House's dialogue]]) to the various factions, stems from what he perceives as humanity's inability to learn from its past mistakes. His own strategies and decisions are largely based on mathematical calculations, and he is confident in his own ability to succeed.[[The House Always Wins]] He styles himself as an "autocrat," viewing [[New Vegas]] as his rightful dominion, and is dismissive of other factions vying for control, comparing them to "two snarling dogs fighting over a curve of bone." He further disparages both groups as nothing more than "regurgitations of the past" drawing parallels between the two as attempts to revive past civilizations rather than offer a palpable future. He derides the NCR as a "society of customers" led by scheming leaders who wish to take Vegas out from under him, while showing disgust at the Legion's practice of slavery, technophobia and general brutality.The [[Courier]]: ''"In the meantime, you'd rule Vegas as some kind of dictator?"''
Robert House: ''"I prefer the term "autocrat." I would rule as a chief executive. I would not answer to a board of directors or any other entity. Nothing to impede progress. If you want to see the fate of democracies, look out the windows."''
([[MrHouse.txt|Robert House's dialogue]]) Nevertheless, he vastly prefers the NCR to the Legion, viewing the NCR as a possible long-term business partner while understanding that the Legion does not tolerate what they cannot control, and thus, while maintaining a facade of neutrality, actively plans for an NCR victory in the Mojave: just one on his terms with an Independent Vegas. Focused only on achieving his goals, he has little interest in monitoring or controlling the lives of others. He allows autonomy to the Three Families and is largely reliant on the information networks at his disposal and his Securitron patrols to maintain order. He takes pride in his achievements, seeing himself as a visionary. He also takes great interest in the Courier, seeing them as a valuable asset for overcoming obstacles too challenging for his other agents. Though their relationship is mainly professional, Mr. House comes to regard the Courier with respect and shows appreciation for their services, should they choose to help Mr. House. The Courier's success equates to his own success in judging them capable, inviting them to continue aiding him in his increasingly ambitious goals.The [[Courier]]: ''"Say you keep control of New Vegas. What happens next?"''
Robert House: ''"New Vegas is more than a city - it's the remedy to mankind's {{Tooltip|derailment|beat}}. The city's economy is a blast furnace in which can be forged the steel of a new rail line, running straight to a new horizon. What is the NCR? A society of people desperate to experience comfort, ease, luxury... A society of customers. With all that money pouring in? Give me 20 years, and I'll reignite the high technology development sectors. 50 years, and I'll have people in orbit. 100 years, and my colony ships will be heading for the stars, to search for planets unpolluted by the wrath and folly of a bygone generation."''
([[MrHouse.txt|Robert House's dialogue]]) ===Relations with other factions=== {{See|Free Economic Zone of New Vegas#Foreign relations|t1=Free Economic Zone of New Vegas}} ==Interactions with the player character== ===Interactions overview=== {{Interactions univ |essential = |temp companion = |perm companion = |perk = |wares = |caps = |max condition = |heal = |cure addiction = |cure radiation = |rent = |items modified = |quests started =* [[The House Always Wins]] * [[All or Nothing]] |quests involved =* [[For the Republic, Part 2]] * [[The Moon Comes Over the Tower]] * [[Wild Card: Change in Management]] * [[Render Unto Caesar]] }} ===Quests=== * [[The House Always Wins]]: Mr. House gives the player character the quest, which leads to one of the final quests, [[All or Nothing]]. In this case, the player character communicates with House only through the computer terminal in his office. * [[For the Republic, Part 2]], [[Wild Card: Change in Management]], [[Render Unto Caesar]]: However, if the player character decides to side with NCR, Caesar or fight for an independent New Vegas, Mr. House has to be killed or disabled. * [[The Moon Comes Over the Tower]]: [[Emily Ortal]] asks the player character to bug one of House's terminals for important medical information. ===Effects of player's actions=== * Upon his death, the quest [[The House Has Gone Bust!]] will simultaneously trigger and fail, and his obituary "[[A tragedy has befallen all mankind|A Tragedy Has Befallen All Mankind]]" will appear in the player character's inventory. * If the player character takes Mr. House out of his stasis chamber, he will ask them why they have ruined his plans and he will react differently depending on what they tell him. ** If told they did it in the name of the [[New California Republic|NCR]], he will belittle them for working for them, declaring them "snakes," and call the Courier a "sad, misguided whore." ** If told they are acting on behalf of [[Caesar]], he will be horrified at the prospect of slavery being humanity's future. ** If told they did it for [[Yes Man]], he will tell them their "vanity project" is doomed for failure. ** If saying it was "just business," he will retort by saying that they should have worked for him if what they wanted was personal gain. ** Finally, if the player character says they did it just because they didn't like him, he will call them a fool for letting their feelings about him jeopardize humanity's future. ===Other interactions=== * Mr. House plays a major role in the game. The Courier hears a lot about him while traveling, but upon reaching New Vegas, they are invited via Victor to visit House in Lucky 38. There, he provides vital information about [[Benny]] and the [[platinum chip]] and allows the Courier and their companions to use the [[Lucky 38 presidential suite]] as housing. * Mr. House has an interest in the collectible [[Snow globe (Fallout: New Vegas)|snow globes]] found in the game, and will pay handsomely for each.The [[Courier]]: ''"What's the deal with the snowglobe collection?"''
Robert House: ''"What of it? I enjoy them. There's something about a little diorama set inside a glass dome that I... {{Tooltip|find|beat}} pleasing. If you run across any out in the wastes, turn them in to Jane. She'll compensate you."''
([[MrHouse.txt|Robert House's dialogue]]) The snow globes can be given to [[Jane (Lucky 38)|Jane]] in exchange for 2000 [[Bottle cap (Fallout: New Vegas)|cap]]s each. Once the [[Courier]] has sold a snow globe to Jane it is placed on display (on a mantle) in the Lucky 38 presidential suite. However, if the player kills Mr. House, the snow globes will stay in their inventory and Jane will disappear. * Mr. House will have unique dialogue if one sides with him and then completes [[Beyond the Beef]] by either stopping Mortimer's plans (he approves of the player's actions)The [[Courier]]: ''"Did you know I killed some White Gloves who were eating their customers?"''

[[Robert House|Mr. House]]: ''{{Tooltip|"No, I was not aware of this.|Perturbed by the news}} Is it really so hard {{Tooltip|not|Emphasized}} to engage in cannibalism? My goodness... It's a violation of their contract. I authorize you to deal with them in any way you see fit."''
([[MrHouse.txt|Mr. House's dialogue]]) * The Courier can also attempt to pickpocket Mr. House, but he does not yield any items. * Mr. House counts as an abomination for the [[Abominable]] challenge. Because he is considered an abomination, shooting him with the [[Flare gun (Lonesome Road)|flare gun]] results in the "The abomination panics and flees!" message, but nothing else happens. * House is one of the characters that the player character must eat in order to earn the [[Meat of Champions]] perk. ===Endings=== {{Transcluded|Fallout: New Vegas endings}} {{transcludesection|article=Fallout: New Vegas endings|section=Mr House|options=nointro}} ==In the ''Fallout'' TV series== ===[[The Innovator]]=== {{section|FOTV}} ===[[The Profligate]]=== {{section|FOTV}} ===[[The Wrangler]]=== {{section|FOTV}} ===[[The Handoff]]=== {{section|FOTV}} ===[[The Strip]]=== House, newly restored, expresses pleasure at being alive again after his physical body expired and reveals to the Ghoul that over the years since he copied his mind to the computer, his body had become something of a target for wandering travelers with something to prove, resulting in House being poisoned, shot and bludgeoned with a crowbar, resulting in House's physical death. The Ghoul threatens to shoot the diode which House admits will have unknown effects but urges the Ghoul to exercise extreme caution as the damage would likely extend to other planets. The Ghoul questions why House hadn't told him about the management vault in Vegas which House reveals was because the Ghoul hadn't brought him the diode yet. The two men reach a deal where House will lead the Ghoul to his family in exchange for House being left the cold fusion diode and House smugly tells the Ghoul that like it or not, everyone eventually ends up working for him. Inhabiting a [[Pip-Boy]], House monologues about how Vault-Tec had wanted an impenetrable Vault buried half a mile below the city, but he had always been one step ahead, rigging every part of the city to protect its future and even rigging the Vault for management. However, House had miscalculated because the facility belongs not to Vault-Tec, but their investors. House was off by a bit when it came to predicting the end of the world, but he was wholly outclassed when it came to controlling the future by the invisible adversary who set the [[Deathclaw (TV series)|Deathclaws]] on [[New Vegas]] and to whom the Ghoul had delivered the cold fusion diode two hundred years ago: the [[Enclave]], whom [[Hank MacLean]] is currently working for. In doing so, the Ghoul had helped bring forth the greatest threat to the Wasteland. House eventually helps the Ghoul find his wife and daughter's cryo pods, but they're empty with only a postcard from [[Barb Howard]] left behind. Having found proof that his family is still alive, the Ghoul abandons the Pip-Boy and House on the floor while he goes to search for Barb and Janey. [[Maximus]] and [[Lucy MacLean]] enter the Lucky 38 penthouse soon after the Ghoul's departure; they do not see House's face on the monitor, which only displays a Signal Lost message.
